2. STANDING RULES

2.1 PROVISIONAL RESOLUTION — replaces blanket "ambiguity resolves to HALT"

Five halts have occurred in this project. Four were drafting gaps in the delta, not author decisions, and in all four the author then ruled the option a conservative default would have chosen. Each cost a full relay. This closes that class without inventing authority.

When a decision point arises that no tree in this delta covers, resolve it rather than halting — IF ALL FIVE HOLD:

  1. Reversible. No tag, push, stamp, or commit to main. A commit on phase1 counts as reversible.
  2. It does not change what a registered text SAYS.
  3. It does not require deciding what an amendment MEANS (G2).
  4. Every option on the table preserves all five quality rules.
  5. You can state the choice, the rejected alternatives, and the reason in three sentences.

Then take the option most conservative FOR A FUTURE READER — the one that preserves the most information, makes the fewest claims, and is easiest to reverse.

Record it in the report as PROVISIONAL, with its alternatives and reason, under a heading the author can scan.

If any of 1–5 fails: HALT, exactly as before.

Corollary. A PROVISIONAL decision the author does not overturn in the next round becomes settled. Say so when you record it, so they do not accumulate unresolved.

Not covered by this rule, ever: anything on the halt list in §6; anything §10 reserves to the author; a design decision with no conservative default (B6 was correctly halted on exactly this ground).

2.2 DON'T STOP AT THE END OF A DELTA

When the last item completes with nothing to rule on, continue to the next item in the standing sequence rather than stopping. The standing sequence after B10 is: §9.2 cross-tool comparison → DESIGN.md's Phase 1 section (§39/§72.2/§139) → the D10 fail-loud redesign → R110 register sweep → K2.

2.3 BACKGROUND THE LONG BLOCKS

Any single block over ~10 minutes runs in the background while other work proceeds. B8's ~40-minute sweep is the immediate case.

2.4 The rest, unchanged
  1. The report is a file. Bank each item before the next — and bank each failed attempt before writing the next script.
  2. Scripts that edit repository content are write-once-guarded; verify their effect by reading, never by re-running.
  3. §218. Every irreversible act in its OWN invocation, after the preceding exit status has been READ. Never check && commit.
  4. D2.1. No heredocs, no non-raw string literals for file content.
  5. Derivation, not assertion. Let a gate name the disagreeing sites.
  6. §36.2 at set scale. Full site list before editing any of it.
  7. Register form. Facts, not conversation.
  8. Frozen dated records are superseded, never rewritten.
  9. Stage explicitly. Never git add -A.
  10. Line endings checked per file before every write.
  11. Never end a turn on an announcement.

5. H-L26 — lands at A15, after the tag

  • A report that lives only in the chat dies with the turn — and banking on completion is not enough. An item that takes three attempts has no banking point until it succeeds. Bank the attempt.
  • An exemption whose anchor no longer resolves is an exemption granted to whatever now occupies that position, by nobody. The same exemptions keyed by value announced their own staleness the moment the reference set changed.
  • A check whose population is a pinned path reports on the path, not the work — and the one time it fired, it fired on the report about the work.
  • Do not transcribe the thing under test. Intercept its inputs instead. A transcribed builder is like the builder; an intercepted one is the builder, and the difference is a min_periods nobody notices.
  • An adapter that serves an aggregate makes the raw frame unread, and probing an unread frame records a silence the adapter caused and the report presents as a fact about the pipeline. Exclude it visibly, not implicitly.
  • Four of five halts were gaps in the instructions, not decisions needing an author. A tree that cannot anticipate a case should carry a default, not a stop.

1.1 THE DECLARATION'S DRAFT HEADER — RULED: FIX BEFORE THE TAG

AVAILABILITY_DECLARATION.md line 31, on main at d39643e, reads:

Status: DRAFT. Nothing in this file is a registered declaration.

Nothing lifts it. Line 3664's "not a draft" refers to the fixture manifest's filename, not this file's header.

This is not a §1.6 deviation. PREREG SC-7(a) hands a detector "the availability declaration's declared elements"; SC-8(f) calls the same file the one that "carries the scoring key." Registered text states the file declares and carries; the file states it declares nothing. That is two registered texts in conflict — on the halt list since R119, a §188 halt, and outside what §1.6 governs. §1.6 decides what happens to findings; it does not convert a halt condition into a non-halt.

And §1.6's stated mechanism cannot run pre-tag. DEVIATIONS.md is one of the twenty files the tag enumerates, so editing it before the tag invalidates the hash set A9 verified. A pre-tag finding has exactly two dispositions — held outside the hashed set and landed after the tag, or fixed. §1.6 as written offered a third that does not exist. Corrected at §2.6.

Consequence: the correction cannot be placed inside the signed object by any route except fixing it. D-STALE worked as a precedent because its disclosure was attested in the tag message; a post-tag DEVIATIONS entry is not attested by the v30a tag at all.

Defect class, second instance. tagmsg.txt was a v30 leftover that would have attested the wrong content. This is the same shape: a status marker true when written, never updated. SC-4(k2) enforces the fixture manifest's status at the tag; nothing enforced the status of the file that carries the key. Record that asymmetry — it is why this survived A9.

2. STANDING RULES

2.1 PROVISIONAL RESOLUTION

When a decision point arises that no tree in this delta covers, resolve it rather than halting — if all five hold: reversible (no tag, push, stamp, or commit to main; a phase1 commit counts as reversible); does not change what a registered text SAYS; does not require deciding what an amendment MEANS; every option preserves all five quality rules; and you can state the choice, the rejected alternatives and the reason in three sentences.

Take the option most conservative for a future reader. Record it as PROVISIONAL with alternatives and reason. Any of the five fails → HALT. A PROVISIONAL decision the author does not overturn next round becomes settled. Never reaches the §6 halt list, anything §10 reserves to the author, or a design decision with no conservative default.

2.2 DON'T STOP AT THE END OF A DELTA, AND DON'T IDLE ON A WATCH

A detached, checkpointing background job does not need supervision. Standing sequence after B10: finish §9.2's execution → DESIGN.md's Phase 1 section (post-tag) → the D10 fail-loud redesign (post-tag) → R110 register sweep → K2.

2.3 BACKGROUND ANY BLOCK OVER ~10 MINUTES.
2.4 THE INSTRUMENT'S POPULATION EXCLUDES THE INSTRUMENT — and its size is

asserted before its verdict is believed, because a scanner over nothing passes.

2.5 A STATUS MARKER IS A VERIFICATION VALUE, NOT PROSE

DRAFT, SUPERSEDED, PROVISIONAL, a version string, a "last updated" line — these are read as claims about the file's standing. Under §187 a stale verification value is FIXED, not disclosed. Two instances now: tagmsg.txt carrying v30's message, and the declaration's DRAFT header. Check them explicitly rather than reading past them.

2.6 §1.6 CORRECTED — the closeout rule, as it can actually be executed

From A9 green until the tag is pushed, a finding is disposed of one of two ways:

  • Held. Recorded in the round report, outside the twenty hashed files, and landed in DEVIATIONS.md after the tag is pushed. This is the default and covers the long tail §1.6 was written to stop.
  • Fixed. Only when the finding is itself a halt condition — an irreversible act done wrong, or two registered texts in conflict. Not "important", not "cheap": a halt condition.

There is no disposition that writes to DEVIATIONS.md before the tag.

5. H-L26 — lands at A15(5), after the tag

  • A report that lives only in the chat dies with the turn — and banking on completion is not enough. An item that takes three attempts has no banking point until it succeeds. Bank the attempt.
  • An exemption whose anchor no longer resolves is an exemption granted to whatever now occupies that position, by nobody. The same exemptions keyed by value announced their own staleness the moment the reference set changed.
  • A check whose population is a pinned path reports on the path, not the work — and the one time it fired, it fired on the report about the work.
  • Do not transcribe the thing under test. Intercept its inputs instead. A transcribed builder is like the builder; an intercepted one is the builder, and the difference is a min_periods nobody notices.
  • An adapter that serves an aggregate makes the raw frame unread, and probing an unread frame records a silence the adapter caused and the report presents as a fact about the pipeline. Exclude it visibly, not implicitly.
  • An instrument that scans files must exclude its own source. Every earlier instance of the too-narrow-domain defect hid findings; this one invented one.
  • A rule restated in every round and violated in three of them is not a discipline problem. Detect the damage instead of recalling the rule.
  • A status marker is a verification value, not prose. Twice in one ceremony a marker that was true when written and never updated would have gone into the signed object: a tag message naming the prior version, and a declaration saying it declared nothing. One check enforced the status of a file the declaration names, and none enforced the status of the declaration itself.
  • A closeout rule that says "record it and proceed" must name a place the record can go. Ours named a file inside the hash set the tag freezes, so its own disposition was unexecutable at exactly the moment it was meant to apply.

1.1 PREREG.md — A GATE, NOT A PROHIBITION. Correction.

Twelve deltas have said "No PREREG.md edit is authorised." That is accurate as a statement of each delta's scope and it is drifting toward an absolute this project already withdrew: "PREREG.md is never edited, not one byte" was an invention, it made a Class C amendment impossible, and it concealed a blocker for seven rounds.

The standing rule: PREREG.md is edited only by applying a diff the author has explicitly approved. A gate, not a prohibition.

So: no step in this delta may edit PREREG.md on its own authority. A step that needs one HALTs and presents the diff — with the finding, the proposed text, the class (A / B / C), and what changes if it is not applied. The author rules.

1.2 The declaration's DRAFT header — RULED, and A16 has applied it

2. STANDING RULES

2.1 PROVISIONAL RESOLUTION

Resolve rather than halt if all five hold: reversible (no tag, push, stamp, or commit to main; a phase1 commit counts); does not change what a registered text SAYS; does not require deciding what an amendment MEANS; every option preserves all five quality rules; and you can state the choice, the rejected alternatives and the reason in three sentences. Take the option most conservative for a future reader; record as PROVISIONAL. Any of the five fails → HALT. Unoverturned next round → settled. Never reaches the §6 halt list, anything §10 reserves to the author, or a design decision with no conservative default.

2.2 BANK THE FINDING WHEN IT IS FOUND, NOT WHEN IT IS CHARACTERIZED

The last turn ended on "I'll report those" and the findings reached nobody. A sweep is an item; its result is banked before the next item starts, even as "two status markers in PREREG.md, uncharacterized." An uncharacterized finding is still a finding, and the record of what was seen is what survives a stop.

2.3 DON'T STOP AT THE END OF A DELTA, AND DON'T IDLE ON A WATCH

A detached, checkpointing background job does not need supervision. Standing sequence after B10: finish §9.2's execution → DESIGN.md's Phase 1 section (post-tag) → the D10 fail-loud redesign (post-tag) → R110 register sweep → K2.

asserted before its verdict is believed, because a scanner over nothing passes.

2.6 A STATUS MARKER IS A VERIFICATION VALUE, NOT PROSE

DRAFT, SUPERSEDED, PROVISIONAL, a version string, a "last updated" line — read as claims about a file's standing. Under §187 a stale verification value is FIXED, not disclosed.

But rule 8 still governs: a dated record that was correct as of its date is not a stale marker. A16 drew that line correctly on ties and on the Part I markers. The test is whether the marker claims something about the file's standing now, or records something that was true then.

  • FIXED. Only when the finding is itself a halt condition — an irreversible act done wrong, or two registered texts in conflict. Not "important", not "cheap": a halt condition.

There is no disposition that writes to DEVIATIONS.md before the tag — DEVIATIONS.md is one of the twenty.

5. H-L26 — lands at A15(5)

  • Bank the attempt, not only the success — and bank the finding when it is found, not when it is characterized. An item that takes three attempts, or a sweep whose results are held back for a tidier write-up, leaves nothing behind when the turn ends.
  • An exemption whose anchor no longer resolves is an exemption granted to whatever now occupies that position, by nobody.
  • A check whose population is a pinned path reports on the path, not the work — and the one time it fired, it fired on the report about the work.
  • Do not transcribe the thing under test. Intercept its inputs instead.
  • An adapter that serves an aggregate makes the raw frame unread; probing an unread frame records a silence the adapter caused and the report presents as a fact about the pipeline.
  • An instrument that scans files must exclude its own source.
  • A rule restated in every round and violated in three of them is not a discipline problem. Detect the damage instead of recalling the rule.
  • A status marker is a verification value, not prose — and the mirror error is real: a dated record correct as of its date is not a stale marker, and a sweep hunting stale markers is exactly where a frozen record gets trampled.
  • A closeout rule that says "record it and proceed" must name a place the record can go. Ours named a file inside the hash set the tag freezes.
  • A scope statement repeated every round drifts into an absolute. "No edit is authorised by this delta" became indistinguishable from "never edited" — the same invention this project withdrew once already, at the cost of seven rounds and a concealed blocker.

2. STANDING RULES

2.1 PROVISIONAL RESOLUTION

Resolve rather than halt if all five hold: reversible (no tag, push, stamp, or commit to main; a phase1 commit counts); does not change what a registered text SAYS; does not require deciding what an amendment MEANS; every option preserves all five quality rules; and you can state the choice, the rejected alternatives and the reason in three sentences. Take the option most conservative for a future reader; record as PROVISIONAL; unoverturned next round it settles. Any of the five fails → HALT.

2.2 BANK THE FINDING WHEN IT IS FOUND, NOT WHEN IT IS CHARACTERIZED

A sweep is an item; its result is banked before the next item starts, even as "two markers in PREREG.md, uncharacterized." The record of what was seen is what survives a stop.

2.3 DON'T STOP AT THE END OF A DELTA, AND DON'T IDLE ON A WATCH

Standing sequence after B10: finish §9.2's execution → DESIGN.md's Phase 1 section (post-tag) → the D10 fail-loud redesign (post-tag) → R110 register sweep → K2.

2.4 BACKGROUND ANY BLOCK OVER ~10 MINUTES.
2.5 THE INSTRUMENT'S POPULATION EXCLUDES THE INSTRUMENT — and its size is

asserted before its verdict is believed.

2.6 A STATUS MARKER IS A VERIFICATION VALUE, NOT PROSE — fixed, not

disclosed. But rule 8 still governs: a dated record correct as of its date is not a stale marker. The test is whether it claims something about standing now or records something true then. A16 and A18 F1 both drew that line correctly.

2.7 THE CLOSEOUT RULE, AS IT CAN ACTUALLY BE EXECUTED

From A9 green until the tag is pushed: HELD (recorded in the round report, outside the twenty hashed files, landed in DEVIATIONS.md after the push — the default) or FIXED (only when the finding is itself a halt condition, or when the author rules it fixed, as at §1.1). There is no disposition that writes to DEVIATIONS.md before the tag.

2. STANDING RULES

2.1 PROVISIONAL RESOLUTION

Resolve rather than halt if all five hold: reversible (no tag, push, stamp, or commit to main; a phase1 commit counts); does not change what a registered text SAYS; does not require deciding what an amendment MEANS; every option preserves all five quality rules; and you can state the choice, the rejected alternatives and the reason in three sentences. Take the option most conservative for a future reader; record as PROVISIONAL; unoverturned next round it settles.

2.2 A GUARD MUST PROBE SOMETHING DISTINCTIVE, OR IT GUARDS NOTHING

A19's write-once guard probed the block's second line, which is empty — so it matched any empty line in PREREG.md and would have reported "already applied," skipping the application silently while claiming it had run. A guard that passes for the wrong reason is worse than a guard that fails, because its pass is read as evidence. Probe a line that appears nowhere else, and say in the guard which line it probes and why that line is unique.

2.3 MARKDOWN STRUCTURE IS SEMANTICS, NOT FORMATTING

A --- flush against a paragraph is a setext heading underline: inserting a block that opens with a rule directly after an anchor silently re-typed a registered **Registration:** line into an H2. Whitespace placement can change what a registered line is. After any structural insertion into a registered markdown file, confirm the lines above and below still parse as what they were.

2.4 THE PARALLELISM WINDOW IS ANY WAIT ON THE AUTHOR

Not only A10, A12 and A14 — a halt is a wait too. On halting Track A, state the halt, bank it, and immediately begin the next Track B item. Do not ask whether to; do not idle. Standing sequence after B10: finish §9.2's execution → DESIGN.md's Phase 1 section (post-tag) → the D10 fail-loud redesign (post-tag) → R110 register sweep → K2.

2.5 BANK THE FINDING WHEN IT IS FOUND, NOT WHEN IT IS CHARACTERIZED.
2.6 BACKGROUND ANY BLOCK OVER ~10 MINUTES.
2.7 THE INSTRUMENT'S POPULATION EXCLUDES THE INSTRUMENT — and its size is

asserted before its verdict is believed.

2.8 A STATUS MARKER IS A VERIFICATION VALUE, NOT PROSE — fixed, not

disclosed. But rule 8 governs: a dated record correct as of its date is not a stale marker. A16 and A18 F1 both drew that line correctly.

2.9 THE CLOSEOUT RULE, AS IT CAN ACTUALLY BE EXECUTED

From A9 green until the tag is pushed: HELD (recorded in the round report, outside the twenty hashed files, landed in DEVIATIONS.md after the push — the default) or FIXED (only when the finding is itself a halt condition, or when the author rules it fixed). No disposition writes to DEVIATIONS.md before the tag — DEVIATIONS.md is one of the twenty.

2.10 The rest, unchanged
  1. The report is a file. Bank each item before the next; bank each failed attempt before writing the next script.
  2. Scripts that edit repository content are write-once-guarded (§2.2 now governs the guard) and their effect is verified by reading, never by re-running.
  3. §218. Every irreversible act in its OWN invocation, after the preceding exit status has been READ.
  4. D2.1, with B8.2's detector behind it.
  5. Derivation, not assertion. 6. §36.2 at set scale. 7. Register form. 8. Frozen dated records are superseded, never rewritten.
  6. Stage explicitly; never git add -A. 10. Line endings checked per file before every write. 11. Never end a turn on an announcement.

B8.3 — REPORT B8's RESULTS [~30 min] ← take this now, per §2.4

The sweep completed four rounds ago and no summary has reached the report. It gets its own section:

Do not score against the R9 ground-truth map. SC-7(c) keeps the map out of the tool's input surface, and B8's output is a dependency map — Layer 1 — not a verdict set. Reporting it as a verdict set would be the tool making exactly the claim it exists to catch other tools making.

  • Value detector — preserving: (shuffle, in-dtype sentinel) × all columns; promoted: (out-of-dtype sentinel,) × all columns.
  • Null detector — preserving: (nan,) × float columns; promoted: (nan,) × int columns.

  §6.6 permits a combination whose eligible cohorts are a dtype-defined subset
      -> build both detectors as above
  every combination must span all columns
      -> report the clause and propose an alternative; do not force it
  an empty promoted combination is legal
      -> the value detector may omit the out-of-dtype sentinel; simpler
  otherwise -> HALT
§9.2 — EXECUTE THE COMPARATORS [~3 h]

Against the acceptance fixture, not the prior-art set. Each comparator with its own positive control first — a failing or absent control forces uninterpretable regardless of what the tool reported. could_not_run maps to covered_with_exclusion, never a pass. Zero comparators run is not a pass (SC-11a). Not blocking the tag; it blocks publishing any Phase 1 result.

B10 — REPORT, then continue into the standing sequence (§2.4).

5. H-L26 — lands at A15(5)

  • Bank the attempt, not only the success — and bank the finding when it is found, not when it is characterized.
  • An exemption whose anchor no longer resolves is an exemption granted to whatever now occupies that position, by nobody.
  • A check whose population is a pinned path reports on the path, not the work.
  • Do not transcribe the thing under test. Intercept its inputs instead.
  • An adapter that serves an aggregate makes the raw frame unread; probing an unread frame records a silence the adapter caused and the report presents as a fact about the pipeline.
  • An instrument that scans files must exclude its own source.
  • A rule restated in every round and violated in three of them is not a discipline problem. Detect the damage instead of recalling the rule.
  • A status marker is a verification value, not prose — and a dated record correct as of its date is not a stale marker.
  • A closeout rule that says "record it and proceed" must name a place the record can go.
  • An amendment applied in part leaves the applied half citing the unapplied half. Thirteen of fifteen hunks landed; the two that did not were what five landed clauses pointed at, and every gate passed — because no gate asks whether a citation resolves.
  • Three times a superseded version sat where the current one belonged, with nothing marking it superseded, and a gate passed over each: a tag message from the prior version, a status header from before the file was registered, and a draft block still cited as current while the revision sat in the source of record. When two versions of one text exist, name which is authoritative at the point of use — not in a document somewhere that says so.
  • A guard that passes for the wrong reason is worse than a guard that fails, because its pass is read as evidence. Ours probed a blank line and would have reported an unapplied change as already applied.
  • Markdown structure is semantics. A horizontal rule flush against a paragraph turns that paragraph into a heading, and a registered line quietly became something else.

2. STANDING RULES

2.1 A DERIVED VALUE STATES ITS DERIVATION

A count, total or enumeration in registered text names the population it was derived from and the method, so a reader can re-derive it. The 6-versus-23 divergence survived because a hand-authored count had no way to be re-checked and no gate asks. Derivation is not only how a value is produced — it is what the text has to say about itself.

2.2 HUNK TEXT IS READ FROM SSF, NEVER FROM A SPLIT WORKING FILE

Where SSF and any split or working document disagree about amendment text, SSF is the text. Fourth instance of the same shape this ceremony: a superseded version sitting where the current one belonged, with nothing marking it superseded, and a gate passing over it.

2.3 MARKDOWN STRUCTURE IS SEMANTICS, NOT FORMATTING

A --- flush against a paragraph is a setext heading underline. After any structural insertion into a registered markdown file, confirm the lines above and below still parse as what they were.

2.4 A GUARD MUST PROBE SOMETHING DISTINCTIVE, OR IT GUARDS NOTHING

A guard that passes for the wrong reason is worse than one that fails, because its pass is read as evidence. Probe a line that appears nowhere else, and say in the guard which line it probes and why that line is unique.

2.5 THE PARALLELISM WINDOW IS ANY WAIT ON THE AUTHOR — a halt included.

State the halt, bank it, begin the next Track B item. Do not ask; do not idle.

2.6 PROVISIONAL RESOLUTION

Resolve rather than halt if all five hold: reversible (no tag, push, stamp, or commit to main); does not change what a registered text SAYS; does not require deciding what an amendment MEANS; every option preserves all five quality rules; and you can state the choice, the alternatives and the reason in three sentences. Take the option most conservative for a future reader; record as PROVISIONAL; unoverturned next round it settles.

2.7 CHECK A SILENCE, DON'T REPORT IT

aggressor_side is the case: a column the builder demonstrably reads went silent under a valid probe. Reported as-is it reads as a probe hole and the finding dies. Where a silence contradicts something you know about the pipeline, establish the mechanism before recording the outcome — then record both.

2.8 The rest, unchanged

Bank the finding when found, not when characterized · bank each failed attempt · background any block over ~10 min · the instrument's population excludes the instrument and its size is asserted first · a status marker is a verification value, fixed not disclosed, but a dated record correct as of its date is not a stale marker · §218, every irreversible act in its own invocation after the preceding exit status is READ · D2.1 with B8.2's detector behind it · derivation, not assertion · §36.2 at set scale · register form · frozen dated records superseded, never rewritten · stage explicitly, never git add -A · line endings checked per file before every write · never end a turn on an announcement.

2.9 THE CLOSEOUT RULE, AS IT CAN BE EXECUTED

From A9 green until the tag is pushed: HELD (recorded in the round report, outside the twenty hashed files, landed in DEVIATIONS.md after the push) or FIXED (only when the finding is itself a halt condition, or the author rules it fixed). No disposition writes to DEVIATIONS.md before the tag.

  • An amendment applied in part leaves the applied half citing the unapplied half, and every gate passed, because no gate asks whether a citation resolves.
  • Four times a superseded version sat where the current one belonged with nothing marking it superseded. When two versions of one text exist, name which is authoritative at the point of use.
  • A guard that passes for the wrong reason is worse than one that fails.
  • Markdown structure is semantics: a rule flush against a paragraph turned a registered line into a heading.
  • A hand-authored count cannot be re-checked and no gate asks. Six became twenty-three and the table went on saying six. A derived value must state its derivation, or it is an assertion wearing a number's clothes.
  • The probe went silent on a column the builder reads, and the silence was the finding: a predicate false for every row, a feature named for signed flow carrying negative volume. The declaration had already frozen the symptom as a degenerate constant. Measuring found that something was wrong; perturbing found what.

2. STANDING RULES

2.1 AN INSTRUMENT MUST NOT TREAT THE FALSIFIER AS THE CONFIRMATION

The declaration's clause probe searched for the heading stem and reported two citations as RESOLVING at l.579 and l.580 — the exact lines A20 had proved were never replaced. It found the superseded text and counted that as the citation resolving. A citation claiming "X was superseded by clause Y" was confirmed by locating X.

This is not a domain that is too narrow. It is an instrument whose evidence for a claim is the thing that falsifies it. When a probe checks that a supersession happened, it must require the marker of the new text — never the presence of the old. Ask of every screen: could this pass by finding exactly what the claim says should be gone?

2.2 DERIVE, DON'T SAMPLE

Where the question is "does X match Y", build Y from its source and compare, rather than testing X for properties Y should have. Five rounds sampled this file and each sample proved the last partial; two reconstructions answered exactly. A20b's whole-file longest-common-substring is the same move: remove the unit that could hide the answer.

2.3 THE CHAT MESSAGE CARRIES THE HEADLINE AND THE POINTER, ALWAYS

Before a turn can end, one line exists in chat: the headline finding and the report path.

2.4 ENCODING IS A SILENT-FAILURE VECTOR ON THIS MACHINE

append_section.py died in the cp1252 console encoder on a ⛔ and did not bank its section. Every script that writes or prints reconfigures stdout to UTF-8, and the write comes after every check, so a late failure lands nothing partial. That ordering is why this one cost nothing.

2.5 The rest, unchanged

A derived value states its derivation · hunk text is read from SSF, never a split working file · markdown structure is semantics, checked before the write · a guard must probe something distinctive · the parallelism window is any wait on the author, a halt included · check a silence, don't report it · the instrument's population excludes the instrument and its size is asserted first · bank the finding when found, and each failed attempt · a status marker is a verification value, but a dated record correct as of its date is not · §218 · D2.1 · derivation not assertion · §36.2 at set scale · register form · frozen dated records superseded, never rewritten · stage explicitly, never git add -A · line endings checked per file before every write · seed every stochastic instrument from a stable function and record the seed · background any block over ~10 min · never end a turn on an announcement.

2.6 PROVISIONAL RESOLUTION

Resolve rather than halt if all five hold: reversible; does not change what a registered text SAYS; does not require deciding what an amendment MEANS; every option preserves the five quality rules; statable in three sentences. Take the option most conservative for a future reader; record as PROVISIONAL; unoverturned next round it settles.

2. STANDING RULES

Read a precedent at its authority, not at the document citing it · do not answer an undecided question by producing its artifact · enumerate by deriving, never by transcribing a prior enumeration · an instrument must not treat the falsifier as the confirmation — could this screen pass by finding exactly what the claim says should be gone? · derive, don't sample · the chat message carries the headline and the report path before the turn ends · encoding is a silent-failure vector: reconfigure stdout, and the write comes after every check · a derived value states its derivation · hunk text is read from SSF · markdown structure is semantics, checked before the write · a guard must probe something distinctive · the parallelism window is any wait on the author, a halt included · check a silence, don't report it · the instrument's population excludes the instrument, size asserted first · bank the finding when found and each failed attempt · a status marker is a verification value, but a dated record correct as of its date is not · §218 · D2.1 · derivation not assertion · §36.2 at set scale · register form · frozen dated records superseded, never rewritten · stage explicitly, never git add -A · line endings checked per file before every write · seed every stochastic instrument from a stable function and record the seed · background any block over ~10 min · never end a turn on an announcement.

2.1 PROVISIONAL RESOLUTION

Resolve rather than halt if all five hold: reversible; does not change what a registered text SAYS; does not require deciding what an amendment MEANS; every option preserves the five quality rules; statable in three sentences. Take the option most conservative for a future reader; record as PROVISIONAL; unoverturned next round it settles.

5. H-L26 — held until HISTORY.md is unfrozen

  • Derive, don't sample. Five rounds probed one file; two reconstructions answered exactly.
  • An instrument must not treat the falsifier as the confirmation.
  • A registration can be unsatisfiable and no citation will say so. Only arithmetic found that criterion 2's anchor cannot be met by any horizon.
  • Read a precedent at its authority.
  • A list carried forward is an assertion, not a finding.
  • Do not answer an undecided question by producing its artifact.
  • A suspension can force work onto the branch that cannot carry it. A rule written to protect the tagged tree pushed an edit to a hashed file onto a branch the tag would never see.
  • An amendment can be applied perfectly and still be described wrongly.
  • A long common substring is not a quotation.
  • Do not transcribe the thing under test — intercept its inputs.
  • A guard that passes for the wrong reason is worse than one that fails.
  • The probe went silent on a column the builder reads, and the silence was the finding.
  • hash() on a string is salted per process; the byte-identical re-run was luck, not evidence.
  • A red that says one true thing beats a green bought by transcribing a block that forbids transcription.

2. STANDING RULES

A presentation of a text never becomes the text (§2.1, new) · read a precedent at its authority · do not answer an undecided question by producing its artifact · enumerate by deriving, never by transcribing a prior enumeration · an instrument must not treat the falsifier as the confirmation · derive, don't sample · the chat message carries the headline and the report path before the turn ends · encoding is a silent-failure vector; the write comes after every check · a derived value states its derivation · hunk text is read from SSF · markdown structure is semantics, checked before the write · a guard must probe something distinctive, and pin the invariant rather than a constant (§2.2) · the parallelism window is any wait on the author, a halt included · check a silence, don't report it · the instrument's population excludes the instrument, size asserted first · bank the finding when found and each failed attempt · a status marker is a verification value, but a dated record correct as of its date is not · §218 · D2.1 · derivation not assertion · §36.2 at set scale · register form · frozen dated records superseded, never rewritten · stage explicitly, never git add -A · line endings checked per file before every write · seed every stochastic instrument from a stable function and record the seed · background any block over ~10 min · never end a turn on an announcement.

2.1 NEW — A PRESENTATION OF A TEXT NEVER BECOMES THE TEXT

A24 applied from PREREG_v30a_DIFF.md, not from the proposal document derived from it. A derived presentation used as a source puts a second copy in the chain, and the two drift the moment either is touched. Apply from the source; present from a copy. Same rule as SSF over a split working file, one level up.

2.2 NEW — A GUARD PINS THE INVARIANT, NOT A CONSTANT

The reconciler's guard pinned a literal when the property it protects is "unchanged by this script." Fixing the guard rather than re-pinning the constant is the same move as D8's anchor conversion: state what must hold, not what currently holds. A guard that needs updating whenever the thing it guards changes is a maintenance obligation wearing a check's clothes.

2.3 PROVISIONAL RESOLUTION

Resolve rather than halt if all five hold: reversible; does not change what a registered text SAYS; does not require deciding what an amendment MEANS; every option preserves the five quality rules; statable in three sentences. Take the option most conservative for a future reader; record as PROVISIONAL; unoverturned next round it settles.

An environment note told the agent to make file changes with sed/heredocs. Shell reads and searches are fine and always were. An ambient instruction does not renegotiate a safety rule; flag the conflict, follow the stricter rule.

2. STANDING RULES

2.1 NEW — A DECLARED RANGE IS A CLAIM ABOUT A BOUNDARY; VERIFY THE BOUNDARY

BLOCK_MANIFEST's ranges were treated as authoritative and were 8 lines short twice. When extracting a delimited structure, derive the extent from the structure's own delimiters — the blockquote's fence, the table's last row — and treat a declared range as a cross-check, not a source. A range that ends mid-structure is a finding about the manifest, not a licence to truncate.

2.2 NEW — AFTER A FIX, SWEEP FOR THE PROSE THAT DESCRIBED THE DEFECT (§1.3)
2.3 The rest, standing

A source that warns against its own use is not a source · a positive control shows reachability; a pair shows discrimination · supersession is not approval · D2.1 generalised (§1.2) · a presentation of a text never becomes the text · a guard pins the invariant, not a constant · read a precedent at its authority · do not answer an undecided question by producing its artifact · enumerate by deriving, never by transcribing · an instrument must not treat the falsifier as the confirmation · derive, don't sample · the chat message carries the headline and the report path before the turn ends · encoding is a silent-failure vector; the write comes after every check · a derived value states its derivation · hunk text is read from SSF · markdown structure is semantics, checked before the write · a guard must probe something distinctive · the parallelism window is any wait on the author, a halt included · check a silence, don't report it · the instrument's population excludes the instrument, size asserted first · bank the finding when found and each failed attempt · a status marker is a verification value, but a dated record correct as of its date is not · §218 · derivation not assertion · §36.2 at set scale · register form · frozen dated records superseded, never rewritten · stage explicitly, never git add -A · line endings checked per file before every write · seed every stochastic instrument and record the seed · background any block over ~10 min · never end a turn on an announcement.

2.4 PROVISIONAL RESOLUTION

Resolve rather than halt if all five hold: reversible; does not change what a registered text SAYS; does not require deciding what an amendment MEANS; every option preserves the five quality rules; statable in three sentences. Most conservative for a future reader; recorded PROVISIONAL; unoverturned next round it settles.

5. H-L26 — held until HISTORY.md is unfrozen

  • A declared range is a claim about a boundary; verify the boundary. Two blocks were eight lines short, and the missing lines carried one block's central holding.
  • A fix can falsify the note that described the defect. The provenance note was true until the hunk landed; then every clause of it was false.
  • An approval covers what was read. Sixteen unseen lines do not ride in on an approval of the truncated version, however correct they are.
  • A safety rule outranks an ambient instruction. The environment said heredocs; the rule said file-write tool; the agent flagged the conflict and followed the stricter rule.
  • A source that warns against its own use is not a source.
  • A positive control shows reachability; a pair shows discrimination.
  • Supersession is not approval.
  • Derive, don't sample.
  • An instrument must not treat the falsifier as the confirmation.
  • A registration can be unsatisfiable and no citation will say so.
  • A mapped gate fed the wrong quantity never fires, and never-fired reads as clean.
  • A red that says one true thing beats a green bought by transcribing a block that forbids transcription.

2.2 NEW — AN ADAPTER THAT NEVER POSES THE QUESTION PRODUCES A SILENCE ABOUT

The harness reported the nohup & wrapper's exit as completion while the python process ran on. Track the PID that does the work, or the artifact it must produce — never the shell that launched it.

1. AUTHORITY

1.1 THE TABLE'S FRAMING — three failure modes, one conclusion

"No tool separates the pair" is the claim, and the table shows it three ways: firing identically on both sides, passing both sides, and pointing the wrong way. A tool that fires on everything fails discrimination exactly as a silent one does. The corrections that made the table fair are in the table, not a footnote — keep it that way into any published form.

1.2 DISCHARGE REQUIRES CONTROLS THROUGH THE FINAL ADAPTERS

Step 2's controls ran through the old adapter path; three adapters were then rebuilt. The standing rule — the control must exercise the path the measurement takes — applies to the fix itself.

DECISION 1.2:
  each rebuilt adapter's control, run through the FINAL path, still fires
      -> §D.5(i) is DISCHARGED. Record it in the table; the publish-block on
         B8/B9's results LIFTS.
  a control no longer fires through the final path
      -> that tool's fixture rows are uninterpretable; mark them so and record
         why. The table stands with that row corrected; discharge proceeds on
         the remaining rows per §D.5(i)'s terms.
  otherwise -> HALT
1.3 THE TABLE'S MISSING ROW — the project's own tool. Post-tag design item,

first in the queue. Six external tools, none separating the pair, and no row showing ours does — a reader will ask, and the comparison is asymmetric until it is there. What "separates" means for our tool is a design question: the dependency map may look similar on both sides; the difference lives in availability verdicts, and SC-7 constrains what the tool may be given (never the map). Propose before building — the same discipline as aggressor_side.

1.4 All prior rulings stand. PREREG is closed.

2. STANDING RULES — unchanged from R148 §2, plus:

2.1 NEW — A TOOL THAT FIRES ON EVERYTHING FAILS THE PAIR THE SAME WAY A

SILENT ONE DOES. Discrimination is the instrument; both failure modes are "cannot separate," and a table must not read constant firing as detection.

2.2 NEW — A FIX TO THE MEASUREMENT PATH RE-OPENS THE CONTROL

Any change to an adapter, harness, or input shape after controls ran means the control has not tested what the measurement now does. Re-run the control through the final path before believing the measurement.

  • A control is drawn from the regime the measurement operates in, and the regime is derived, never tuned.   • A frozen tree turns the banking rule against itself. The reconciler scans the pinned root; a record banked there with no repo twin reds the gate at exactly the moment the gate must stay green. While frozen, bank outside the scanned domain and name the fold.

4. TRACK B — PROBE A

B-6 — BUILD THE AVAILABILITY PROBE [~3–4 h; background the sweeps]

The cohort probe from the original architecture, now under the registered machinery that has existed since before the tool:

  • Input: the same (raw, build) surface, plus the declared availability model — SC-7(a)'s permitted input. The same declaration for both sides: the model describes when cells become available in reality; the sides differ in what the code does with them, not in when they arrived.
  • Mechanism: per decision cohort, corrupt every cell with a(j,c) > d(i) — all at once — re-run once, compare exact. Movement ⇒ the feature depends on unavailable information for that cohort. Silence ⇒ observed_silence covering exactly that cohort, with its domain.
  • Discipline, all standing: determinism guard per frame · promotion-status handling per §3.2/§6.6 (two combinations, square products) · seeds stable and recorded · reducers unchanged — if a reducer rejects the trace, the trace is wrong · the excluded MBO frame stays excluded and auditable · SC-7(c): the R9 map never reaches the tool.
  • Known positive before any clean result is believed: a callable that reads a cell the model marks unavailable (the contaminated side's current-bar mid read is the natural candidate — but build a synthetic one too, so the probe's own test does not depend on the thing under measurement).
  • Known negative: a callable reading only available cells; the probe must stay silent, and the negative control's regime is derived from the fixture, never tuned.
B-7 — RUN BOTH SIDES [~two sweeps; background]

Two per-side runs, harness-compared — SC-7(d)'s shape. Report per cohort per side: fired / silent / could_not_run, with silence accounting and domains. Then the row, per §1.2's three-part framing, published whatever it shows.

Seven rows: six external tools + ours, each row stating what it is evidence of. Layer 1's invariance stated as designed. Post-tag, this and the B8/B9 results wire into the README.

(carries the aggressor_side adoption and Probe A's design) → D10 fail-loud redesign → R110 → K2 → criterion-5 polish (install docs final pass).

2. STANDING RULES — unchanged from R152 §2, plus:

2.1 NEW — A PER-FRAME GUARD IS NEVER SUMMED

A guard over N frames asserts per frame, and reports per frame. An aggregate green over per-frame reds is the sibling of N checks over one wrong population: the total was true and the truth was hidden.

2.2 NEW — A TIMEZONE BOUNDARY IS A SILENT NON-MATCH

tz-aware against tz-naive never matches and never errors. At every comparison boundary between time columns, normalize explicitly and assert the per-frame match count — an all-False mask is indistinguishable from a true negative.

2.3 NEW — A PERTURBATION FITS THE DTYPE'S RANGE, NOT JUST ITS KIND

Overflow is the widening cast's quieter cousin. The offset is chosen to be representable at any width, and the guarantee that the value differs is asserted, not assumed.

The commit chain already orders criteria before probe (b5a05c0 was frozen before Probe A existed); the tag makes that order cryptographic. Running acceptance pre-tag would hand a skeptic the one argument this whole apparatus exists to foreclose.

2. STANDING RULES — unchanged from R153 §2, plus:

2.1 NEW — A COMBINATION THAT RAN NOTHING IS A FACT

Emit it (not_applicable × none), never omit it. An absent record and a recorded non-run are different claims, and only one survives an audit.

2.2 NEW — A REQUIRED FIELD IN A FROZEN CONTRACT IS A DESIGN REVIEW

The contract demanded a feature the probe could not name, and the probe got better. When an instrument cannot fill a required field, the gap is the instrument's — fill it with capability, never with a placeholder.

1. THE TWO RULINGS

1.1 — The README's v30a hash block lacks the "as of the tag" framing

The finding is correct and it matters more than it looks. The v30a block presents twenty hashes with no statement of when they were true. The moment DEVIATIONS.md and HISTORY.md are written, at least two of those twenty stop matching. A stranger who checks the README's hashes against the repo then gets mismatches with no explanation — and a stranger checking is the entire content of criterion 5. The v30 block already carries the framing; the v30a block was written without it.

Ruled: fix the framing BEFORE the first write, not after. Both orderings reach the same end state, but only one never puts the repository into a state where its own README makes a false claim. That is A15-3a.

The wording is copied from v30's block, read at the README itself — not paraphrased, not invented. Precedent is read at its authority.

1.2 — The manifest line on the receipt is a scheduled gate failure, and it is mine

v30 tracks its receipt files with no manifest line. R158 asked for one. The line went in and the gate is green — but when the Bitcoin attestation lands and the receipt is upgraded, the .ots file's bytes change, its sha256 changes, and the manifest line I ordered goes stale. The gate turns red on a scheduled date for a reason nobody will remember.

Two ways out. Drop the line and match v30 — the receipt is already attested by git and by its own content, so manifest coverage adds little. Or keep the line and make re-hashing it a named part of the upgrade.

Ruled: keep the line. A gate that goes red when the receipt changes is a live check; silence is not. But that only holds if the obligation is written down now, so §3 carries it as a named step rather than a thing to remember.

Two consequences, both required:

  • The divergence from v30's practice is deliberate and gets recorded at A15-4 as a practice choice with its reason. An unexplained asymmetry between v30 and v30a in the registration record is exactly the kind of thing that costs rounds later. It is not a DEVIATIONS.md entry — the registration does not specify how receipts are tracked, so nothing was deviated from.
  • The pre-upgrade receipt needs no separate preservation step; commit 8fc0a95 holds those bytes permanently.

1. THE DRIFT — first turn, nothing else runs beside it

A15-3a asked a question nobody had asked before: how many of the twenty currently differ from the hashes the tag attests? The answer was three — HISTORY.md, tools/check_registration.py, and DEVIATIONS.md.

DEVIATIONS.md is explained: A15-3b wrote it, deliberately, after the freeze lifted. The other two are not.

Two of these matter differently. HISTORY.md is out of order — A15-6 has not run yet, so whatever changed it changed it outside the step that is supposed to. That is a bookkeeping problem. tools/check_registration.py is not a bookkeeping problem. It is the instrument that verifies the registration, and it is inside the registered set precisely so that it cannot be quietly adjusted to make a failing registration pass. If it changed during a close-out whose steps were each gated by its own output, the hypothesis that has to be ruled out first is the worst one: the instrument was adjusted so a result would come out right. That is the second quality rule, in the form it exists to catch.

I do not think that is what happened. I think it is far likelier to be incidental. But "likelier to be innocent" is not a finding, and this is a registered artifact.

1. THE GOVERNING PRINCIPLE

When an instrument fails, the first move is to fix the world, not the instrument.

An instrument is changed only when the world genuinely cannot be fixed — and then the change is disclosed, with the pre-change instrument's result on the current tree recorded beside it. Never silently, never as a step inside the work the instrument is grading.

Corollary, and it is the whole finding: a green gate that is green only because of a post-hoc exemption is not a green gate. It is a red gate with the red suppressed. The current tree's true status is the tag's checker's status — exit 1, two real failures — until the world is fixed.

0. ESTABLISHED — from §3.1, read-only, nothing changed

§2.1. One D2 finding on the whole tree: HISTORY.md:236, review lesson 28. Zero hex runs of 16+ characters — not one of the twenty digests appears on the line in any form. It trips D2 by naming three registered basenames (DEVIATIONS.md, HISTORY.md, check_registration.py). The fourth path in the finding, PREREG.md, is not on the line at all — the check reads a two-line window and takes it from the ### H-30 — from PREREG.md §6.6 heading below. The detector's own comment states its intent: path enumerations purporting to BE the set. Lesson 28 does not purport to be the set.

§2.2. HISTORY.md:277, l.277, line 277 — zero occurrences in the tree. COMMIT_PLAN.md:217: "HISTORY.md's ### H-34 heading (cited by heading, not line — l.264 was empty by R69, the entry having moved to 271)." CEREMONY_COMMANDS.md:28 and H34_DRAFT.md:28 concur; H34_DRAFT.md:35 calls its line numbers a DATED SNAPSHOT. The pin table's convention: a number means cited by line; None means by heading. The H-34 entry's reason string — "COMMIT_PLAN.md §3 cites the H-34 heading" — is unchanged between the tag and HEAD. At the tag the entry carried a line number while its own justification said heading.

Register relocation is counter-indicated. Lessons append at l.236, above H-30 (238) and H-34 (281); both are cited by heading. The pins at 218/219 (H-L12, H-L13) are genuine by-line citations that resolve correctly today and sit above the append point, so appends do not move them. Moving the register to the file's end would break two real citations to repair one that was never made.

1. THE TEST THAT DECIDES BOTH

R162's principle — fix the world, not the instrument — assumes the instrument is right. Here it is wrong twice. So the principle needs its companion, and this is the rule the project keeps:

Would this instrument change have been made if the content that triggered it did not exist?

Yes → a defect repair. Permitted, once ruled, disclosed, and tested against a known positive. No → an exemption. Forbidden, whatever the reasoning.

And one more, because it is the trap in both of Claude Code's questions:

The ground stated in the record must be the real ground. "Otherwise we were blocked" is never a permitted ground, even when the change is right on other grounds. A record that says a change was made because the alternative was inconvenient cannot be told apart from the bad case by anyone reading it later.

2. RULING — §2.1, THE D2 FINDING

Lesson 28 is not reworded. Not one word. It is a truthful record of what happened; editing it so a defective proxy stops complaining is content adjusted toward a check — the second quality rule, violated head-on, and worse than the exemption was.

The region exemption reverts. An exemption keyed to a region hides a defect instead of fixing it, and this one was made silently inside the work it was grading.

The detector's defect is then repaired properly. By the §1 test this qualifies: a proxy that fires on prose naming three registered filenames does not match its own documented intent, and that is true regardless of whether lesson 28 exists. Two defects are visible:

  1. len(hits) >= 3 over basenames, with no requirement that any digest be present. A hash set without hashes is not a hash set.
  2. A two-line window that attributes the following heading's content to this line. That produced a fourth path that is not on the line.

Lean — establish before adopting: require at least one actual digest in the region before D2 fires, and fix the window. That aligns the check to its stated intent, drops lesson 28 without any exemption, and still catches a genuine second copy of the hash set.

DECISION 2:
  the repair as leaned makes D2 match its documented intent
      -> adopt it. THEN test it against a KNOWN POSITIVE: construct a genuine
         second hash-set enumeration — paths WITH digests — drawn from outside
         the detector's own domain, and confirm D2 fires on it. A repaired
         instrument whose clean result has not been tested against a positive is
         not a repaired instrument.
  the repair as leaned would suppress a real enumeration shape
      -> HALT and report the shape. Do not adopt a repair that trades one blind
         spot for another.
  D2 fires anywhere else on the tree once repaired
      -> report every hit before proceeding.

If the repair cannot be made cleanly, the gate stays red with the defect disclosed. A red gate that states the truth is an acceptable end state and is allowed to persist across invocations. It is not an acceptable end state for A15-7, which is why this is being resolved now rather than deferred.

The planning layer rules on principle. It does not lean on measurable properties of the repository — it asks for the measurement.

A lean about what the corpus contains is a guess wearing a ruling's clothes. A lean about whether a change is an exemption or a repair is a ruling, because that question is decided by principle and the principle is mine to set.

1. THE WINDOW — DEFERRED, and why it is not the exemption again

Option (b), "narrow only forward", is forbidden. Forward-only is being chosen because the backward line happens to be harmless for these three tuples. That is the corpus tuning the change — the same pattern refused twice already, wearing a third costume. The principled question is not which side breaks less; it is what the window was intended to be, which is a measurable property of the repository and therefore not mine to lean on.

Options (a) and (b) collapse. Any real repair re-derives the tuples, because the tuples are window-derived. So the honest choice is: repair properly — correct the window to its intended form, re-derive all five tuples uniformly (never only the three that break), known-positive test, disclose — or defer.

Ruled: DEFER, and repair it in Track B together with the D2 discriminator.

The grounds, in the order that decides it:

  1. They are one subsystem. A discriminator design may change what window is right. Fixing the window now means designing it twice, and the second design would be constrained by the first.
  2. The gain is cosmetic. The window did not cause the false positive — lesson 28 carries three basenames on its own line and fires without any window. The window only added a fourth path to the finding's reported list.
  3. The cost is not. Re-deriving five recorded allowed-counts is a substantive change to registered content, made during the close-out, at the risk of three new gate findings against a gate pinned at one.

This is not the exemption again, and the difference is the whole point. The exemption suppressed a finding. Deferring the window suppresses nothing: the finding still fires, it is disclosed as a false positive, and the window's true shape is recorded with its measurement. Nothing is hidden; one repair is scheduled.

R1662026-08-28THE CORRECTION I OWE, AND THE RULE THAT FOLLOWS

Supersedes R116 through R165 in their entirety. Work from this document only.

The worktree harness was my prescription and it was wrong. The cause of the control_characters artifact was never the script's location — it was a relative --root. The harness I specified manufactures two new failures, and it was caught only because R165 made its disappearance the harness's own test.

0. ESTABLISHED — from R166's step 1, nothing implemented

The artifact's real cause:

p = (root / "evidence" / rel).resolve()        # absolute
try:    pop[p.relative_to(root).as_posix()] = p
except: pop[rel] = p                            # <- loses the "evidence/" prefix

--root . is relative, p is resolved absolute, relative_to raises, and the fallback key drops the prefix so the exemption misses.

Tested directly: with an absolute root, control_characters PASSES. The tag checker drops from 3 failures / 10 findings to 2 failures / 2 findings, leaving exactly line_citations as the sole difference — which is precisely R165 §5's permitted set, reached without a worktree.

The worktree harness manufactures two new failures, manifest_coverage and round_reconciliation. It fails its own test.

1. THE CORRECTION I OWE, AND THE RULE THAT FOLLOWS

R162 §3.4, R163 §5, R164 §5 and R165 §3.1 all specified "extract via git show / git worktree into the same relative location." That came from my diagnosis that the artifact was caused by the script's location. The diagnosis was wrong, and the mechanism I prescribed on the strength of it introduces artifacts of its own.

This is the fourth of my leans on a measurable property to die on measurement, one delta after H-L35 was written against exactly that. But it failed in a new place, and the new place is the useful one:

The planning layer specifies the REQUIREMENT and its TEST. It does not specify the MECHANISM.

"The harness must not manufacture differences, and its proof is that control_characters disappears" was mine to write, and it was right — it is what caught this. "Use a worktree at the same relative location" was not mine to write, and it was wrong.

The test survived my bad mechanism. That is the whole argument for writing tests into deltas rather than instructions.

And a correction to R165 §4: I called the lesson register "final, superseding all prior specifications," and this round produced two more entries. The prohibition that mattered was against renumbering or splitting H-L29–H-L41, and that stands. "Final" was the wrong word while rounds were still producing findings. The register closes at A15-6's commit, not before.

2. THE HARNESS — diagnose, then choose

DECISION 2 (diagnose FIRST, read-only, report before implementing):
  manifest_coverage and round_reconciliation fire because the worktree does not
  reproduce tree state those checks read — i.e. they are worktree artifacts
      -> DROP THE WORKTREE. The harness is: extract the tag's checker to a file
         with `git show prereg-v30a:tools/check_registration.py`, run it against
         the CURRENT tree with an ABSOLUTE --root, matching the gate's own
         invocation form. Already demonstrated to yield exactly line_citations.
  they are real differences between the two checkers
      -> HALT. That is a third instrument difference and it outranks everything
         downstream.
  the cause is neither, or cannot be established by reading
      -> HALT and report what you found.

The harness's acceptance test is unchanged and is not negotiable: run both checkers on the same tree, and the difference is exactly line_citations. Any harness that produces more, or fewer, is not accepted — whatever its shape. The shape is yours to choose; the property is not.

3. THE LATENT DEFECT — establish, disclose, defer

The checker's output depends on whether --root is absolute. An instrument that reports differently according to its invocation form is one bad invocation from a false alarm or a false clean.

DECISION 3 (read-only, ~10 min):
  establish how the gate is normally invoked — every invocation path in the repo,
  scripts and documented commands alike — and whether each passes an absolute or
  a relative root.
    every path passes an absolute root -> the gate's history is unaffected.
                                          Record that, with the paths listed.
    any path passes a relative root    -> report it. That path's past results
                                          carried a spurious control_characters
                                          failure or its equivalent, and the
                                          record needs to say so.

Do not repair it this turn. Same reasoning as the window: an instrument change during the close-out it certifies, against a gate pinned at one finding, for a defect that is now understood and disclosed. It joins the D2 discriminator and the window in Track B, and the three are designed together — they are one subsystem and this is the third time that has proved true.

1. THE SECOND FINDING — my rule was too broad, and the process point still stands

D10 fired on the work root's stale mirror during A15-4's gate. Claude Code diagnosed it as the known coupling, verified the mirror was a byte-identical duplicate, applied D10's own documented "bring it in" remedy, re-gated to one finding, committed, and recorded it in the commit message rather than passing over it.

Every one of those steps was correct. And the batch was under a halt list that said any second gate finding halts, and it did not halt.

Both halves are true and both go in the record.

My half, and it is the larger one. The halt list did not distinguish a new, unexplained finding from a previously-ruled coupling with a remedy documented in the check itself. A rule that would halt a batch over a byte-identical stale mirror is a rule that will be overridden, and writing a rule that invites its own override is a drafting failure, not an execution one. Pre-ruling the known cases is what a decision tree is for and it is my job.

The process half, which is not cancelled by the outcome being fine. When a halt list says halt and the situation looks like it warrants an exception, the correct move is to halt and say "the halt list says stop; here is why I believe it should not apply; ruling?" — not to apply the exception and report it after. An instrument that says stop, overridden by an operator who believes it does not mean it, is the same shape as the thing this close-out was convened to examine. The difference between an exception judged correctly and one judged wrongly is invisible from inside the judgment.

The corrected rule — in force for the rest of the batch
A second gate finding appears:
  it is D10 on the work root's stale mirror
      -> DISCHARGEABLE. Verify byte-identical first; apply D10's own documented
         remedy; re-gate; report it at the TOP of the report, not inside a step's
         paragraph. Continue.
  anything else, of any kind
      -> HALT where it stands. Report it and wait. Do not discharge it, do not
         diagnose past it, do not finish the step you are in.

That list has exactly one entry. If a second coupling turns out to deserve one, it is added by me, in a delta, before the batch that meets it — never in the moment.

  1. Write each lesson accurately. Its content is decided by what happened, not by what the checker tolerates.
  2. If an accurate lesson needs three or more registered paths on one line, split it across lines. Splitting is choosing among true phrasings; it costs nothing.
  3. If it cannot be split without losing content, write it accurately and accept a second gate finding, reporting it under §1's HALT branch.

Never drop or soften a lesson's content to keep the gate at one finding. That is exactly what was refused for lesson 28, and a lesson authored under the constraint is no more permitted to be inaccurate than one already written.

Normative language is already present in four existing lessons, so the register's own convention permits it — that check was the right one to run.

1. THE POSTURE CHANGES HERE

Ceremony intensity was proportionate to a one-shot signed object that could not be revised after the fact. Track B is writing Python against a deadline.

  • The five quality rules govern. The freeze apparatus does not.
  • Halt lists shrink to genuinely irreversible acts and genuinely ambiguous scope. Ordinary code, tests and docs do not need a pre-ruled branch each.
  • Batching is the default, not the exception. Report at natural boundaries, not per commit.
  • Cost budgets still apply to read-only sweeps; exceeding one by 10× is still a halt.
  • The register is closed at H-L45. Track B's lessons accumulate for a later append; it is not reopened per round.

Criterion 5 — installable by a stranger, 15 October 2026 — is 47 days out and has had no work against it. That is the binding constraint on every scope call from here.

2. THE BRANCH RECONCILE — no rebase

A15-5 specified a rebase: 36 commits replayed onto a main carrying 44 they lack, conflicts at nearly every commit, a prior attempt halted at 7 of 36, and a resolution that means choosing main's superseding text 36 times over.

Ruled: do not rebase. Two grounds, and the first is this project's own.

  1. History is not rewritten. R162 §5 forbade rewriting eight commits because the record must show what happened. Thirty-six commits do not earn an exception to a rule eight could not. Two lines of work diverged and were reconciled; a merge commit says exactly that, and a rebase says something that is not true.
  2. Thirty-six near-identical conflict resolutions is thirty-six chances to get one wrong, to produce a history that claims the divergence never happened.

Measure before choosing the mechanism — this is a property of the repository, not a principle, so it is not mine to guess:

3. CONFLICT POLICY — by class, not by count

  • The twenty registered files, and every registration-record file — main wins, always, without exception. phase1's copies are stale by construction; main carries the tagged lineage.
  • Phase 1's own work — src/leakaudit/, tests/phase1/, pyproject.toml, anything Phase 1 authored — phase1 wins, unless main also changed it, in which case report both sides and HALT.
  • Derived files — the manifest above all — are never conflict-resolved. They are regenerated from their sources after the merge. Hand-merging a derived file produces an attestation that matches nothing, which is why the manifest conflicts at nearly every commit in the rebase shape. Regenerate once, at the end.

4. AFTER THE MERGE — what "clean" means

The pinned gate cannot stay at exactly one finding: main gains files it did not have, and manifest coverage legitimately changes.

Acceptance: the gate reports the known hash_set_single_source finding, plus only findings demonstrably caused by files newly present on main, each named individually. Regenerating the manifest clears the coverage class. Anything else HALTS.

Then both suites, reported as R168 §2 requires:

  • tests/registration — exactly one failure, test_prereg_stage_on_real_repo_exits_zero, from the pinned finding. Any second failure halts.
  • tests/phase1 — must collect and actually run. Report the collected count and the pass count. Exit 0 with zero tests is not a pass and is not to be reported as one.

Confirm the branch-split D10 finding has cleared.

5. THEN — §6.2, its own round

The acceptance run does not start in this turn. The tag timestamps the criteria, so results score against a provably frozen registration — and the scoring apparatus (compute_runtime_metrics, the acceptance machinery, the R9 map as a harness input per SC-7(c), never a tool input) has never run. That is Phase 1's gate and it gets a clean entry with its own report.

After it: README wiring (comparison table, B8/B9 results, net_delta, install instructions) → DESIGN.md Phase 1 section → the D2 subsystem (discriminator + window + relative-root defect, designed together) → D10 fail-loud redesign → R110 register sweep → criterion-5 polish.

Queued — the receipt upgrade. When the Bitcoin attestation lands: ots upgrade or re-fetch → verify it still attests b45b3f52… → re-hash and update its manifest line → commit.

6. HALT LIST

Any rebase, amend, reset or force on either branch · a non-uniform conflict resolution · main's registered files losing to phase1's in any conflict · a derived file being hand-merged instead of regenerated · reporting an empty test collection as a pass · any gate finding after the merge that is not either the known one or demonstrably caused by a newly-present file · starting §6.2 acceptance in this turn · any PREREG.md edit, without exception · anything §10 reserves to the author.

7. REPORT FORMAT

§2's measurement first — ancestry, conflict count, uniformity. Then the merge and its resolutions by class. Then the gate, named finding by finding. Then both suites with their collected counts. Then "what you must rule on" or "nothing to rule on."

The concern R170 raised is confirmed by measurement rather than by argument: phase1 has never contained the tagged state, so any §6.2 acceptance run on that branch would score against a pre-tag registration and forfeit the entire reason for waiting for the tag.

The merge is therefore a prerequisite to §6.2, not a tidy-up before it. The merge commit is the first commit whose ancestry contains both the tag and Phase 1's work, and that is the object acceptance results are scored against.

  4. Gate acceptance: the known hash_set_single_source finding, plus only findings demonstrably caused by files newly present on main, each named individually. Regenerating the manifest clears the coverage class. Anything else HALTS.

R170 §3 said derived files are regenerated, not conflict-resolved. That was right in principle and under-specified in fact: a from-scratch rebuild would discard the 220 comment section headers and the grouped, non-globally-sorted ordering.

Regenerate means: recompute every digest from its file in place, preserving the existing structure, grouping and ../ entries, and append lines for the newly-present files.

Predict, then measure. State the expected line count before regenerating — 730 hash lines plus the newly-present evidence files — and compare to the actual. A silent mis-regeneration is invisible without the prediction.

1. THE __pycache__ CALL — correct, and correctly flagged

R175 §4 ordered the repoint; §7 forbade a second gate finding; importing from inside evidence/ writes bytecode into an attested tree. Two orders in tension, and you found a third path that satisfied both.

It was right, and the test that decides it is R163 §1. Would sys.dont_write_bytecode around imports from an attestation directory have been done anyway, absent any finding? Yes — writing machine-specific build artifacts into an attested tree is undesirable whether or not a check notices.

The decisive distinction, and it is worth stating for the record: an exemption suppresses a check's finding; this prevents the condition the check reports. Nothing was exempted, no file was excluded from scanning, and the check still fires if __pycache__ ever appears — verified under a full suite run, not a single import. The general rule, now written down: when two orders in a delta conflict and a path exists that satisfies both without weakening either, take it and report it prominently. If no such path exists, halt. You did the first; flagging it was right and nothing further is owed.

2. AN UNADDRESSED HALT IS UNRECEIVED — both directions

R175 did not address R173's halt because the halt was past the end of the report I received. The reports reaching the planning layer are a partial view of the turn that produced them; this is H-L31 arriving in a new place.

Two rules, and both are standing from here:

Silence is never resolution. A delta that does not mention a prior halt has not overruled it — it has not seen it. Re-report the halt at the top of the next turn, before any work, exactly as you did. Do not proceed past it on the assumption it was considered and dismissed.

The planning layer never lifts a halt implicitly. If I intend a halt lifted, I say so by name and give the ground. Anything else is an omission on my side.

3. §6.2 PHASE TWO — the pre-commitment, with one addition

The structure stands as R172 §4 set it. One thing is added, and it is the project's own principle applied one level down.

3.1 — Commit before running

Commit, before executing anything: the harness, the exact invocation, the inputs, every criterion with its pass threshold stated numerically, the output paths — and §3.2's expectations.

Freezing the thresholds in the pre-commit is the point. A threshold that is still adjustable when the numbers arrive is not a threshold.

3.2 — State the expectation, per criterion [the addition]

One line per criterion, in the pre-commit, saying what you expect the result to be and why. Not a target. A falsifiable prior.

This is the registration's own method applied to the round: a result that differs from a recorded expectation is impossible to quietly absorb, and a result that matches one you never wrote down is impossible to distinguish from one you rationalised afterwards.

A result differing from its stated expectation is a finding to report — never a reason to adjust the harness, the threshold, the inputs, or the expectation.

3.3 — Run once

One run. stdout, stderr, exit status to files.

3.4 — Commit the output unmodified

Before interpreting any of it. If the harness turns out wrong, that is a finding, it is recorded, the fix is its own commit, and the re-run is a second, separately labelled result with the first still in the record. Do not interpret from a terminal before the output is committed.

3.5 — Then interpret

A result that does not clear a criterion is a result. The registration exists so that outcome can be published rather than engineered away.

Criterion 3 specifically: the corrected fixture genuinely leaks in 18 of 48 instrument-months, so silence is not the target and a zero may not be published as a pass.

4. HALT LIST

Executing any part of the scoring apparatus before §3.1's pre-commit is committed · adjusting a threshold, input, harness or expectation after any result is visible · re-running after a first result without the first in the record · interpreting from a terminal before the output is committed · publishing a zero as a criterion-3 pass · any push flag, or re-pushing / moving / deleting prereg-v30a · any gate finding beyond the known hash_set_single_source · touching check_registration.py this round · any rebase, amend, reset or force · any PREREG.md edit, without exception · anything §10 reserves to the author.

The pre-commit's SHA first, with the criteria, thresholds and stated expectations it contains. Then the run: exit status and the committed output paths. Then the comparison — expectation versus result, criterion by criterion, including every one that missed. Then "what you must rule on" or "nothing to rule on."
