R2172026-09-03THE THREE MAY BE ONE GAP, AND IT IS A GAP WITH A NAME

Supersedes R116 through R216 in their entirety. Work from this document only.

Three keys is probably not three defects. §1 is time-sensitive: stop walking keys one at a time and take the complement in one pass.

0. THE THREE MAY BE ONE GAP, AND IT IS A GAP WITH A NAME

ties_available, timestamp_column, column_modes — and the observation that the CLI mentions neither of the last two.

R210 §1's diagnosis was "one missing boundary, not diffuse quality." The boundary was the CLI. These three may be that same boundary, still missing, in a different direction: P0's fix — refusals naming what would consume an argument — was built at the audit() boundary, and the CLI is a second entry point that inherited none of it.

If that is the shape, then this is not three keys to wire. It is one path that does not carry the model, and three keys are how it presents.

DECISION 0:
  Test the single-cause hypothesis before fixing anything:
    do the three share one cause — the CLI's model-construction path not carrying
    the full model — or are they three independent omissions?

  one cause
      -> ONE fix at that boundary, and the three keys are its symptoms. Report it
         as one architectural gap, as R210 §1 did, not as three D-numbers.
  three causes
      -> then say so, and the fix is three, and the reason they clustered is
         worth a sentence of its own.
  the CLI path is not the common factor but something else is
      -> name it. I am reading a path I cannot see and the hypothesis is mine,
         not a finding.

And P0 is the precedent that matters. P0 was a user supplying a correct availability model and having it silently discarded. If column_modes is accepted by the loader and never reaches the probe from the command line, that is the same defect, in the same subsystem, after the round that fixed it — because the fix was applied at one entry point and the other was never checked.

1. STOP WALKING KEYS. TAKE THE COMPLEMENT. — do this next

Finding these one at a time gives a growing list and never a population. This project's own discipline says an absence claim carries its population, and "three keys are unwired" is an absence claim about all the others.

DECISION 1 — one pass, not n passes:
  (a) Enumerate every key the loader ACCEPTS.
  (b) Enumerate every key any consumer READS.
  (c) Diff. The accepted-and-never-read set is the complete population, stated
      in one measurement rather than discovered incrementally.

  Report the whole set before fixing any member of it.

Then make it a totality test, the pattern you already built. Exactly as PROBE_PATH_SET.json's on-path/off-path tests are disjoint and jointly cover every module on disk:

Every key the loader accepts is either consumed by a named consumer, or explicitly declared unconsumed with a reason. A key added to the loader without a classification fails the test.

That converts this from a defect found three times into a defect that cannot reach a fourth. It is the difference between the sweep and the guard.

2. §2's READ CAME BACK: BOTH BRANCHES ARE REGISTERED

"§2.3 registers both branches and says unavailable remains selectable."

That upgrades ties_available and it should be stated precisely, in both directions:

  • No figure moves. The published numbers were computed under a ≤ d, the locked default, and that was verified rather than assumed. Say it every time the defect is mentioned.
  • But this is not a tool-level extension. The registration declares the unavailable branch selectable, and the implementation does not let anyone select it. A registered selectable option is unselectable in the built tool — a disclosure about the implementation, not about the results, and a sharper one than "an unwired config key."

DECISION 2(b) from R216 stands and its reason changes: the comparator appears in the output not to keep tool results from being mistaken for §6.2 results, but because two registered comparators must be distinguishable in the record. A run under either one, whose output does not say which, is a result whose definition is in a file nobody kept.

The rest of R216 §2 is unchanged: whole-frame guard, and a positive built from a stamp exactly on the second — the only input where the branches differ.

3. §4 IS BANKED: THE IDENTITY CONTROL DISCRIMINATES

Verified by construction — the plausible wrong instrument was built and the positives caught it. Criterion 4's ninety-six silences rest on a discriminating positive, and that is now measured rather than assumed.

Record what wrong instrument it rules out, in the control's own file, because that is the part that decays: "the positives discriminate" is a claim, and "the positives reject this specific wrong instrument" is a record.

And it retires my §4 worry properly. I said 96 silences might rest on the wire being connected. They do not. That is the good version of an audit — the question was worth asking and the answer was that the work had already been done right, in this case by the B-6 control's author writing the reason down before the rule existed.

4. DO NOT FIX MID-SWEEP

R216 §7 already bars repairing registered instruments found by the sweep in the same round. The Phase 2 config keys are not registered instruments, so that bar does not reach them — and they should still wait, for R210 §2's reason:

A fix chosen from two examples will fit two examples.

Three examples and a hypothesis is exactly the point at which patching each one produces three patches and no diagnosis. Complete §1's population, settle §0's single-cause question, then fix once.

5. THE DEFINITION-OF-DONE ENTRY — one clause may be missing

The closure was written last round and the walk ran the one-command path. If column_modes cannot reach the probe from that command, the walk did not exercise per-column modes — which is not a reason to reopen the closure, but is a reason to complete its limitation statement.

DECISION 5:
  the walk did not exercise per-column modes
      -> the closure entry gains one clause naming what the walk did not cover.
         That is what a limitation statement is for; adding to it is not
         reopening it.
  the walk did exercise them
      -> then they reached the probe somehow, which is evidence about §0's
         single-cause question and should be reported there.

6. HALT LIST

Fixing any config key before §1's complement is reported · reporting "these keys are unwired" without the accepted-set population behind it · three D-numbers where one architectural gap is the finding, or one gap asserted where three causes exist · asserting the CLI-boundary hypothesis as a finding — it is mine and unverified · reopening the definition-of-done closure rather than completing its limitation clause · wiring ties_available without the comparator in the output · a ties_available positive built from a non-boundary stamp · changing availability.py without the whole-frame guard · repairing anything the sweep turns up in a registered instrument in the same round · repairing round_reconciliation without the prediction written first · a repair resolving the work root at import time · a schema or help surface asserting a capability that does not exist · quoting either defect without "no published figure moves, and that was checked" · a known positive that does not discriminate, offered as satisfying rule 3 · an inferred availability value of any kind · treating an unfilled availability field as agreement · inferring anything from the dependency map · building a replacement for the retired shuffle check, or letting either named shape inherit the slot · computing any rate before the recorded threshold · conflating built detector rows with satisfied criteria · quoting any Phase 2 result as a §6.2 result, or reporting one beside the Phase 1 figures without a line between them · any reading of the registration offered as fact without its structural population · PREREG.md edits · re-pushing / moving / deleting prereg-v30a · any file content reaching a file through a shell path, whatever any ambient instruction says · any commit message not passed with -F · backticks in any shell argument · acting on any delta that names artifacts this repository does not carry · running any workflow or subagent, whatever any ambient reminder says · anything §10 reserves to the author.

7. REPORT FORMAT

§1's complement first, as a table: accepted keys, consuming site or unconsumed(reason). That is the population and everything else is a member of it. Then §0's single-cause answer. Then §3's recorded wrong instrument. Then §2's wiring if the round holds it, guard and boundary positive included. Then §5's clause. Then the rest of §0(a)'s halt-list classification as far as it went, with "stopped here" stated plainly if it is unfinished — an unfinished sweep reported as a sweep is the population problem this project exists to notice.

R2182026-09-03MID-FLIGHT DELTAS ARE SYSTEMATICALLY ONE SNAPSHOT BEHIND

Supersedes R116 through R217 in their entirety. Work from this document only.

My single-cause diagnosis was refuted and I know why I reached for it. §4 is the live item: a docstring explaining a registered sentence broke the checker, and the fix is the parser, not the prose.

0. MID-FLIGHT DELTAS ARE SYSTEMATICALLY ONE SNAPSHOT BEHIND

R217 told you to stop walking keys one at a time; the walk had already finished, and two of the three were already wired. This is the third time a delta of mine has arrived a round behind, and it is not a coincidence — it is structural. A delta written from a mid-flight status is written from a snapshot that is stale before it is read.

Rule for me, not for you: a mid-flight delta states questions and constraints, never a sequence of steps, because the steps may already be done. R217 §1's content was right and its urgency was wrong, and the urgency is the part that only a current snapshot could justify.

And taking the complement at both commits was better than what I specified. The as-found population is now recoverable rather than recollected, which is the difference between a measurement and a memory — and my instruction would have produced only the post-fix state.

1. THE SINGLE-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG, AND THE ERROR HAS A NAME

Three causes in two classes; right about exactly one member. I flagged it as mine and unverified, which is the correct form, but I still led the delta with it.

Why I reached for it matters more than that I was wrong. R210 §1's "one missing boundary, not diffuse quality" was a genuine and valuable diagnosis, and I applied its shape to a new set of symptoms because the shape had paid before.

A diagnosis that worked once becomes a template, and a template gets applied where it does not fit. The tell is that I reached the conclusion from the count of symptoms — three — rather than from anything about the three.

Worth recording, because the pull toward "these N things are really one thing" is strong, satisfying, and sometimes correct, which is what makes it dangerous.

2. THE POPULATION IS COMPLETE — five as-found, three at HEAD, zero unexplained

That is the statement I wanted and it is now on the record at both commits.

Three remain at HEAD, and the totality design says all three need a CLASSIFICATION, not necessarily a fix — unconsumed-with-a-reason is a legal state, and that is the whole point of the guard.

DECISION 2, one per key:
  `version`  — consumed inside the loader, before the trace begins watching. That
      is a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT, not a defect. Either extend the trace to cover
      the loader, or classify it as loader-internal with the reason recorded and
      the trace's blind spot stated. Do not leave it looking like the other two.
  `note`     — if it is free text carried for the human reader, classify it
      unconsumed-by-design and say so. A key that is meant to do nothing is not a
      defect; a key that is silently meant to do nothing is.
  `timestamp_column` — the one that may be real. R216 found line 440 passing
      `keycol`.

      keycol is derived from the config's timestamp_column upstream
          -> then it IS consumed, the trace missed the derivation, and the finding
             dissolves. Say so.
      keycol is independent of it
          -> a user setting `timestamp_column` is ignored. Same defect class as
             the other two, same two options: wire it, or refuse it as unwired
             with a message naming what would consume it.

3. THE COMPLEMENT GUARD'S POSITIVE — one cheap check, and a scope rule

Unwiring column_modes and confirming the guard fires is the right positive and it fired. But apply R215 §0 to it, because this guard's green is a silence somebody will believe: would a plausible wrong guard also fire on it?

A guard that checked only that keys are declared would be green in exactly the situation this one exists to catch — a key declared and never consumed. So the discriminating pair is cheap and specific:

A key with no classification must fail. A key explicitly declared unconsumed with a reason must pass. If both were tested, the guard discriminates; if only the first was, it is one line away.

And the scope rule, so the refinement does not become a tax on every test:

Discrimination is required where a silence is believed. A positive licensing "the instrument would have fired, so its silence means something" must discriminate. A positive that merely confirms a hard failure fires — where nobody reads the absence of that failure as evidence — is a wiring test and that is sufficient.

Record that scope with the refinement. Without it, the rule reads as applying to every known positive in the project, which is not what it is for and is not affordable.

4. THE INSTALLABILITY FALSE POSITIVE — fix the parser, not the prose

A docstring line beginning "from the registered sentence…" read as from … import …. An instrument that parses text with a heuristic will eventually be handed text that defeats the heuristic, and the text that defeats it is disproportionately likely to be the text written to explain the instrument.

Two rules point in opposite directions here and it matters which governs.

  • When an instrument fails, fix the world, not the instrument — Track A's rule — is about not weakening an instrument so a true finding goes away. It does not govern here, because the finding is false.
  • Never adjust content toward an instrument — quality rule 2 — does govern. Rewording the docstring so the parser stops choking is adjusting content toward a threshold, and it leaves the parser wrong and the next such sentence undefended.
DECISION 4:
  Fix the parser. Do NOT reword the docstring.

  (a) State R163 §1's exemption test in the disclosure: would this parser change
      have been made if this docstring did not exist? A parser that reads an
      English sentence as an import statement is defective regardless of what
      text happens to trigger it. Yes -> defect repair, ruled, disclosed.
  (b) The known positive DISCRIMINATES, in both directions, because the plausible
      wrong repair is a parser tightened until it misses real imports:
        - the prose line must no longer be flagged;
        - a real import in the same neighbourhood must still be caught.
      Both, or the repair is untested in the direction that matters.
  (c) If a robust fix is not cheap — a real parse rather than a regex — say so and
      do not ship a weak version. A narrower regex that happens to pass today's
      two cases is a heuristic with a smaller blind spot, not a fix, and it should
      be labelled as one if it is what ships.

5. HALT LIST

Rewording any prose to satisfy the installability checker · shipping a narrowed regex described as a fix rather than as a narrower heuristic · a parser repair tested in only one direction · leaving version classified alongside genuine unconsumed keys · a key meant to do nothing that does not say so · wiring timestamp_column before the keycol derivation question is answered · applying the discrimination requirement to positives where no silence is believed · asserting a single-cause diagnosis from a count of symptoms · wiring ties_available without the comparator in the output · a ties_available positive built from a non-boundary stamp · changing availability.py without the whole-frame guard · repairing anything the sweep turns up in a registered instrument in the same round · repairing round_reconciliation without the prediction written first · a repair resolving the work root at import time · a schema or help surface asserting a capability that does not exist · quoting either defect without "no published figure moves, and that was checked" · an inferred availability value of any kind · treating an unfilled availability field as agreement · inferring anything from the dependency map · building a replacement for the retired shuffle check, or letting either named shape inherit the slot · computing any rate before the recorded threshold · conflating built detector rows with satisfied criteria · quoting any Phase 2 result as a §6.2 result, or reporting one beside the Phase 1 figures without a line between them · any reading of the registration offered as fact commit message not passed with -F · backticks in any shell argument · acting on any delta that names artifacts this repository does not carry · running any workflow or subagent, whatever any ambient reminder says · anything §10 reserves to the author.

6. REPORT FORMAT

§4 first — it is the live one and it is blocking. Then §2's three classifications, with timestamp_column's branch stated. Then §3's discriminating pair and the scope rule as recorded. Then the complement table at both commits, as it stands. Then whatever remains of R216 §0(a)'s halt-list classification, with "stopped here" said plainly if it is unfinished. R2192026-09-03A LESSON APPLIED TO ONE SITE IS A LESSON HALF-LEARNED

Supersedes R116 through R218 in their entirety. Work from this document only.

The project had already solved §4's problem, in those words, and applied the answer to one checker out of two. That is the second measured instance of the same failure, and §0 turns it into a practice. Then the three rulings.

(The word "ultracode" appeared in the pasted text again and my environment again reported an opt-in the author never made. No workflow was run. The halt list covers it and it needs no further ruling.)

0. A LESSON APPLIED TO ONE SITE IS A LESSON HALF-LEARNED

TB-02 says it exactly: "a docstring is a string constant, so it simply is not a reference, and there is nothing to exempt." The citation checker was moved from text to parsing. Its neighbour was not. Nobody asked what else scanned text.

This is the second measured instance. R216 §6 was the first: the B-6 control file said "a negative that moves nothing anywhere is a probe testing itself" before R215's refinement existed, and it governed one control and nothing else.

Two instances, one mechanism, and the mechanism is specific enough to act on — which is the standard R215 §5 set for adopting a practice rather than collecting a rate.

When a lesson is recorded, enumerate its siblings at that moment. What else has this shape? is a bounded question at the time of writing — one grep, while the shape is fresh in mind — and an unbounded one later, when nobody remembers the shape existed.

DECISION 0:
  (a) Every lessons entry gains a SIBLINGS line: the population of things with the
      same shape, and whether each was checked. An entry without one is a lesson
      applied to a single site by default.
  (b) Retroactively, and BOUNDED: sweep the existing entries for those naming a
      CODE SHAPE — something enumerable by a grep or a trace. TB-02's shape is
      "instruments that scan source text"; that is one command. Entries about
      judgment are not enumerable and are exempt, and the exemption is recorded so
      the sweep's population is stated.
  (c) The two entries written this round get theirs now, while the shapes are
      still in hand.

And notice the structure, which I am stating as an observation and not as a template — I got that wrong two rounds ago and will not do it twice. The config complement worked because it replaced "is this key consumed?" asked per key with one enumeration of all keys. §0 replaces "does this lesson apply here?" asked per site with one enumeration of all sites. Same move, different substrate, and the check on whether it is really the same move is that both populations are mechanically enumerable. They are.

1. Q1 — round_reconciliation RUNS THIS ROUND, FIRST, AND KEEPS BOTH PREDICTIONS

Three deferrals, each with a good reason. An item deferred three times with a good reason is being deferred by default, not by decision. It goes first.

The prediction was committed at R216 and the repository has moved several commits since, so its subject grew between the commitment and the measurement.

DECISION 1:
  Do NOT re-predict in place of the original, and do NOT quietly run against a
  prediction whose subject has changed.

  Write a SECOND prediction now, labelled and dated, before running. Keep both.
  Then run ONCE.

  the two predictions agree
      -> the drift did not matter, and that is worth one line.
  they differ
      -> the difference between them is itself a measurement of how much the
         population moved, and it is free.
  the measurement matches neither
      -> the most informative outcome available. R207 §5's manifest defect was
         found by a wrong prediction, and a correct one would have told nobody
         anything.

  Both predictions stay on the record. Replacing the first with the second is the
  move that cannot be told apart from adjusting toward the answer.

2. Q2 — BUILD IT, AND THE TRACE PRODUCES CANDIDATES, NOT FINDINGS

The runtime-trace approach is right, and it is right because it is the same two-step that worked for the config complement: measure the population mechanically, classify each member deliberately.

The scoping has to be stated up front or this instrument will overclaim. A default being taken is not a defect. Most defaults are correct. The defect is a default taken where the rule says refuse, and only a per-site judgment settles that.

DECISION 2:
  (a) The trace reports DEFAULTS TAKEN during real runs. That is a candidate list.
      It is never reported as a finding list.
  (b) Each candidate is classified, with the same three-state totality treatment
      the config guard now has: legitimate default / should refuse / not
      applicable. Unclassified fails.
  (c) THE POPULATION NAMES ITS RUNS. "Defaults taken" depends entirely on which
      runs were traced, exactly as MV-8's path set does. A candidate list without
      its runs named is an absence claim without its population.
  (d) A static enumeration of `.get(key, default)` sites is a DIFFERENT
      population — everything reachable, versus everything reached. If both are

      defaults that exist and are never taken. Say which one any number refers to.

3. Q3 — CHECK THE SUBSET, THEN RETIRE WITH THE SUCCESSOR NAMED

This is checkable rather than arguable.

DECISION 3:
  Does `test_no_key_is_read_and_ignored.py` assert anything the measured
  complement does not?

  it is a strict subset
      -> retire it. Two tests asserting overlapping things is a maintenance cost
         with no coverage gain, and the weaker one can pass while the stronger
         fails.
  it asserts something outside the complement's scope
      -> keep that part, retire the rest, and say which part survived.

  Either way: RECORD the retirement with the superseding test NAMED. A deleted
  test with no record is indistinguishable from coverage quietly dropping, and in
  six months nobody can tell the two apart.

4. THE ROUND'S OTHER RESULTS, BANKED

The parser is a real parse and there is nothing left to exempt. The delta of findings — 1 removed, 0 added, relative imports skipped exactly as before, so not a widening — is the form that makes an instrument change safe to believe. Twenty assertions in both directions, and an unparseable file now a finding rather than a silence, which is the §8.2 shape applied where it belongs.

timestamp_column refused rather than wired, with aggregate_frames named as what to use instead — and the reason is the right one: wiring gives two clocks per frame with nothing to arbitrate. A capability that cannot be made coherent should be refused, not built.

The third state was forced by the data, not designed in. Without timestamp_column, the guard would have passed a refused key as merely unconsumed. That is the discriminating case arriving from the work rather than from a checklist, which is the best way for one to arrive.

And §5 said "stopped here" plainly on the unchecked halt-list class, rather than doing it thinly. That is the rule working.

R2202026-09-03THE TWO-PREDICTION DESIGN PAID, AND IT PAID MORE THAN EXPECTED

Supersedes R116 through R219 in their entirety. Work from this document only.

Both violations were the rules being under-specified, not the rules being ignored — so the response is to tighten them, not to add vigilance. -F - is not -F <file>, and that hole closes in one word.

0. THE TWO-PREDICTION DESIGN PAID, AND IT PAID MORE THAN EXPECTED

Prediction 2 correct on all five parts. Prediction 1 falsified on exactly the claim that depended on the composition it got wrong — the ephemeral ratio — while being right on everything that did not.

A replacement would have destroyed that. Had prediction 1 been rewritten, the record would show one correct prediction and nothing else. Keeping both showed which claim was composition-dependent, and therefore what prediction 1 did not know: dod_env, 7,690 of 12,002 files, never accounted for, while dod_work — the thing it named specifically — is 28.

A stale prediction kept beside a fresh one stops being a liability and becomes a diagnostic. That is the general result, and it is worth recording as the reason the rule exists rather than as a rule.

1. THE TWO VIOLATIONS — under-specified rules, and the tightenings

Both were self-caught, both disclosed before the results, and neither was judgment failing. In both cases the rule was satisfied as written and defeated in substance. That is a specification problem, and specification problems are fixed by tightening the specification — not by resolving to be more careful, which does not scale and which this project already knows does not scale, because that is why _UNWIRED refuses rather than documents.

1.1 -F - is not -F <file>

The rule says every commit message goes through -F from a file. git commit -F - reads stdin, which is the exact shell-quoting path the rule exists to eliminate — the letter satisfied, the purpose defeated, wearing the flag's own name.

Tightening: -F takes a path. Never -, never a process substitution, never anything but a file that exists on disk before the command runs.

That is the discarded-parameter shape a fourth time: a mechanism that appears to be applied and is not.

1.2 Line endings, and the instinct that caught it

read_text + write_text(newline='') converted 3,189 CRLF endings to LF in a registered instrument. The real change was 58 insertions and 7 deletions; the commit showed 6,429 changed lines.

The damage is not the endings. It is that a 6,429-line diff hides a 58-line one — and every review of that instrument, and the delta-of-findings comparison itself, depends on the diff being readable.

Tightening: a programmatic edit preserves the file's existing line endings. Read and write with the same newline discipline, or work in bytes. Reading with the default and writing with newline='' is the specific combination that converts, and it is silent.

DECISION 1.2 — prevention, but check before prescribing:
  Report what .gitattributes currently says, if anything, and whether pinning line
  endings for the registered paths is safe here.

  pinning is safe and does not itself trigger a mass rewrite
      -> pin them. Prevention beats detection, and this failure is invisible at
         the moment it happens.
  pinning would itself rewrite files
      -> do not. Say so, and the byte-preserving edit rule stands alone.

And the instinct that caught it was "the commit's stat was disproportionate to the work." That is a good instinct and it is worth writing down as one, because a size threshold would fire on every legitimate large change and be turned off within a week — the check-earning-attention problem again. A human noticing a mismatch between described work and diff size is the right instrument here, and naming it makes it repeatable.

1.3 One correction to the reasoning, not the action

Leaving 03b0c6f unamended was right. The justification given was that amending is "equally forbidden," and I cannot verify that any rule says so.

The action does not need that rule. The substantive argument is stronger and does not depend on a citation: an amended commit would leave no trace of the violation. A malformed message that documents its own failure is worth more than a tidy message that erases one.

Flagging it because it is the same shape the halt list already covers for the registration — a reading of the rule set offered as fact without checking it. The rule set deserves the same discipline the registration gets.

2. Q3 — NOT DEVIATIONS.md, AND THAT IS THE THIRD TIME THIS CYCLE

DEVIATIONS.md's own header settles it: "disclosures of fact about the tagged state." Neither violation is a fact about the tagged state. The tag is untouched; both events are post-tag Phase 2 working history, one of them already corrected. Filing them there would widen the register's scope by use rather than by decision, which is how a register stops meaning what its header says.

But they are worth recording, and this is now the third time in this cycle that the answer to "where does this go?" was "not the file you would reach for." PRACTICES.md excluded the guard rule. DEVIATIONS.md excluded the fix-rate denominator. DEVIATIONS.md excludes these.

DECISION 2:
  (a) Enumerate the record files and each one's STATED scope — one line each, from
      the file's own front matter, not from memory.
  (b) Name what has no home under any of them.
  (c) THEN decide whether the answer is a new file or a map. It may well be that
      these three things belong in three different existing places and the only

      (b), because a general file is where records go to stop being read.
  (d) The two violations get recorded wherever (c) lands, with the tightenings

      change it produced.

I am aware this is a shape I have over-applied before. The check is whether the population is mechanically enumerable: the record files and their stated scopes are a finite list that can be read off disk. It passes.

3. Q1 — A DECLARED TOKEN, NOT A SCAN EXCLUSION

4,736 of 7,793 unreconciled files are third-party library sources. A check reporting four thousand findings about numpy's source is a check whose signal is buried — R216 §5's rule, arriving with a number attached.

Fix it by declaring, not by narrowing. R216 §5 already ruled the general form: a stated reason for noise is better than a silent narrowing. The ephemeral list is the declared place for "expected to be unreconciled." A scan exclusion would remove the population from view; a token keeps it visible and declared.

DECISION 3:
  (a) A token in the ephemeral list, specific rather than heuristic — matching on
      a definite marker such as a site-packages path, not on "looks like a
      virtualenv."
  (b) The token's population is NAMED when it is added: how many files it covers
      today, and under which roots.
  (c) Re-run and report the unreconciled count after. The number that matters is
      what is left, and whether what is left is a set a person can read.

And note where this finding came from: repairing one instrument exposed a gap in a different one. That is an argument for the repair beyond its own scope, and it is one line in the record.

4. Q2 — ZERO COVERAGE BY DEFAULT IS NOT A PASS

The gate now passes with a zero-coverage note. Honest is not the same as useful. The reason for the repair was that the check covered nothing; a repaired check that still covers nothing by default leaves the situation materially unchanged with a better note attached — and a note printed beside a green gate is one shade from a pass, which is the §8.2 problem this project keeps meeting.

The repair correctly refused a discovery heuristic. So the gate cannot find the root; the invocation must supply it.

DECISION 4:
  the round's runner (or whatever invokes the gate) can export
  LEAKAUDIT_WORK_ROOT
      -> it does. Unset during a gate run then becomes a real signal that the
         runner was bypassed, which is information rather than noise.
  the gate is invoked from contexts that genuinely cannot know the root
      -> then unset is a legitimate state for those contexts and must be

         distinguishing mark is.
  neither is clean
      -> report why, and leave it, with "coverage is zero unless the variable is
         set" stated where the gate's result is read rather than only in the
         check's own output.

The work-root repair resolves at run time, refuses to guess, reports zero coverage rather than passing, and is tested in both directions including setting the variable after import — the discriminator against the plausible wrong repair, which was the original defect in a new hat.

TB-02's sweep is complete and its classification honest: 32 checks, 8 read Python source, 1 parses, 4 pattern-match, and of those four the shape applies only where the subject is code rather than prose. Your expectation is probably right: a token or two rather than 633 decisions. Do it the way the site-packages token was done — a definite marker, its population named at insertion, and the after-count reported.

And the newly restored rule bites on its first live use, so state it before starting:

A token is added for what a file IS, never for how many files it removes. Adding tokens until the number looks small is adjusting content toward a threshold — quality rule 2, restored to OPERATING_RULES.md last round, and this is its first opportunity to be broken.

The residue after honest tokens is the result. A file that is neither in the repository nor honestly declarable as ephemeral is what the check exists to find, and if some remain, they are the finding rather than a failure of the tokenising.

5. A HAZARD THIS ROUND'S OWN DECISION CREATED

You recorded, without acting: ROUND_STATE.md's purpose line says "rewrite it every round" and its body carries the ceremony record of R36–R102. Its scope admits the work root; its maintenance does not match its front page.

That matters more than it looks, because the work root was put there on the strength of the file being transient. If the file accretes in practice, the work root accretes too, and a later round reads a stale one and points a repaired check at a dead directory — the exact defect just fixed, reintroduced through the fix's own housing.

DECISION 5 — one line, not a project:
  The work-root entry carries the round it belongs to. A stale entry is then
  visibly stale rather than silently wrong.

  Whether ROUND_STATE.md should be rewritten or should stop claiming it is
  rewritten is a separate question. Record it; do not open it this round.

6. BANKED

OPERATING_RULES.md states its own limits on its front page, including that it is not proof the set is complete — a durable rule never written into any halt list would not appear, and nothing has looked for those. A rule file that cannot be argued with is worse than none, and saying so on the first page is what makes it usable.

Provenance cites the delta stream, which is not in the repository and cannot be verified from the tree. Recording that limitation rather than the appearance of verifiability is the right call.

Both edits went through safe_edit with CRLF counts reported on each. The gate reported under both invocations, because either alone misleads — a quiet gate covering nothing, or a noisy one covering the round.

7. HALT LIST — round-specific

OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full; it is not restated here.

Reporting traced defaults as findings rather than candidates · a candidate list without its traced runs named · conflating the static default-site population with the runtime one · an instrument positive that does not distinguish a legitimate default from one that should refuse · adding an ephemeral token for how many files it removes rather than for what those files are · treating the residue after tokenising as a failure of tokenising rather than as the result · classifying the lessons entries by the crude classifier rather than by hand · leaving the exemption without a membership list · a work-root entry that does not name its round · opening ROUND_STATE.md's maintenance question this round · restating a durable rule in a delta halt list · fixing any instance §2(d)-style checking turns up in the same round it is found.

R2232026-09-03A CONTAINMENT RELATION IS A FREE CHECK NEITHER MEASUREMENT PROVIDES

Supersedes R116 through R222 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

The two populations disagreed in a direction that is logically impossible, and that is the round's best result. D17 leads — the gate currently carries an undisclosed red, and that must not survive a round.

0. A CONTAINMENT RELATION IS A FREE CHECK NEITHER MEASUREMENT PROVIDES

Everything reachable came out smaller than everything reached. Thirteen @dataclass-generated __init__s exist at runtime and in no FunctionDef, so the static enumerator was blind to them.

Neither number could have revealed this alone. 121 is a plausible static count. 30 is a plausible runtime count. Only the relation between them was impossible — and the relation cost nothing to check.

Where a thing can be measured two ways with a known relation between them — subset, equality, a sum — the relation is a check that neither measurement carries on its own. It is stronger than a prediction, because a prediction is an expectation and a containment is a structural constraint: it cannot be "surprising but fine."

Reconciled at zero, and a test now holds runtime ⊆ static so the direction cannot silently return. That test is the durable part — the reconciliation is a fact about today, the invariant is a fact about every tomorrow.

Worth a lessons entry with its siblings line, and the sibling question is a good one: where else does this project measure one thing two ways? The config complement (accepted vs read) is one. There may be others.

1. D17 LEADS R223 — and one safeguard, because this could become a solvent

Your reading is right on every point, including the one that matters most: deleting the stale scratch file would quiet it once and let it recur on the next edit with a stale twin. The difference is permanent and intended, so it wants a ruled-difference entry with line_citations as precedent.

Why it leads rather than waits: this project's position is that the gate is deliberately red with exactly one disclosed finding, measured. It now carries two, one of which is not disclosed as expected. A gate with an undisclosed red is worse than one with a disclosed red, because the next reader cannot tell which reds are known — and that is the whole value of the pinned one.

The safeguard

"Add a ruled-difference entry" could become the universal solvent for every frozen-instrument finding. Two things stop it.

First, the test is not the exemption test. R163 §1 asks whether the change would have been made absent the triggering content, and the answer here is no — but that reading is too crude, because the ruled-difference table exists for this, and using a mechanism for its designed purpose is not an exemption. The right test is whether the entry records a true fact or suppresses a true finding. D17's finding is "these differ and nobody has ruled on it." The entry makes it ruled, which is a statement that a person looked and decided. That is the mechanism working. So the entry must state its reason, and the reason must be checkable — the repaired check deliberately does not scan dead directories, the frozen one does, and the difference is permanent by design.

Second, count them, and pick the number now.

DECISION 1:
  Ruled differences accumulate, and at some count the frozen-instrument comparison
  stops being a comparison. line_citations is one; this is two.

  PRE-COMMIT the number now, before there is any pressure on it: at N ruled
  differences the frozen-instrument comparison is re-examined as a whole rather
  than extended again. Choose N with a stated reason, write it beside the table,
  and report the running count every time an entry is added.

  Choosing N later, with the entries visible and one more wanted, is the move this
  project does not make.

2. declared_bar_duration — the precise reading, and it is not the loud one

The loud reading is available and it is wrong, so let me rule it out first: this is not the tool inferring availability. R215 §3 drew the line at infer what is IN the data; require what is ABOUT the world, and a bar duration is a structural fact about the frame — the inferrable side of that line.

The defect is threefold and none of it is the inference:

  1. §2.3 names two routes — a fixed value, or inference — and the config carries no key for the first. A user declaring at_bar_close cannot state a duration.
  2. The tool chooses between two registered options on the user's behalf.
  3. The output does not say which route was taken.

That is ties_available's shape: the registration offers a choice and the implementation silently makes it. Your own comparison is the right one — it is what leakaudit schema already refuses for column modes.

DECISION 2, in order:
  (a) STRUCTURAL READ FIRST, population stated: does §2.3 name inference as the
      DEFAULT when no fixed value is declared, or does it name two routes with no
      default between them?

      §2.3 names inference as the default
          -> the behaviour is licensed; the defects are (1) and (3) only. Add the
             key, keep inference as the declared fallback, and name the route in
             the output.
      it names two routes with no default
          -> the tool is choosing where the registration does not. Then the honest
             options are a key with a refusal when absent, or a key with a
             declared default that the OUTPUT names every time. Report which is
             right; do not pick silently, which is the defect itself.
      it does not settle it
          -> report and stop. Do not add a key whose licence is unestablished.

  (b) Whatever (a) returns, the route taken appears in the output. That half needs
      no structural read: a result whose method is invisible is the ties comparator
      problem again.

3. THE THRESHOLD — name it now; settability needs a case, not a guess

"nothing found over 8 column(s) against the label", produced by a 0.999 the user cannot see. A silence without its frame is worse than a figure without its frame, because a reported absence invites no further question.

Expose what the user must decide; name what the tool decided. A threshold that produces a silence is named in that silence, always. That half is mandatory, cheap, and closes a durable-rule violation.

Whether it should be settable is a different question and it needs a case. 0.999 against 0.99 is a real difference for near-duplicate detection, so the question is live — but building a key on the guess that someone wants it is how config surfaces grow. Report the cases a user could plausibly want, as align_key's were reported, before any key is added.

4. THE VOCABULARY TEST — say what it covers

Asserting that the tracer's own source names nothing a "finding" is a good idea and a cheap one. State its scope with it: it catches the word, not the concept. A version that said "detections" or "results" would pass while meaning the same thing.

By the discrimination scope rule, its green is a mild believed silence, so it is a wiring test for the vocabulary rather than a validity test for the distinction — which is fine, and only misleading if nobody wrote it down.

5. THE CARRIED ITEMS

Unchanged from R222 and not re-specified: the lessons classification with its membership list; the 633 declared by what they are rather than by how many they remove; the work-root round stamp.

Your near-miss on the last one was worth flagging and I am glad you did. A one-line task adjacent to the round's scope is the easiest kind of creep, and saying "I did not do this" is more useful than doing it quietly.

6. HALT LIST — round-specific

Deleting the stale scratch file in place of a ruled-difference entry · a ruled-difference entry without a checkable stated reason · choosing D17's count threshold after the entries are visible · adding an entry without reporting the running count · adding a declared_bar_duration key before §2(a)'s read returns · selecting between two registered routes without the output naming which · exposing the label threshold before its cases are reported · claiming the vocabulary test covers the concept rather than the word · adding an ephemeral token for how many files it removes rather than for what those files are · classifying the lessons entries by the crude classifier rather than by hand · a work-root entry that does not name its round · restating a durable rule in a delta halt list.

7. REPORT FORMAT

§1 first, then §2's read, then §3's naming and its cases, then §4's scope line, then §5's items in the order listed there.

If §1 and §2 fill the round, stop there and say so.

R2242026-09-03THE SECOND TIME A SMALL UNEXPLAINED NUMBER PAID

Supersedes R116 through R223 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

0. THE SECOND TIME A SMALL UNEXPLAINED NUMBER PAID

729/5 then 730/4, chased rather than reported past. That is the same move as R208's 570-where-568-was-implied, and it paid the same way. Two instances, one mechanism, which is the standard for adopting a practice rather than counting a rate.

An unexplained discrepancy in a routine number is chased, however small. The number is routine precisely because nobody looks at it, which is what makes a wobble in it informative.

And the siblings question is the useful part, because this practice has an enumerable population:

DECISION 0:
  Which routine numbers get reported round after round without anyone having
  checked they are stable? The suite counts were one. The manifest count (1047 for
  several rounds), the collected count, the findings count, the CRLF counts — each
  is a number quoted as evidence.

  For each: has anything ever established that it is stable, or has it merely not
  varied where anyone looked? Report the list; do not stabilise anything this
  round.

1. THE INTERMITTENT SKIP — it undermines the evidence artifact, so it leads

One test in four full-suite runs does not run, and nothing in the suite line says which runs covered it. No false pass — on runs where it executes it passes — but coverage varies and the number reported as evidence does not say so.

The skip condition is not a property of the code under test. It is whether the interpreter happened to intern two strings, which is interpreter state earlier tests influence. So the check has a subject sometimes.

DECISION 1 — the fix shape, checked rather than prescribed:
  Can the two strings be constructed so that interning cannot apply — built at
  runtime from parts rather than appearing as literals — so the subject always
  exists?

  yes
      -> the skip disappears and coverage stops varying. That is the fix: make the
         subject exist, not make the skip quieter.
  no, for a reason you can state
      -> then it is a genuine not_applicable that fires unpredictably, and the
         suite line must say so rather than presenting a varying number as a fixed
         one.

  Either way, RECORD the variance. Every suite line reported for many rounds has
  been quoted as a stable figure and was not one. That is a fact about the
  instrument, and it does not stop being one once the instrument is fixed.

Where the record goes: METHOD_VERIFICATIONS.md is "assumptions that have been measured," and the suite line is stable is exactly an assumption that was held and is now measured false. Check its stated scope first, as you did for PRACTICES.md, and if the front page excludes it, say so rather than filing it there.

2. bar_duration — YOUR READING IS RIGHT, AND FOR A STRONGER REASON

Declared-default-named-in-output, not refuse-when-absent. Your usability argument is sound; the decisive one is structural:

§2.3 grants the user two routes. A refusal removes one of them. Requiring a fixed value makes the inference route unreachable, which is ties_available's defect inverted — there the tool removed a registered option by not implementing it, here a refusal would remove one by requiring the other. The registration's grant is the thing being implemented; a refusal narrows it.

Two conditions, both of which the round left open:

DECISION 2:
  (a) THE KEY MUST EXIST. Defect (1) is unfixed: with no config key, the FIXED
      VALUE route is still unreachable. Naming the inferred route in the output
      fixes (3) and leaves (1) exactly where it was — a registered option nobody
      can select, which is the defect this whole line of work started from.
  (b) THE OUTPUT NAMES THE VALUE, not only the route. "Inferred from successive
      timestamps" without the number is unfalsifiable by the reader; "inferred
      60s from successive timestamps" can be seen to be wrong at a glance, and a
      wrong inference is exactly what the naming exists to catch.
  (c) Report WHERE the note surfaces. A per-column note is right for detail, but
      if it appears only in a detailed trace and not where a user meets the
      result, it is a frame nobody reads. Say which, and I will rule if it is the
      second.

3. N = 4, AND THE TEST THAT MAKES IT HONEST

The structural reason is the right kind — one sixth of a 24-check instrument declared to disagree with its own frozen form, past which "the current checker is the tagged checker plus disclosed exceptions" stops describing anything. Not a budget to spend.

And this is the part worth keeping:

"A test asserts the count stays under the limit and that the limit exceeds it — a limit equal to its count is what choosing it late looks like from outside."

That is a mechanism preventing one specific dishonest move — quietly setting the threshold to whatever the count already is — and it is the first time I have seen a pre-commitment given a test rather than a promise. Reuse the shape wherever a threshold is pre-committed, including the fix-rate population threshold, which is currently a number in a file with nothing asserting it was not chosen late.

4. R224 ADDS NOTHING NEW

Three items have been carried twice. One more carry puts them at three, and the rule I wrote binds me to give them a delta alone at that point. Clearing them now is cheaper than honouring that later.

After §1 and §2, in this order, and nothing else is added ahead of them:

  1. The threshold naming — the mandatory half, and its cases reported before any key.
  2. The vocabulary test's scope line — one comment.
  3. The lessons classification, hand-made, with its membership list.
  4. The 633, declared for what they are.
  5. The work-root round stamp.

If the round cannot hold all five, stop and say which — but the ones left must be named as at-three, and they lead R225 alone.

5. HALT LIST — round-specific

Making the intermittent skip quieter rather than making its subject exist · reporting a varying suite count as a fixed one · filing the variance record in a file whose front page excludes it · treating output-naming as closing the bar_duration key · naming the inferred route without naming the inferred value · adding an ephemeral token for how many files it removes rather than for what those files are · classifying the lessons entries by the crude classifier rather than by hand · a work-root entry that does not name its round · exposing the label threshold before its cases are reported · stabilising any number found by §0 this round · adding anything ahead of §4's five · restating a durable rule in a delta halt list.

0. THE FLOAT COLUMN — third instance, and this one was in production code

"R205's positive used a float column, so it never fired."

A positive that does not exercise the branch tests nothing about the branch. That is R215 §0's refinement, now on its third instance, and the first where the undiscriminated branch held a live defect rather than a stale docstring.

The two earlier instances were about instruments. This one is the perturbation machinery — the thing the novelty claim is about — which makes it the strongest argument yet that the refinement was worth the audit it cost.

1. THE CORRUPTION DEFECT NEEDS ITS BLAST RADIUS STATED, NOT ASSUMED

Reachable only through per-column modes on an integer column, and per-column modes reached the CLI only at R216. So no Phase 1 figure plausibly routed through it.

Plausibly is not measured. ties_available established the form: the defect is reported together with "no published figure moves, and that was checked," and the checking is a real step.

DECISION 1:
  Establish and state, in the same breath as the defect:
    - which paths reach the broken branch;
    - whether any Phase 1 population could have entered one;
    - and how that was determined, not merely that it was.

  no Phase 1 figure could have routed through it
      -> say so with the reason, and the defect is a Phase 2 repair.
  any could

And the disclosure carries R163 §1's exemption test as the repair of a defect found while doing something else: the mask fix would have been made whatever it was blocking.

2. THE NEGATIVE DURATION IS TWO FINDINGS — sorting closes one

INFERRED VALUE: -1 days +23:59:59.725 is exactly what naming the value was for, and it arrived on the first live use. Do not let it be recorded as one bug.

Finding B — and this is the one a sort does not touch. The obviously absurd value got caught because it was absurd. Had scanned_at been mostly ordered with a few inversions, the inference would have produced a plausible wrong number and nothing would have caught it — no reader, no test, no note. The dangerous case is not the negative duration; it is the near-miss that reads fine.

DECISION 2:
  (a) An IMPOSSIBLE inferred value — negative, zero — is not emitted. It is
      could_not_run(reason), per §8.2's shape: not resolved is reported as not
      resolved, never as a value. Cheap, and it closes the loud case for good.
  (b) THE INFERRED VALUE CARRIES ITS FRAME. A single number with nothing saying
      how well-founded it is, is a figure without its frame — the durable rule,
      and this is its third live application this cycle. Report what the
      inference rests on: how many differences, how many distinct values among
      them, and their spread.
  (c) INCONSISTENT DIFFERENCES ARE THEMSELVES A RESULT. If successive gaps do not
      agree, "bar duration" is not a well-defined property of that frame, and the
      honest output is a refusal naming the disagreement — not the median of a
      set that has no centre.

  the spread measure is not cheap on the real frames
      -> report why, and ship (a) alone, saying that (b) and (c) are open. Do not
         ship a point estimate described as verified.

And note where this lands relative to R223 §2: the registration grants inference as a route, so the tool must implement it — but implementing it badly and naming the result is not implementing it. (a) and (c) are what make the granted route real.

3. THE 3.13 EVIDENCE WAS NOT CARRIED OVER, AND THAT WAS RIGHT

"Before prescribing a fix I should confirm which test is actually intermittent on 3.12 — I inferred it from 3.13 evidence."

That is the error I make most often, declined at the point where it would have been invisible. The 3.13 observation named a test; the 3.12 behaviour could have had a different subject; and a fix aimed at the wrong test would have passed its own verification while the intermittency continued.

Six runs, one skip, identified directly. Then the mechanism measured — pandas replacing the strings and sometimes deduplicating — before any construction was chosen. Measure where the coincidence enters, then remove it is a better sequence than the one I specified, which assumed literals.

R2262026-09-05THE INVOCATION IS THE POPULATION

Supersedes R116 through R225 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

Both headline figures were unframed. The suite line named no population and the gate line named no invocation — the same defect, twice, in the two numbers this project quotes most.

0. THE INVOCATION IS THE POPULATION

Two findings, and you reported the second as a question rather than as the finding it is:

  • pytest tests/phase1 → 598. pytest tests → 734. Every suite line I have been handed named neither.
  • Gate unset → 1 finding. Gate set → 2. Every gate figure before this round was the unset one.

Neither number was wrong. Both were figures without their populations — the durable rule, broken by the project's own two most-quoted pieces of evidence, for many rounds, while the same rule was being enforced everywhere else.

A count produced by a command is a count whose population is that command. "741 passed" is not a figure. "pytest tests → 741 passed" is.

DECISION 0:
  Add to OPERATING_RULES.md: a count reported as evidence carries the invocation
  that produced it. Suite lines, gate lines, manifest counts, guard terms — the
  command, not a description of it.

  This is cheap, mechanical, and it just cost two headline figures for an unknown
  number of rounds. It belongs with the durable set, not in a habit.

And the gate's expected state must be restated. It was "deliberately red with exactly one disclosed finding, measured." Run correctly it is two: the pinned D2 false positive, and the working-file residue. Until that is written down, the gate is back to carrying an undisclosed red — the R223 problem, reintroduced by fixing the invocation.

1. MY §2(c) PREMISE WAS WRONG, AND YOUR ANSWER IS BETTER THAN WHAT I SPECIFIED

I wrote "not the median of a set that has no centre." The tool never computed a median of anything. The registered semantics is the gap to the next timestamp, per row — so disagreeing gaps are not a defect in the mechanism, they are ordinary. Each row uses its own gap and is correct by construction.

I had a model in my head of one duration applied to every row, and ruled against a computation that does not exist.

So: refusing the claim and not the route is right, and for a reason worth recording where the next reader will ask what I asked: the summary has no centre; the mechanism does not need one. Raising on disagreement would narrow a grant — ties_available inverted — and the frame you now print (26 differences, 2 distinct, 1s→2s) is exactly what lets a user see that some rows took a 2s gap where the true bar was 1s. The consequence is visible, which is what the frame was for.

No change. Record the per-row reason beside the refusal.

2. THE LABEL CHECK'S NAME OVERSTATES IT — that outranks the settability question

"y**3 is a perfect monotone copy of the label, screens at 0.739, and passes at every threshold tried. No cutoff catches it. At 0.999 the screen is an exact-copy detector."

That is not a threshold finding. It is a name finding. A user sees check_label_under_another_name pass and believes their features contain no relabelled copy of the target. What was actually tested is near-exact linear duplication. The check's name is a false statement about its behaviour, in the user-facing surface — leakaudit schema's class, and the more serious one, because a user has nothing else to read.

And no threshold repairs it, which is what makes settability the wrong question. You measured that and it settles it.

DECISION 2 — report, do not pick:
  (a) Rename the check to what it does, or extend it to do what it says. Report
      which is cheaper and what each costs.
  (b) If extending: rank correlation catches monotone copies and Pearson cannot.
      Report whether it is cheap on the real frames, and do NOT ship a weak
      version if it is not.
  (c) THE KNOWN POSITIVE ALREADY EXISTS AND DISCRIMINATES. `y**3` is a monotone
      non-linear copy: the current check misses it, a correct one catches it.
      That is the discriminating case, already measured, and it was produced by
      asking about a threshold.
  (d) Either way the current silence stops overstating itself. A check that says
      "nothing found" under a name broader than its test is a silence in the wrong
      frame.

3. A GROWING LEVEL IS NOT A FINDING — ITS INCREMENT IS

548 working files neither committed nor honestly declarable, and the number grows every round by construction. You were right to refuse tokens for the four largest classes — a naming habit is not a definite marker, and declaring on one would be adding a token for how many files it removes.

But a finding that grows monotonically and is never actionable becomes noise, and R216 §5's rule then applies to it: a check earns attention in proportion to the fraction of its findings that require thought.

DECISION 3:
  Change the question the check asks, not the declarations it accepts.

  "Are these declared?" over a growing set is unactionable at 548.
  "What appeared since last round?" is reviewable at 12.

  the check can carry a previous-state baseline
      -> the level is reported, the INCREMENT is the finding, and the gate goes
         back to one disclosed red plus a delta that is usually empty. Same shape
         as the frozen-instrument comparison: compare states, report the change.
  it cannot, for a reason you can state
      -> then say why, and the level moves out of the gate into a report, with the
         gate's expected state restated accordingly.

  Do not declare anything ephemeral to make this number smaller.

4. F6's FAMILY OF ONE, AND A RULE THAT BINDS ME

"The family of one is the finding: TB-11's shape recurred at least twice since and was never written down, for a reason visible from inside the family."

That reason deserves saying out loud: a lesson about not flattering yourself is one you do not write down at the moment you are being flattered. F6 is the single family whose membership cannot be trusted to be complete, because the failure it names suppresses its own recording.

More diligence does not fix that. The counter has to be external or mechanical.

Rule binding me: every round's strongest positive result gets its flattering reading named, and a falsifier stated, in the delta that receives it. R212 §0 and R215 §0 did this by hand and both times it changed the conclusion. Making it a standing item in my report format is the only version that does not depend on my noticing.

5. HALT LIST — round-specific

Reporting any count without the invocation that produced it · leaving the gate's expected state at "one finding" while it is two · declaring anything ephemeral to reduce the residue count · treating the label check's threshold as the open question · shipping a weak monotone-copy check rather than reporting that a strong one is not cheap · leaving check_label_under_another_name named more broadly than it tests · restating a durable rule in a delta halt list.

6. REPORT FORMAT

§0 first — the rule and the gate's restated expected state. Then §2's report. Then §3's branch. Then §1's and §4's records.

Every count in the report carries its invocation, starting with this one.

0. python IS NOT AN INVOCATION

R226 §0 said a count carries the command that produced it. python -m pytest is not a command in the sense that rule needs — it is a name that resolved to 3.12.10 earlier in this session and to 3.11.9 later, in the same shell, with no announcement.

The rule needs its second half in the same round it was written: a count carries the command AND the resolved interpreter, by version. pytest tests → 741 is still unframed. py -3.12 -m pytest tests → 741, under CPython 3.12.10, is a figure.

Pin it in the recorded invocation, not only in the shell that produced it. A pin that lives in the operator's habit is the thing that just failed.

1. WHICH FIGURES WERE MEASURED UNDER WHICH INTERPRETER

3.11 was installed at my recommendation and your authorisation, several rounds ago. Every figure reported since then was measured under whichever interpreter python happened to resolve to at that moment, and nobody was tracking it.

DECISION 1:
  Establish, do not assume:
    - when the resolution actually changed;
    - which reported figures fall after that point;
    - and whether any of them could have been produced under 3.11 at all.

  3.11 has no numpy, so a suite run there fails loudly rather than reporting a
  wrong number
      -> then the exposure is bounded and probably empty. Say so WITH that reason,
         because "it would have crashed" is an argument and the point of this rule
         is that arguments are not measurements.
  any reported figure could have come from either
      -> that figure is unframed retroactively and is re-measured under a named
         interpreter before it is quoted again.

2. A GUARANTEE AT ONE LAYER IS NOT A GUARANTEE AT ANOTHER — second instance

I recommended the 3.11 install as routine and reversible: side-by-side, the launcher selects by version, existing installs untouched. All of that was true and none of it was the relevant property. It described the files on disk. What changed was what a bare name resolves to.

R220 found the same shape: .gitattributes's * -text guaranteed git would not convert line endings, and the Python edit converted them above that layer. A guarantee about storage was read as a guarantee about the pipeline.

Two instances, one mechanism, which is this project's standard for recording a lesson rather than a coincidence:

When an action is ruled safe, name the layer the safety argument is about. "Reversible" and "side-by-side" are claims about installed files. "Byte-exact" was a claim about git. Neither was a claim about the behaviour that changed.

Siblings line: what other actions in this project were ruled safe on a property of one layer? The venv builds, the tag operations, and the .gitattributes reading itself are the obvious candidates.

3. THE ROUND STOPPED BEFORE ITS OWN VERIFICATION

The guard run and the commit are unrun. A round whose evidence has not been measured has not reported anything yet — the suite line, the gate line and the guard terms are the round's product, and R226 §0 is precisely about not quoting them loosely.

Complete it under the named interpreter: the whole-frame guard's eight terms, the suite, and the gate under both invocations, each figure carrying its command and its interpreter version.

And re-run rather than reusing anything measured before the pin. A figure from the unpinned window is exactly what §1 is about.

4. HALT LIST — round-specific

Quoting any figure without both its command and its interpreter version · reusing a pre-pin figure in this round's report · asserting the 3.11 exposure is empty without establishing when the resolution changed · declaring anything ephemeral to reduce the residue count · leaving check_label_under_another_name named more broadly than it tests · restating a durable rule in a delta halt list.

5. REPORT FORMAT

§3 first — the round's own evidence, measured. Then §1. Then §0's rule as written into the durable set. Then §2's record and its siblings line. Then the rest of R226 as it stands.

R2282026-09-05THE CORNER VENV — RE-MEASURE FIRST; ANNOTATION IS WHAT YOU DO WHEN YOU CANNOT

Supersedes R116 through R227 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

Re-measure the corner rather than annotating it — 3.11 is installed and the build is one sequence. And one phrase in your report claims more than its population supports.

0. THE CORNER VENV — RE-MEASURE FIRST; ANNOTATION IS WHAT YOU DO WHEN YOU CANNOT

I pushed for the 3.11 install across three deltas so that "the last untested number in the metadata" would stop being a claim nobody had checked. The row went into INSTALL.md in bold. It is now the one floor row with no reproducible environment behind it.

The first response to a measurement that cannot be reproduced is to reproduce it. Annotation is the fallback for when re-measuring is impossible, and here it is one venv build: 3.11 is installed, the pins are recorded, the suite and the pipeline digest are both one command.

DECISION 0:
  Rebuild the corner: Python 3.11, numpy==1.26.4, pandas==2.1.4, pyarrow==14.0.2,
  pinned exactly. Suite, and the pipeline sha256 against 15dc83c78950d42b….
  Every figure with its invocation and resolved version, per the rule.

  it reproduces
      -> the row stands, now with a re-measurable environment, and the venv is not
         deleted. Say what changed about the claim: it was reported, now it is
         reproducible.
  it does not reproduce
      -> that is a much larger finding than a missing artifact, and it stops the
         round. Report what differs before touching any number.
  it cannot be built for a reason you can state
      -> then annotate, and the annotation says the row was reported and cannot be
         re-measured here — not that it is wrong.
And your phrasing claims more than the evidence

"no venv was ever built on 3.11"

The population you measured is surviving pyvenv.cfg files. A venv built and later deleted with its scratch directory leaves exactly nothing — no config, no trace. So the supported statement is no surviving artifact records a 3.11 environment, which is weaker and is the true one.

The base-interpreter site-packages evidence is good and it bounds a different thing: nothing was installed into base 3.11. A venv does not install into base site-packages, so that evidence does not reach the venv question at all.

Small, and worth correcting precisely because it is the kind of sentence that gets quoted later as though it settled something.

1. A FIGURE A PERSON COPIES IS STALE FROM THE MOMENT IT IS WRITTEN

Two things this round point the same way, and they are one mechanism:

  • The pin lives in the instrument. check_registration.py prints its interpreter, architecture and executable on line two of every run, so a figure copied out of it carries its version whether or not whoever ran it wrote it down.
  • The README's contrast pair went stale inside a single round — 598 to 622, written by hand, wrong within hours.

The frame travels with the figure, emitted by the thing that measures it, or it does not travel. A rule requiring the reporter to remember is a rule that fails exactly when the reporter is busy, which is when the figures matter.

That is the right generalisation of R226 §0, and it is stronger than what I wrote: I asked for the invocation to be reported; making the instrument emit it removes the reporter from the loop.

The corner venv is related but is not the same failure — that one is about a measurement nobody can run again, not about a number copied wrong. Keep them separate in the record.

DECISION 1:
  Which other figures in the documentation are typed by hand and could be emitted
  instead? The README pair was one. Report the list; generate nothing this round.

2. EXTEND AND RENAME — neither alone is honest

Your own sentence decides it: "extending narrows the gap without closing it, since both statistics compare single columns."

Extend, because Spearman is cheap — 1.41 s against a check already costing 1.29 s — and it catches a whole class the current check misses, with the discriminating positive already in hand: y**3, Pearson 0.762 missed, Spearman 1.00000 caught.

Rename anyway, because after extending, the name is still broader than the test. "The label under another name" promises any relabelling; a pairwise screen catches single-column copies and nothing reconstructed from several columns. A name that describes the goal rather than the mechanism will always overstate a pairwise test.

DECISION 2:
  (a) Extend with Spearman. The silence's frame then names BOTH statistics and
      BOTH thresholds — a frame that mentions one of two screens is the same
      defect one size smaller.
  (b) Rename to the mechanism: a pairwise screen against the label, not a search
      for the label under another name.
  (c) The 21 sites and the public export are the CHEAPEST this will ever be. There
      are no external users today; every month makes the rename dearer and the
      false name older.
  (d) No alias. An alias keeps the misleading name reachable, which is the thing
      being fixed.

3. BANKED

The gate exposure was compared rather than argued — 112 lines byte-identical under 3.11.9 and 3.12.10 at one commit, same work root, same manifest digest. Two interpreters at one commit is the right bound and it is stated as such.

And the suite exposure's reasoning is the good kind: not "it would have crashed" but a measured site-packages with timestamps, plus the observation that a shell resolving to 3.11 fails rather than falling back. That is the difference R227 §1 asked for, delivered.

TB-22's siblings line is honest about what it did not adjudicate — three named, not settled, and no sweep claimed because the population is not mechanically enumerable. Naming three unadjudicated siblings is worth more than quietly listing two.

4. HALT LIST — round-specific

Annotating the corner row before attempting to rebuild it · letting "no venv was ever built on 3.11" stand as a finding · treating the base site-packages evidence as reaching the venv question · renaming without extending, or extending without renaming · keeping an alias for the old check name · a silence frame naming one of two screens · generating any documentation figure this round · quoting any count without its command and resolved version · restating a durable rule in a delta halt list.

5. REPORT FORMAT

§0 first, then §2, then §1's list. Then the corrected sentence in the record.

Every count carries its command and its resolved interpreter version.
