15dc83c7… was quoted as the portability evidence in about fifteen deltas and cannot be regenerated by anyone. The claim survives; the number does not. And the floor had no guard while the probe had one.

0. A DIGEST WITHOUT ITS RECIPE IS NOT EVIDENCE

Sixteen conventions over five stored bodies, none producing 15dc83c7. All five bodies hash identically to each other under every convention — so the artifacts agree and the recipe is gone.

Separate the two things, because only one of them is damaged:

  • The portability claim stands, and is now stronger. ddb133ff2fc959f0… reproduces byte-for-byte across CPython 3.11.9 with the declared floors and 3.12.10 with the latest resolution. That spans a Python minor and the full dependency range, which 15dc83c7 never did.
  • The published digest is retired. It cannot be checked by anyone, including us. A number nobody can regenerate is not evidence — and a bare hash is the most authoritative-looking unframed figure there is, which is why it survived fifteen quotations unchallenged.
DECISION 0:
  (a) Retire 15dc83c7… wherever it is quoted, replacing it with ddb133ff… and the
      two environments it was measured in.
  (b) RECORD THE RECIPE beside the new digest: what is hashed, in what encoding,
      with what line endings, including or excluding which banner, from which
      offset. The recipe is the difference between a digest and a decoration.
  (c) Say why the old one was retired — not that it was wrong, but that it cannot
      be reproduced, and that the code has since changed by one line. Both are
      true and the second alone would be a softer story than the facts support.
  (d) Add to the durable set: a digest is quoted as evidence only where the recipe
      that produces it is recorded with it.

1. THE PROBE HAS A GUARD. THE FLOOR HAD NONE.

The corner was measured at a023011 and was correct when written — you established that from the tree rather than assuming it. Sixty-three minutes later watch() moved to sys.monitoring, and nothing re-measured the floor.

That is exactly what the whole-frame guard exists to prevent, in a domain that has no equivalent. A change to a module on the probe's path re-runs the guard. A change that breaks the declared floor interpreter runs into nothing at all.

And the deeper fault is the one §1 of R228 named: the floor row is a hand-typed number in INSTALL.md. A measured fact about one commit, written as a standing fact about the package, with nothing connecting it to the tree it was measured from.

DECISION 1:
  The corner venv now EXISTS and is kept, so the floor's suite is one command. The
  fix is not a rule asking someone to remember.

  (a) The floor figures are EMITTED by a run, not typed. Same lesson as the pin in
      check_registration.py: the frame travels with the figure or it does not
      travel.
  (b) Report what triggering it costs — the corner suite's wall-clock — before
      choosing a cadence. A guard nobody will wait for is a guard that gets
      skipped.
  (c) The floor row becomes the most important member of R228 §1's hand-typed
      figure list, which is carried and still owed.

2. DO NOT RAISE requires-python. GATE IT.

Your bound settles this and it is the sharpest thing in the report: tools/ is not distributed. packages = ["leakaudit", "protocol"], the package imports on 3.11, 755 tests pass, the pipeline agrees.

Raising requires-python to >=3.12 would narrow a published claim about the package to accommodate a repository instrument that is not in the package. It would make the tool unavailable to 3.11 users for a reason that has nothing to do with the tool — a number changed to dispose of a problem.

That leaves gate or fallback.

DECISION 2:
  (a) GATE watch() on 3.12+, and the guard's tests report UNSUPPORTED on 3.11 —
      §8.2's vocabulary, the treatment the cost-deferred tests already have. Not a
      failure: the instrument does not run there and says so.
  (b) THE FALLBACK ONLY IF MEASURED USABLE. R211 measured sys.setprofile giving no
      answer in fifteen minutes on the fixture build — but that was a different
      workload from watch()'s, and I am not going to assert it carries over.
      Measure it on watch()'s actual workload.

      usable
          -> a fallback is better than a gate, because the instrument then covers
             the floor it is meant to protect.
      not usable
          -> gate, and say the fallback was measured and rejected with its number.
             A fallback that hangs is coverage on paper.
  (c) The floor's suite figure is then restated as N passed with M unsupported,
      with its invocation and interpreter — not as the old bare 632.

3. THE SWEEP — bounded by totality, as the others were

"Other tools are unexamined, not confirmed clean" is the correct phrasing and it is an absence claim waiting to be made wrongly.

The 3.11 suite run already swept everything the suite exercises. What it does not reach is tools/ entries the suite never touches.

DECISION 3:
  Enumerate tools/. Each entry is either exercised by the corner suite run
  (covered, and say by which test) or not (unexamined, and say so). Disjoint and
  covering, held by a test, as the config complement and the lessons families are.

  Then "the tools are clean on the floor" is either a statement with a population

4. SEARCH FOR WHAT IT PRODUCED, NOT ONLY FOR WHAT IT WAS

dod_work/py311_out.txt, two minutes after the installer finished, carrying all four versions. The environment recorded itself in its output while its configuration was deleted with the directory.

"The search population was wrong, not merely narrow: it looked for the environment's configuration and not for what the environment produced."

That is the better statement of R228 §0's correction, and it is a general one: configuration is transient and output is committed, so a search for evidence that something existed should look at what it emitted first. Worth a lessons entry with its siblings line — and the sibling question is whether any other "no artifact records this" conclusion in the project was reached by searching only for configuration.

5. HALT LIST — round-specific

Quoting 15dc83c7… as current evidence · recording a digest without its recipe · raising requires-python to accommodate a non-distributed tool · reporting the guard's 3.11 state as a failure rather than as unsupported · restoring the setprofile fallback without measuring it on watch()'s workload · claiming the tools are clean on the floor without the enumeration · leaving the floor figures hand-typed once the corner venv exists · quoting any count without its command and resolved version · restating a durable rule in a delta halt list.

6. REPORT FORMAT

§2 first, then §0, then §3, then §1, then §4. Then R228's two carried items — extend-and-rename, and the hand-typed-figure list — in that order.

R2302026-09-05A BENCHMARK WHOSE BASELINE DOES NOT MOVE IS MEASURING NOTHING

Supersedes R116 through R229 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

Constraints only — written mid-round. The important one is §1: say what "usable" means before the number lands, not after.

0. A BENCHMARK WHOSE BASELINE DOES NOT MOVE IS MEASURING NOTHING

Two synthetic attempts, and the first inverted the real answer — fixed costs dominated and the cheap instrument looked expensive. You caught it because the baseline stayed at 0.05 s, which is the tell: if the instrumented and uninstrumented runs cost the same, the instrument's cost is not in the measurement at all.

A synthetic benchmark that cannot reach the real workload's scale can return the opposite answer and look fine doing it. The check is a relation the numbers must satisfy before any of them is believed — here, that the baseline moves.

Same family as R223 §0: reachable smaller than reached was impossible, and the impossibility was the finding. A relation the measurement must obey costs nothing and catches what the numbers alone cannot.

And the resolution was right: stop proxying and measure the real thing. A proxy that cannot be shown to reproduce the real scale is not cheaper — it is free and wrong.

1. STATE THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION BEFORE READING THE NUMBER

The setprofile measurement is in flight and it decides gate-versus-fallback. If "usable" is defined after the number arrives, it will be defined by the number.

DECISION 1 — before the measurement is read:
  Write down what makes a fallback usable, with a reason, and commit it.

  The anchor already exists: R211 accepted the guard at "seven minutes against a
  comparison point that is current," and R227 measured 266 s and 265 s per side.
  So the question is a MULTIPLE of that, and the criterion is not about
  milliseconds — it is about the cost at which the guard stops being run at all.

  A guard that gets skipped protects nothing, so a fallback that makes it skippable
  is worse than a gate that says plainly it does not run on 3.11.

  Then use the shape you invented for N = 4: assert BOTH that the measured cost is
  under the limit AND that the limit exceeds the measurement. A limit equal to its
  measurement is what choosing it late looks like from outside.

And if the fallback is rejected, the report carries its number, not just the verdict — R229 §2(b) asked for that and it is the half that makes the rejection checkable.

2. THE DIGEST INSTRUMENT'S DATA — the same lesson, one level down, unprompted

"The digest instrument needs its data committed to the repo rather than living in scratch."

That is the corner venv all over again and you saw it before it happened. An emitted digest whose inputs live in a scratch directory is reproducible exactly until that directory is cleaned — which is precisely how 15dc83c7 became unverifiable.

The instrument reproducing ddb133ff… from the repository alone is what makes it evidence rather than a record of something that once ran here. That property is the point of the whole exercise, and it should be stated in the instrument's own output: this digest is reproducible from the repository at this commit.

3. HALT LIST — round-specific

Defining "usable" after reading the setprofile number · reporting the fallback verdict without its measured cost · a limit set equal to the measurement it bounds · believing any benchmark whose baseline did not move · a digest instrument whose inputs are not in the repository · quoting 15dc83c7… as current evidence · quoting any count without its command and resolved version · restating a durable rule in a delta halt list.

4. REPORT FORMAT

§1's criterion, quoted as written before the measurement, then the measurement, then the gate-or-fallback decision. Then the rest of R229 in its stated order, then R228's two carried items.

R2312026-09-05A PRE-COMMITMENT IS A STEP, NOT A CONSTRAINT

Supersedes R116 through R230 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

A pre-commitment cannot be issued mid-round — that is my error, not a discipline failure of yours. I also put the decision on the wrong axis. And extend-and-rename leads this delta by the rule I wrote to bind myself.

0. A PRE-COMMITMENT IS A STEP, NOT A CONSTRAINT

R218 §0 established that a mid-flight delta states constraints and never sequences of steps, because the steps may already be done. R230 §1 broke that rule while looking like it obeyed it.

A pre-commitment is the one instruction whose entire content is its timing. "Decide this before you see the number" is not a constraint that can arrive late — arriving late destroys it.

Refusing to present the criterion as pre-committed was right, and the test asserting that the document still says it was written after is the part worth keeping: it is the N=4 shape again, a mechanism stopping one specific future misreading rather than a note asking a reader to be careful.

Rule for me: pre-commitments go only in deltas that arrive before the work. If I have missed the window, the honest instruction is "state it now, marked after-the-fact, and say whether it would have changed anything" — which is exactly what you did without being told.

1. AND I PUT THE DECISION ON THE WRONG AXIS

I framed gate-versus-fallback as turning on cost, and asked for a cost criterion. It did not turn on cost at all. The fallback passed the cost bar and was rejected for recording 2 modules where sys.monitoring records 4 — a false negative in the one direction a staleness guard exists to prevent, with no threshold in it anywhere.

That is R226 §2(c) again: I ruled on a decision before establishing what it actually turns on. Twice now, and both times the specification was confident and aimed at a mechanism I had not looked at.

And your note is the consequence: "had the report said only 'rejected', a reader would have assumed cost and been wrong" — the delta had primed the wrong reason, so the right one had to be said out loud.

2. THE KILLED-RUN FINDING IS MINE, AND IT NEEDS A SWEEP

"'No answer in fifteen minutes' and 'over thirty-four minutes' are lower bounds that were carried as costs. Completed: ×1.8."

I quoted the fifteen-minute figure in R227 as a measurement of setprofile's cost. It was a lower bound on a run somebody stopped. The real ratio is 1.8, comfortably inside the acceptable range — so the original decision to abandon setprofile rested on a non-measurement, and was right for a reason nobody had found yet.

A killed run licenses "at least N" and nothing more. These licensed "prohibitive," across four rounds, in a project whose central discipline is that figures carry their populations.

DECISION 2:
  Sweep it, and the population is small: every figure currently quoted as a COST —
  guard timings, capture times, suite durations, the profiler numbers.

  For each: did the run complete, or was it stopped?
    completed   -> it is a cost.
    stopped     -> it is a lower bound, and it is rewritten as one wherever quoted.
    unknown     -> say unknown. That is the honest third state and it is not a
                   failure of the sweep.

3. Q2 — DO NOT BUILD THE CORRECTED HOOK

It would let the guard run on 3.11. Nothing this project measures runs on 3.11. The probe's evidence is produced on 3.12, the guard is a repository instrument that pyproject.toml does not distribute, and a 3.11 user of the package never invokes it.

And the decisive reason is what this round just found. Two recorders that must agree is a new relation between two instruments — and TB-24's unadjudicated candidate is that the guard already has one such relation and does not check it. Adding a second unchecked relation in the round that discovered the first is the wrong order.

Build nothing here. Record the ×1.8 measurement, which is now a real number and retires a false one.

4. Q3 — THE GUARD'S UNCHECKED RELATION IS THE REAL WORK

"The whole-frame guard would pass if both sides broke identically, and the relation between them is asserted in prose rather than checked."

This is the hole in the instrument that has gated more rounds' evidence than any other. The guard's SAME is a believed silence, and nothing establishes that the instrument could have said anything else — R215 §0's refinement, pointed at the guard itself.

DECISION 4:
  Assert the RELATION, not only the equality: the contaminated side must find, and
  the corrected side must not. Today that holds only because the term-by-term
  comparison happens to encode it, which is a property of the arrangement rather
  than a checked fact.

  the relation is cheap to assert inside the existing run
      -> assert it, and the guard's SAME becomes a discriminating silence rather
         than a coincidence of two numbers.
  it needs a separate contaminated fixture
      -> report the cost against the 20-minute criterion before building it.
  it cannot be asserted for a reason you can state
      -> then say so, and the guard's result is quoted with that limit attached
         from now on.

This goes after §5, not ahead of it, and only because of the rule below.

5. EXTEND-AND-RENAME LEADS — because I wrote the rule that says so

Ruled at R228, carried at R229, carried at R230. Third carry. R221 §4 binds me: an item at three deferrals leads the next delta, nothing placed ahead of it.

§4 is more interesting and that is exactly why the rule exists — "something more important arrived" is what has kept this item moving for three rounds. A rule that costs nothing when honoured was not a rule.

Unchanged from R228: extend with Spearman, rename to the mechanism, no alias, and the silence's frame names both statistics and both thresholds.

6. HALT LIST — round-specific

Placing anything ahead of §5 · building the corrected setprofile hook · quoting any stopped run's duration as a cost · reporting the guard's SAME without either the asserted relation or its stated limit · adding a second unchecked instrument-to-instrument relation · renaming without extending, or extending without renaming · keeping an alias for the old check name · a silence frame naming one of two screens · quoting 15dc83c7… as current evidence · quoting any count without its command and resolved version · restating a durable rule in a delta halt list.

7. REPORT FORMAT

§5, then §4, then §2's sweep. Then §3 recorded as a decision with its number.

Stop where the round ends and name what is left.

R2322026-09-05THE GUARD'S SAME MEANS SOMETHING NOW — and so, retroactively, do the old ones

Supersedes R116 through R231 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

Nothing is carried, the guard's silence is discriminating for the first time, and the rules live in a file. That is the moment to turn back toward features. §5 is inference.

0. THE GUARD'S SAME MEANS SOMETHING NOW — and so, retroactively, do the old ones

Every previous "8 of 8 SAME" established that eight numbers matched eight committed numbers. This one established first that the instrument could have said something else: the contaminated side found 5,220 records, the corrected side found none, checked against the run rather than against the baseline file.

And that reaches backwards. The relation holds for this run, and this run's terms match the committed baseline. So the baseline's terms are terms for which the relation holds — which means every prior SAME against that baseline was a comparison against discriminating values, even though nobody had checked it at the time. The old results are vindicated by today's check, not by themselves. That is the honest form of the strengthening and it costs nothing.

Two other things from §4 worth keeping:

  • The guard lived in a scratch directory for twenty rounds. Moving it to tools/ before adding the relation was R229 §0's lesson applied before it bit — a relation asserted in a file that gets cleaned is asserted nowhere.
  • The move exposed its own defect — module-level body, whole guard run as an import side effect, 421 s, passed. Caught because the test was slow, not because it failed. Time is a signal, and the disproportionate-duration instinct is the same one that caught the CRLF rewrite.

1. A DOCUMENT ABOUT A DEFECT CLASS IS WHERE THE CLASS APPEARS

HAND_TYPED_FIGURES.md hand-typed four figures, three already stale, and its two tallies disagreed. That is the fourth instance of one shape this cycle:

  1. R216 dropped "a config key the loader reads and ignores" from the halt list in the delta headlined by that phrase.
  2. ROUND_STATE.md says it is rewritten every round and accreted for sixty.
  3. TB-21's shape recurred in the file that records TB-21.
  4. The list of hand-typed figures hand-typed the figures.

The author of a document about a failure mode is attending to the abstraction, not applying it to the document in hand. The document about X is the most likely place for X, not the least.

Four instances, one mechanism, population enumerable — the documents that describe a defect class. Worth a lessons entry, and its siblings line is the list of such documents, each checked against its own subject. Do not sweep them this round; list them.

2. Q1 — NO SEPARATE NON-MONOTONE SCREEN. The right instrument already exists.

y**2 at Pearson 0.011 / Spearman 0.022 is a real gap in the pairwise screens and there is no equally cheap closure — every candidate (mutual information, distance correlation, a flexible fit) carries a binning, memory or model choice that would need its own pre-commitment and known positive.

But the reason not to build it is not cost. A feature derived from the future label is leakage whatever its functional form, and the availability probe catches it regardless of form, because it perturbs cells rather than measuring correlation. That is the registered instrument, and non-monotone label copies are its job. The pairwise screens are a cheap early warning for the exact-copy case, which is common and embarrassing — not a second detector.

DECISION 2:
  (a) Do not build. R215 §2's rule applies: the case for a new check starts from a
      demonstrated need, and y**2 is a constructed case nobody has met.
  (b) Name the bound in the silence. The frame already names both screens; it also
      says what neither sees — monotone copies are caught, non-monotone functional
      copies are not, and the availability probe is where those are caught.
  (c) Record the candidate approaches with their costs where the analysis lives, so
      the next person with this idea meets the reasoning rather than repeating it.

3. Q2 — CONFIRMED CLOSED, and here is why the two checks together suffice

TB-24's candidate was: the guard passes if both sides break identically. Walk the cases:

  • both sides break and find nothing → the relation fails (contaminated must find).
  • both sides break and find the same thing → the relation fails (corrected must be silent).
  • both sides break and the relation still holds → the terms changed, and the comparison fails.

No identical break survives both checks. Closed — and it is closed by the conjunction, not by the relation alone, which is worth stating so nobody later removes the comparison as redundant.

4. Q3 — YES. The baseline carries its constants.

Stride, seed and instrument-month in one file; the baseline in another; nothing checks they describe the same run. Same shape as the digest and its recipe, and the same fix: the baseline is a figure, and its generation constants are its frame.

DECISION 4:
  The baseline file records the constants it was generated under. The guard reads
  them and refuses to compare if its own constants differ — the R213 currency
  check's shape, applied to the guard's own inputs.

  A refusal, not a warning. A guard comparing against a baseline from a different
  run is a guard producing a number that means nothing, and it should not produce
  one.

Small, and it closes the last entry on the hand-typed list that has a mechanical form.

5. THE TURN BACK TO FEATURES — inference

The last fifteen or so rounds have been instruments and records, not features. That was right: the guard was a coincidence, the rules were in my memory, two headline figures were unframed, and a digest nobody could regenerate carried the portability claim. Features built on that would have been untrustworthy.

It is done enough. Nothing is carried, the guard discriminates, the rules are durable, the figures carry their invocations. The author's mandate was "include all the features to make it easy and useful," and the largest ease feature is designed and unbuilt.

Inference, per R215 §3, unchanged in substance:

Infer what is IN the data; require what is ABOUT the world.

DECISION 5 — the build, from the design already in hand:
  (a) A draft model file. Structure — key column, granularity, join shape, whether
      the key sits on boundaries — determined from the frames and marked as
      determined, with the evidence named per column.
  (b) Availability — lag, publication delay, when a value became knowable — left
      UNFILLED, with the observable evidence beside each column to help the user
      fill it. Never a value.
  (c) The audit refuses an unfilled availability field. It does not default it and
      it does not read a blank as agreement.
  (d) The header sentence already written at R225 is the feature: it says why half
      the file is filled and half is not. Keep it.
  (e) S6 — inferring from the dependency map — stays omitted, with the reason at
      the signal registry and in the draft's own output, as R215 §4 placed it.
  (f) The seven signals and their seven wrong cases from PRE_BUILD_READS.md are the
      spec. Each signal ships with its wrong case as a test that must NOT produce
      a confident answer on it.

  The known positive discriminates: a frame where structure is determinable and
  availability is not, confirming the draft fills the first and leaves the second
  blank. A wrong inference fills both.

One build. Not align_key's zone key, not the D2 subsystem — those are queued and stay queued. Inference is the one that changes what a user can do.

6. HALT LIST — round-specific

Building a non-monotone screen · a silence frame that does not name what neither screen sees · removing the term comparison as redundant to the relation · the guard comparing against a baseline whose constants it has not checked · a baseline constants mismatch reported as a warning rather than a refusal · sweeping the defect-class documents this round rather than listing them · an inferred availability value of any kind · treating an unfilled availability field as agreement · inferring anything from the dependency map · a signal shipped without its wrong-case test · starting align_key or the D2 subsystem ahead of inference · quoting any count without its command and resolved version · restating a durable rule in a delta halt list.

7. REPORT FORMAT

§4 first, it is small. Then §2 and §3 as records. Then §1's list. Then §5, which is the round's work — stop there if it fills the round and say how far it got.

R2332026-09-06THE WRONG-CASE TESTS EARNED THEIR PLACE ON THE FIRST RUN

Inference shipped and its wrong-case tests paid twice on the first run. The second catch is the third instance of one hole — the test took the library path and the user takes the CLI — and §3 closes it structurally.

0. THE WRONG-CASE TESTS EARNED THEIR PLACE ON THE FIRST RUN

S2's case caught a unit bug — astype("int64") % 1_000_000_000 assumes nanoseconds and datetime64[us] is microseconds. A boundary fraction of 0.00% on a 1 Hz lattice, which the wrong-case test refused to accept as a confident answer. That is what asserting the absence of a conclusion is for: a test that checked for a specific number would have needed to know the number.

The second catch is the one to record. _is_datetimeish asked dtype == object, which is how text presents under pandas 2; under pandas 3 it is str. One mechanism, three instances, and an enumerable population — the CLI's commands. §3 closes it.

1. Q2 — WRITE THE FILE, and the half-filled file is safe because the audit refuses it

Printing only means the user copies the output into a file by hand. That is a hand-transcription step, which is the class this project just spent five rounds removing from its own records. A feature whose first step is "copy this carefully" is not the easy feature the mandate asked for.

Your concern is right and it resolves itself: what does a half-filled model file on disk mean to the audit path? It means a refusal. §5(c) already says the audit refuses an unfilled availability field. So a draft on disk is safe exactly because the boundary that reads it is the one that refuses.

DECISION 1:
  (a) `draft` writes the file. Printing stays available; writing is the default
      path a user takes.
  (b) THE DRAFT CARRIES PROVENANCE: generated-by, commit, source frames, and a
      per-field marker — determined-from-data or unfilled. That is the frame
      travelling with the figure, applied to a model file.
  (c) The audit's refusal on a drafted file NAMES it as a draft and lists the
      unfilled fields. "Missing field" is a generic message; "this draft has 3
      availability fields you have not filled" is the route out.
  (d) When an audit runs on a file whose structure fields were drafted and never
      edited, the OUTPUT says so. There is no "accept the tool's guess" path for
      availability any more — the tool never guesses it — but structure can still
      be accepted unread, and a finding produced under drafted structure should
      carry that fact.
  (e) NEVER OVERWRITE. If the target exists, refuse. A user with a hand-written
      model who runs `draft` by mistake must not lose it. Irreversible-act rule,
      one check, cheap.

2. Q3 — THE DECISION FRAME IS ABOUT THE PIPELINE, and it stays out of draft

"Nothing in the frames identifies which frame carries the decision instant." Correct, and that is the answer. Which frame's clock is d(i) is a fact about what the user's pipeline does with the frames — the spine it builds output rows on — not a shape in the frames themselves. R215 §3's line puts it on the require side.

And a wrong guess here is the worst silent error available: the audit runs against the wrong decision clock and reports clean. The evidence-without- conclusion treatment is right: list the candidate frames with their keys and granularities, leave the field blank.

One thing to rule out before it drifts in. The callable could identify the decision frame — the dependency map shows which frame's key indexes the output. That is not S6's error (which was "read, therefore available"); it is a structural fact about the callable's behaviour. But it is inference-from-behaviour, not inference-from-data, and draft() is frames-only with a test asserting no probe symbol is reachable from it.

DECISION 2:
  The decision frame is unfilled in the draft, with candidate frames and their
  evidence beside it. Out of scope for `draft`, and say so in the draft's output.

  Whether the CALLABLE can identify the decision frame is a different feature with
  its own establish step. Record it as a candidate. Do not build it this round,
  and do not let it reopen S6 by the side door — the boundary "draft reads frames
  and nothing else" is tested, and it stays tested.

3. THE CLI-PATH TEST — the hole has bitten three times; close it as a standing check

DECISION 3:
  For each CLI command, one test that invokes it AS A USER WOULD: through the CLI
  entry point, with file inputs in the user's format, checking the output. Not the

  The known positive for this suite already exists and discriminates: a CSV with

This is small and it is the structural fix for a defect class that has now reached the user path three times. The definition-of-done walk caught the six frictions once; this is the version that keeps catching them.

TB-25's reason for deferring is exact: a sweep in the same breath is the same act of attention and inherits the same blind spot. So it wants a different act of attention — the opening item of a round, cold, checking each document against its own stated subject concretely rather than thinking about the class.

R234 opens with it and nothing is placed ahead. Eight documents, one question each: does this document exhibit the thing it describes? Not urgent, and "not urgent" is how items reach three deferrals — so it gets a slot now.

R2342026-09-06draft GUESSING aggregate_frames FOR EVERY DATETIME COLUMN IS A DEFECT

Supersedes R116 through R233 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

The aggregate_frames-for-every-datetime-column finding is real, not a limitation, and it is the mirror risk arriving through the front door. It leads. Then the eight-document sweep, which R233 §4 already promised opens R234.

0. draft GUESSING aggregate_frames FOR EVERY DATETIME COLUMN IS A DEFECT

You flagged it as "structurally defensible but probably not what a user wants." It is a defect, and naming it precisely matters: draft is inferring an availability mode — aggregate_frames is a mode — from the shape of the frame. That is inferring what is ABOUT the world from what is IN the data, which R215 §3 forbids and §5(a)/(b) were built to honour.

The station frame is the proof. A single datetime column got aggregate_frames because that is what a lone timestamp looks like, and in the live run that frame carries the decision instant, not an aggregate. DECISION 0:
  The availability MODE is not structure. It goes on the require side with the
  rest of availability.

  (a) `draft` does NOT assign a mode. It reports, per frame: the datetime columns
      present, their granularity, whether values sit on boundaries — the evidence
      — and leaves the mode UNFILLED.

  (c) What `draft` MAY say is narrower and honest: "one datetime column, on 1 Hz
      boundaries — if this frame is an aggregate, aggregate_frames fits; if it
      carries the decision instant, it does not. You decide which." Evidence and
      the fork, not a pick.

  This is the mirror risk you set out to prevent, found inside the feature built
  to prevent it. Fixing it is the round.

And the discriminating positive already exists: the station frame. The wrong draft fills its mode; the correct draft leaves it blank and names the fork. A draft that assigns any mode to it fails.

1. WRITE THE column_modes SKELETON — commented, so the blank is visible

"Nothing writes column_modes into the draft; the refusal tells the user to fill it there, but the key is absent." Write it, commented, and the reason is the one this project keeps arriving at: the refusal names a place, and a place that does not exist in the file is a route out that dead-ends. The skeleton is the frame travelling with the instruction.

  The drafted file carries a commented column_modes skeleton: one entry per column
  that needs a mode, each with its evidence inline as a comment and the value left
  blank or as a fill-me sentinel.

  a commented sentinel could be read by the loader as a real value
      -> it must not. The loader refuses a sentinel exactly as it refuses a blank —
         a fill-me left unfilled is an unfilled field, not a mode. Test both.
  the skeleton could drift from what draft actually determined

This composes with §0: the skeleton's entries are the frames whose mode draft now refuses to guess, each carrying the fork sentence rather than a value.

R2352026-09-06THE ROUND'S STRONGEST RESULT, AND ITS FLATTERING READING NAMED

Supersedes R116 through R234 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

The decision frame is the one require-side field with no scaffold and possibly no refusal — if the audit picks one silently, that is the aggregate-mode defect again, unshipped-fix version, and it leads. Then the answer vocabulary, before use makes it a contract.

0. THE ROUND'S STRONGEST RESULT, AND ITS FLATTERING READING NAMED

Per the standing rule (R226 §4): the aggregate_frames catch is the round's best result, and the comfortable reading is "the draft/require discipline is so sound it caught its own violation."

It is not that. The violation shipped — draft assigned modes from R232 through R234, a full round live, and it was caught because you asked a question in R234, not by a test and not by the discipline detecting anything. The discipline named the fix once the defect was pointed at; it neither prevented the defect nor found it. The test added this round is what makes it not recur — after the fact.

The honest statement: the draft/require split is a good design that was mis-implemented in exactly the way it exists to prevent, went unnoticed for a round, and is now guarded. That is a smaller and truer claim than "the discipline works," and it is the one that goes in the record.

And your 1-in-8 reading was already the honest one — "clean because an earlier round was bitten, not by good writing" — so I am affirming it, not correcting it. The flattering version is "the sweep found almost nothing, so TB-25 is minor." The falsifier is yours: the four originals were found by accident over five rounds, so one hit in a deliberate eight-document pass, with three more clean only because prior rounds were already bitten, means the class's pre-mitigation rate is high, not low.

1. THE DECISION FRAME — establish the refusal FIRST; it may be a live defect

"draft still writes no decision_column, so a filled draft needs one hand-added key the skeleton does not mention."

The scaffold gap is real, but there is a worse question underneath it, and it decides whether this is a defect or a gap:

When the decision frame is absent from a model file, does the audit refuse, or does it pick one? If it picks, that is the worst silent error the tool can make — an audit run against the wrong clock, reported clean — and it is the aggregate_frames defect again, one field over.

DECISION 1 — establish before building:
  Trace the audit path with no decision frame declared. What happens?

  it refuses, naming the missing decision frame
      -> then this is only a scaffold gap. The skeleton gains the decision frame as
         an explicit unfilled field, with its candidate frames and keys as
         evidence beside it — the same treatment the availability fields and the
         modes now have. One unfilled-field refusal path, three kinds of field.
  it picks a decision frame silently (first frame, only datetime frame, any rule)
      -> LIVE DEFECT, and it leads everything. A drafted file a user completes to
         the skeleton's satisfaction would then audit against a guessed clock. Fix:
         the audit refuses an undeclared decision frame, the refusal names the
         candidates, and the skeleton scaffolds it. Disclose with the exemption
         test and a discriminating positive — a frame set where the guessed clock
         and the true clock differ.
  the decision frame is declared through some path draft does not write
      -> report which, and whether that path is itself refused when blank. Do not
         assume a path outside draft is safe because it is outside draft.

The discriminating positive is constructible either way: two frames whose clocks disagree, where picking the wrong one flips a finding. If the audit picks, that test fails today.

2. THE ANSWER VOCABULARY — settle it before use makes it the contract

accept() takes "aggregate:<col>" and "decision_frame" — strings you chose, not in leakaudit schema. This is the config-key class caught one step early: an undocumented user-facing surface, before anyone depends on it rather than after.

The rule that decides its shape is not "document it." It is tighter:

The fork draft states and the answers accept() takes are one contract, and they must be the same set of options. A user reads a fork with named branches and must be able to express exactly those branches back, in the words the fork used. If the fork says "aggregate, or decision instant, or neither" and accept() takes two strings, the question and its answer space have diverged — the figure and its frame again, applied to a question and its reply.

DECISION 2:
  (a) REPORT the distinctions the vocabulary must carry before fixing its words —
      the cases, as align_key's and the threshold's were reported. How many fork
      outcomes are there really? aggregate-over-column, carries-decision-instant,
      and is there a third (naive throughout / not-a-time-frame)? A vocabulary with
      a case nobody can produce, or missing a case the fork states, is the defect.
  (b) The fork text and the accept() vocabulary are generated to match, or tested
      to match — not maintained as two hand-kept lists. Two lists that must agree
      and are edited separately is the guard-constants-and-baseline shape.
  (c) THEN document the settled vocabulary in leakaudit schema, where the user
      meets it.

  Do not pick the words silently and document them after. That is the order that
  makes an ad hoc string a contract by inertia.

3. THE SWEEP SWEPT THE DIAGONAL — say so, and that is the fix

"The sweep checked each document against one class only — a document can exhibit a different class than the one it names, and nothing looked for that. Unexamined, not clean."

Correct, and the response is not to sweep the full matrix. It is to record the axis the sweep covered, so the result cannot be read as more than it is.

A sweep result carries the axis it swept, exactly as a count carries its invocation and an absence claim its population. "The eight documents were checked against the class each describes" is the true statement; "the eight documents were swept" is the one that will be quoted, and it claims the whole matrix.

DECISION 3:
  (a) The sweep record states its axis: diagonal only — each document against the
      class it names. Not the off-diagonal — a document against a class it does not
      describe.
  (b) Do NOT sweep the full matrix. No instance motivates it — every measured case
      of a document exhibiting a defect class has been a document exhibiting its
      OWN class. R215 §2: the case for the work starts from a demonstrated need.
  (c) Record the off-diagonal as a bounded, stated gap with its population (eight
      documents × the enumerable class list) and the trigger that would open it:
      the first instance of a document exhibiting a class it does not name.

  That converts "unexamined, not clean" into "unexamined on a named axis, with the
  trigger recorded" — which is the honest form, and it costs three sentences.

4. BANKED

draft assigning nothing and stating the fork — "THE FORK, AND ONLY YOU CAN TAKE IT" — is the mirror risk closed at the field that let it in, with a test asserting no frame receives a mode across four shapes. That test is the durable half; the fix is the occasion.

The refusal ordering — comprehensive draft message before the per-key sentinel — is the route-out placed where the user hits it first, and it is R210 §1's missing-boundary lesson applied to the draft's own surface.

TB-26 — sys.modules caches by name, not path, and tmp_path isolates the filesystem but not the module cache — is a real generalisation and it was self-caught by existing tests failing on a column they never wrote. A fixture that names a module must assume another fixture named it too is the line worth keeping.

5. HALT LIST — round-specific

Building the decision-frame scaffold before its refusal behaviour is established · an audit that picks a decision frame when none is declared · picking the answer vocabulary's words before its cases are reported · a fork text and an accept() vocabulary kept as two separately-edited lists · documenting the vocabulary before it is settled · sweeping the off-diagonal without an instance motivating it · recording the sweep without its axis · draft assigning any availability mode · treating an unfilled field as agreement · inferring anything from the dependency map · any probe symbol reachable from draft() · quoting any count without its command and resolved version · restating a durable rule in a delta halt list.

6. REPORT FORMAT

§1's establish step first, and the branch it lands on. Then §2's cases, reported before any word is fixed. Then §3's axis record. Then "what you must rule on."

R2362026-09-06THE STANDING RULE, AND THE OPPOSITE TEMPTATION

Supersedes R116 through R235 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

The decision-column default was live for the whole project and the fix was caught before building on it — establish-first working as designed. But "caught the defect" is not "no reported figure ran through it," and that is unmeasured. It leads.

0. THE STANDING RULE, AND THE OPPOSITE TEMPTATION

The round's strongest result is the decision-column defect: a real leak reported as observed_silence, exit 0 — the tool's affirmative "this is evidence." Found by the establish step, before the scaffold was built on top of it.

This time the flattering reading is also the true one. Unlike the aggregate_frames defect, which shipped and was caught by a question, this one was caught by the establish-first step doing exactly its job. I am not going to manufacture a falsifier to look rigorous — inventing skepticism where the result is clean is its own dishonesty, and the rule serves truth, not a performance of it.

What the catch did not establish is the boundary, and that is real: "we caught the defect" is measured; "the defect harmed no reported figure" is not. The default has been in the code the whole project. That is §1.

1. THE DECISION-COLUMN DEFECT'S BLAST RADIUS — unmeasured, and it leads

load_model defaulted to "timestamp" for the project's whole history. Every audit ever run under a model file that did not declare decision_column used that default. The fix stops it going forward; it says nothing about what already ran.

DECISION 1 — measure, do not argue:
  Did any REPORTED figure run under the defaulted decision_column?

  The likely answer is "no, Phase 1 declared its model" — and that is an argument,
  which is exactly what R227 §1 said is not a measurement. Establish it:
    - Phase 1's availability declaration: does it set decision_column explicitly,
      or did it inherit the default? Read the declared model, not memory of it.
    - Any Phase 2 figure produced through a model file: same question.

  every reported figure declared it explicitly
      -> the blast radius is empty, stated with the reading: the default was live
         but no reported audit entered it, because every one declared its clock.
         Say how that was determined.
  any reported figure inherited the default
      -> that figure was run against a possibly-wrong clock and is re-examined. If
         its clock happened to be named timestamp correctly, the result stands and
         say so; if not, it is a finding larger than this round.

This is the ties_available form — "no published figure moves, and that was checked" — owed for this defect and not yet paid.

2. THE FORK ASKS TWO QUESTIONS AS ONE — that is why case 3 has no home

Your enumeration found the real defect: the fork mixes two independent questions and offers a two-item menu across their product.

  • Question A: is this frame the decision spine (d(i)), or an availability source (its cells feed features)?
  • Question B: if a source, which availability mode maps its cells to availability times?

aggregate_frames is one answer to B; decision_frame is one answer to A. Cases 3, 4 and 5 have no home because they are other answers to B, or the "neither" of A — and "read at its own stamp" is a mode, the same category as aggregate_frames, not a missing fork branch.

You already reached the shape — "(case, column?), which is what column_modes already uses." So the vocabulary is not invented; it is the mode set that exists.

DECISION 2 — establish, then settle:
  (a) STRUCTURAL READ, population stated: does the existing availability-mode set
      (the six mappings) already contain "read at its own stamp" and the other
      cases the fork needs? R207/R208 discussed at_source_timestamp, so it likely
      does — likely is not established.

      the mode set covers all five cases
          -> the fork routes into it. accept() takes a mode name from the existing,
             already-documented set, not a bespoke "aggregate:col" string. Case 3
             stops being unexpressible because it was always a mode.
      the mode set is missing a case the world has
          -> that is a finding about the MODE SET, not the fork, and it is larger
             than a vocabulary fix. Report it and stop before inventing a word.
  (b) The fork text then asks A first (spine or source), and only for a source asks
      B (which mode) — two questions, in order, not a two-item menu across both.
  (c) The fork text and accept()'s answer space are generated from the one mode
      set, so they cannot diverge — the two-lists hazard, closed by construction.
  (d) Then document it in leakaudit schema.

  The tick-frame user being told to pick between two wrong branches is live output,
  so this is a defect fix, not polish — but it waits behind §1's measurement.

3. THE LIBRARY DEFAULT AND THE SCOPE PROXY — one sentinel closes both

Two things you flagged are the same fix.

  • AvailabilityModel.decision_column still defaults to "timestamp" at the library level — a second entry point, and the recurring lesson (P0 at audit() vs the CLI; the config keys; datetimeish on frames vs files) is that a fix at one entry point does not cover the other.
  • The file-boundary refusal is scoped to "aggregate_frames present + decision_column absent." aggregate_frames present is a proxy for "declares an availability model," and a file declaring column_modes but no aggregate_frames may still default silently. A proxy for the real condition is where a hole hides.

Both dissolve at the same point:

DECISION 3 — establish first, then one fix inward, not two at the edges:
  (a) ESTABLISH the two holes by measurement:
      - construct AvailabilityModel in Python with no decision_column and
        wrong-clock frames: does it silently pick?
      - a model file with column_modes, no aggregate_frames, no decision_column:
        does the audit silently default?

0. TWO AXES, AND THIS IS THE STEP THAT CLOSES THE REGRESS

R239 made the consumers a population. R240 made the test's files a population. This paste shows the population is bounded on two axes, and "all consumers covered" rests on both:

  • The file axis — which files the test scans. You have git ls-files filtered to 398 .py.
  • The read axis — which of the reads it finds are consumers. You have 10 reads in 7 files, and four are consumers.

Both are absence claims, and both have a definite floor — which is why this step ends the recursion rather than spawning another. After the file set is every tracked file that can carry a clock read, and every read found is classified, there is no third axis: a clock use must be a read of decision_column, in a tracked file, in runnable code. Close both and the chain is closed.

1. THE FILE AXIS — .py is a filter chosen by habit; establish it is complete

.py is almost certainly right, and "almost certainly" is the word this project does not accept. The claim underneath it is: no non-.py tracked file carries runnable Python that reads the clock.

  git ls-files with no *.py filter. Inspect the non-.py tail for anything that
  carries runnable Python — .ipynb above all, also .pyx/.pyi or a script with a
  python shebang.

  the tail carries no runnable Python
      -> .py is the complete floor, PROVED not assumed, and the test says so: its
         scope is "every tracked file that can contain a clock read," which equals
         the .py set here, and the reason is recorded.
  any tracked file carries runnable Python outside .py
      -> it is in scope. A notebook that reads the clock is a consumer a .py scan
         never sees.

The gap between 10 reads and 4 consumers is where a consumer hides. "This read is not a clock use" is an absence claim per site, and six of them made by inspection is six eyeballed dismissals, any one of which could be a clock use waved past.

Your protocol/ check was grep decision_column → zero, and that is rigorous, not a shortcut, for a reason worth stating precisely:

A clock use requires the substring decision_column. So its absence proves the use is absent — no parse can find a use of a string that does not occur. Presence proves nothing (R218: the docstring read as an import). The two directions are not symmetric.

DECISION 3:

  confirm a use is PRESENT; substring-absence is sufficient — and stronger — to
  confirm a use is ABSENT. protocol/ used the sound direction. The totality test
  may use substring-absence to exclude a file cheaply, and must parse to classify a
  file that contains the string.

That also makes the file axis cheaper: most of the 398 files contain no decision_column at all, excluded soundly by absence; only the 7 that contain it need parsing.

protocol/runtime_reference.py — the frozen reducer, the sharp case — checked and found not a consumer, by measurement. The flattering reading is "the frozen instrument is clean." R2462026-09-07THE THINGS I COULD NOT SEE, NOW READ — and branch 1 confirmed

Supersedes R116 through R245 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

Constraints only — mid-flight. The count was not test-owned after all: the assertion matches \b27\b inside TB-27, so with contiguous ids it can never fail on a stale total. R245 §2's proof-before-believing surfaced a third can't-fail test this session, and that is the round.

0. THE THINGS I COULD NOT SEE, NOW READ — and branch 1 confirmed

The guard returned SAME on both rounds, relation checked before the comparison, eight terms each — R243 at 4557921, R244 at 231c6d9, check_registration.py byte-identical to its pre-R242 state, count 2 of 4. The work since R243 stands, read rather than inferred.

Branch 1 of §1 held: 26 entries, 26 classified, 0 unclassified, families 5+6+4+5+5+1. "Twenty-one" was stale prose and never hid a gap — the reassuring branch, established by measurement, not assumed.

1. "TEST-OWNED" WAS PSEUDO-OWNERSHIP — the count assertion cannot fail

The count test computes the right total and then checks for it like this:

total = len(_entries(text))          # correct: dynamic
assert re.search(r"\b%d\b" % total, section)   # vacuous: matches TB-<total>

Ids are TB-NN and numbering is contiguous, so len(entries) always equals the highest id number, and \bNN\b always matches that entry's own id. The assertion is satisfied by the newest entry's label, not by any stated total. It has never been able to fail on a wrong count — which is the exact thing it exists to catch.

So "the count is test-owned," which the earlier read reported as the reassuring finding, was false. The test looks like enforcement — it computes the total and searches for it — and enforces nothing. A third can't-fail test this session, and the most convincing kind, because it does real work right up to the assertion and then asserts something always true.

R245 §2's proof is what caught it. "Prove a new entry requires exactly one update" — you simulated a 28th entry, the test passed with no count update, and the \b28\b came from TB-28 itself. A proof-of-the-property revealed the property absent. That is the criterion working exactly as intended.

DECISION 1 — the fix by its property, not my construction:
  The count assertion must FAIL when the stated total is wrong, and it must fail
  even when the wrong number coincides with an existing entry id. That is the
  immune known positive: N entries, the total line stating a different number M,
  where M also appears as TB-M somewhere in the section — the test must fail on it.
    - parse the specific total DECLARATION and compare it to the enumeration; do not
      search the whole section for a bare digit.

1. "CERTIFIED" IS AN ABSENCE CLAIM OVER THE CERTIFICATION STEPS — enforce its population

The skip was possible because certification is several commands — the frozen checker, the hash verifier (R243), the clean-tree check (R247), and the work-root precondition — with nothing ensuring all of them run. You ran a subset and read the result as certification.

That is the totality lesson turned on the process that runs the checks. "The gate passed" has meant "the commands I happened to run passed," and the set of required steps was never enforced complete — the same failure as a count that counts only the entries it happens to see.

  (c) The structural close is a single certification entrypoint that runs every
      step and fails if any is skipped or any precondition unmet — so "certify" is

R2502026-09-07THE ENUMERATOR EXCLUDED THE CASES THAT MATTER, AND YOU CAUGHT IT

Supersedes R116 through R249 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

Constraints only — mid-flight. 141 is too many for bespoke mutations, and the generic one you are converging on is right — but "passes over an empty population" is a CANDIDATE generator, not a verdict, and it covers one vacuity subclass of three. The sweep is honest only if it says which.

0. THE ENUMERATOR EXCLUDED THE CASES THAT MATTER, AND YOU CAUGHT IT

Your population definition went 229 → 115 (LEN/SETDIFF/SETEQ) → and the 115 excluded assert not <collection> — which is exactly how test_decision_clock_consumers, test_lessons_classification, test_manifest_hashes and test_config_key_complement make their repo-population claims. 141 assertions, 30 files. Too many to mutate bespoke, so the generic mutation is the right instrument — with the two corrections below.

1. "PASSES OVER AN EMPTY POPULATION" IS A CANDIDATE, NOT A VERDICT

Emptying the population and asking whether the assertion still passes is the right generic probe — it is exactly the round_reconciliation defect. But an empty population is sometimes a legitimate vacuous truth and sometimes a masked bug, and only a per-assertion judgment separates them. So the probe produces candidates, the defaults-tracer shape (R222): the list is never a finding list.

DECISION 1:
  (a) Run the generic empty-population probe over all 141. Output: the assertions
      that pass over an empty population. A CANDIDATE LIST, named as such.

          the round_reconciliation fix generalised: the assertion also asserts the
          population is non-empty, or reports could_not_run over empty — never a
          silent pass.
        yes — some genuinely optional collection -> empty-pass is correct; record
          why, so the candidate is closed with a reason, not waved off.
  (c) If the can-it-be-empty judgment over 141 is itself more than a round, that is
      fine and expected — report the candidate list with the judgments made so far
      and the remainder as owed, WITH its count. A partial judgment reported as a
      partial judgment is not the half-sweep failure; a partial one reported as
      complete is.

2. THE GENERIC PROBE COVERS ONE VACUITY SUBCLASS OF THREE — name the other two

The empty-population probe catches the round_reconciliation class. It does not catch the other two this session actually hit:

  • Value-coincidence — the count assertion matching \bNN\b inside TB-NN. The population is not empty; a wrong value coincides with data already present. Emptying the population would make it fail (correctly), so the empty probe passes it — and it is exactly the bug we spent R246 on.
  • Wrong-input — the bare=True control that passed a frame where a dict was expected. The assertion never exercised its subject; emptying the population does not surface it.
DECISION 2:

  coverage assertions are swept," full stop, would be the totality over-claim this
  very sweep exists to catch, made about the sweep itself.

3. THE 141 BECOME A TRACKED POPULATION, CHECKED AGAINST THE ENUMERATOR

The enumerator's definition was wrong twice this round and right only because you knew what to look for. That knowledge does not survive to the next person, so it goes into a mechanism.

DECISION 3:
  The coverage-assertion population is a tracked artifact — the list of the 141, as
  data — and a test regenerates the enumeration and fails if the tracked list and
  the current code disagree. A coverage assertion added later is then either in the
  list (and carries its empty-population judgment) or fails the test. Same shape as
  the decision-clock consumer totality: the population is pinned, not remembered.

  And the enumerator's criterion is recorded with it — including that it must catch
  `assert not <collection>`, the shape it first missed — so the definition that took
  three tries is written down where the next change to it can be checked.

4. tasks/ — established frozen-hardcoded, so the A/B is Theo's

_EPHEMERAL is a tuple literal at check_registration.py:1789, inside the frozen instrument. So excluding tasks/ is the A/B branch of R249 §2, and the slot-spend is the author's:

The probe patched emptier names on the test module; the tests call them on the imported tool module (mv.entries(), cas.population()), so most populations were never emptied and 37 of the "candidates" were the probe failing to empty, not assertions passing over empty. You caught it by investigating 37 → 16 rather than trusting 37 — the chase-the-suspicious-number practice (R208, R224). The boundary: that is a number looking off and being chased, not a mechanism. DECISION 0:

  fed through the probe, confirmed to REDDEN. The five it reddened are evidence it

  vacuity is exactly the defect it hunts.

    not-actually-a-coverage-assertion — the enumerator over-included it (a message

1. THE HEREDOC LAPSE — the fix is not more naming, because naming is the thing that failed

Third lapse in three rounds, and your diagnosis is the sharpest thing in the report: "naming a rule in the same breath as breaking it is worse than breaking it quietly, because it shows the naming is not what governs the hand." That is true, and it generalises past this rule: awareness is not a control; mechanisms are. The whole session has leaned on mechanisms precisely because named intentions do not survive a busy hand — and this rule is the one place with no mechanism, so it is where that shows.

Two honest halves, and neither is self-flagellation, which helps no one:

  • The fix removes the decision, since the decision is where the hand slips. The rule invites a judgment — is this content, or just a placeholder short enough to echo? — and the slip lives in that judgment. So the rule loses its exception: any file is created or changed through Write/Edit, with no triviality case — a one-word placeholder included. There is no mechanism to offer and I am not pretending one; the tightened rule just deletes the moment of judgment that has failed three times.

R2552026-09-07WHAT D CLOSES, STATED SO THE BUILD IS AIMED AT IT

Supersedes R116 through R254 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

Theo picked D — slice-with-padding. First feature build since inference, and it carries the full evidential bar the instruments earned, not a lighter one. Build to DESIGN §5.3, which is the spec; I frame the traps this feature walks into, not its construction.

0. WHAT D CLOSES, STATED SO THE BUILD IS AIMED AT IT

A user auditing a slice of a large frame today gets manufactured edge artifacts and masked deeper leakage, silently — the slice's first rows look like they have no history, so their availability is computed wrong, and the audit reports on a frame that no longer resembles the user's. It is the session's worst class — a reasonable action, silently mis-answered — which is why it outranked the label probe.

The fix is DESIGN §5.3, and that document is the authority, not my paraphrase. Read it first. What follows is the set of traps the session's own lessons say this feature will hit, each a property the build must have — not a construction, which is yours and the spec's.

1. ESTABLISH THE PADDING REQUIREMENT BEFORE BUILDING THE REFUSAL

The whole feature turns on how much padding is enough, and that is not a constant — it is how far back a cell's availability depends, which the availability model defines.

DECISION 1 — establish, population stated, before any refusal is written:
  How is the required padding derived from the availability model? Is it a single
  lookback, or does it vary by mode / by column (aggregate_frames' window vs a
  per-column mode vs at_bar_close)?

  it is derivable from the model
      -> the tool COMPUTES the required padding and the refusal compares against it.
         No fixed default — a fixed padding is the silent-default defect (R236) in a
         new place: enough for one model, silently short for another.
  it varies per column/mode and no single number covers a frame
      -> then the requirement is the MAX over the frame's cells, and the report
         names which column drove it, so the number is not a bare figure.
  the model does not determine it
      -> report that and stop before building a refusal whose threshold is
         unfounded — a padding requirement nobody can derive is align_key's
         unestablished-licence situation again.

2. THE REFUSAL IS A REFUSAL, NOT A WARNING

R248's lesson, and it is the one this feature is most likely to break: when padding is insufficient, the tool refuses — non-zero, no edge verdict — it does not warn and audit anyway. A slice audited with too little padding and a printed caveat is a round_reconciliation "this is not a pass" that returns PASS: the caveat is prose, the result is what the user reads.

DECISION 2:
  insufficient padding -> refuse, naming the required amount and which column or mode
    demands it. The user gets "this needs N rows of context you did not supply,"
    not a clean-looking audit of a truncated frame with a footnote.
  adequate padding -> audit rows [i:j] with [i-pad:i] as context, and see §4.

3. EDGE-CONTEXT ROWS ARE NOT REPORTED AS AUDITED-CLEAN

The padding rows are context, not subjects. Reporting them as audited-and-clean is the manufactured-artifact defect inverted — presenting context as result. §8.2 governs: a row not audited is not_applicable, never clean. The output states plainly which rows were audited and which were context, so a reader cannot mistake the padding for findings.

4. THE KNOWN POSITIVE PUTS THE LEAK AT THE EDGE — or it tests nothing

R215 §0, applied to exactly this feature: a positive with the leak in the slice's interior is found with or without padding, so it proves the audit runs, not that padding does anything. The discriminating positive puts the leak in the edge region — the rows whose history the padding restores.

DECISION 4:
  Construct a frame where a feature leaks in the rows near the slice start:
    - audited WITHOUT padding (today's silent behaviour): the leak is MASKED — the
      truncated history hides it, the audit reads clean. Confirm this first; it is
      the defect the feature exists to close, shown to be real.
    - audited WITH correct padding: the leak is FOUND.
  That pair is the validity test — the feature changes a wrong clean result into a
  finding. A positive that fires both ways is a wiring test and is not enough.

5. THE REFUSAL LIVES AT THE SHARED CONSUMPTION POINT — both entry points

The decision-clock lesson (R236–R239): a boundary fixed at the CLI and not the library, or covered by two refusals that must agree, is the recurring defect. The insufficient-padding refusal sits where both the CLI and the library path reach it, and the consumer set is enumerated so a third path does not bypass it.

DECISION 5:
  Before wiring, enumerate the entry points that reach the slice audit. The refusal
  is at their shared point, tested once below both, or — if they do not join — each
  path carries it with a test, and the reason they do not join is stated. One
  refusal, or a stated reason there are two.

6. HALT LIST — round-specific

Building the refusal before the padding requirement is established from the model · a fixed default padding rather than one derived from the model · insufficient padding warned-and-audited rather than refused · padding/context rows reported as audited-clean · a known positive with the leak in the interior, offered as validating padding · the old no-padding behaviour not shown to mask the edge leak first · a padding refusal at one entry point while another bypasses it · a feature given a lighter evidential bar than the instruments got · certifying against a dirty tree or a skipped enumerated step · any file created or changed through a shell · quoting any count without its command and resolved version · restating a durable rule in a delta halt list.

7. REPORT FORMAT

§1's establish-result — how required padding is derived, quoted from the model — before any refusal. Then the build to DESIGN §5.3. Then §4's positive pair: the edge leak masked without padding, found with it, both measured. Then §5's entry-point enumeration and where the refusal sits. Then §3's audited-vs-context output shown on a real slice. Then certification — clean tree, enumerated steps, the guard if a probe-path file moved. Then "what you must rule on."

R2562026-09-08MY "§8.2" WAS A CITATION WITHOUT ITS DOCUMENT

Supersedes R116 through R255 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

Constraints only — mid-flight; the §1 establish result and the build are not yet reported, and I am not assuming them. One citation slip of mine to own, and two traps the spec leaves open that the build will walk into if they are not pre-ruled.

0. MY "§8.2" WAS A CITATION WITHOUT ITS DOCUMENT

R255 §3 said "§8.2 governs." That is PREREG.md §8.2 — the registered not-run vocabulary (not_applicable / unsupported / could_not_run). I cited it into a delta whose authority document was DESIGN.md, so you looked there, found §8 has no subsections, and correctly used DESIGN §8's own text, which says the same thing. Right resolution, and the slip is mine: a citation names its document, the way a figure names its invocation. A bare "§8.2" is a section number without its population.

Everything R255 asked stands unchanged; this is one line of correction, not a re-specification.

1. DECLARED vs DETERMINED WINDOW — never the smaller, silently

DESIGN §5.3 covers two cases: the model determines the maximum window (the tool computes the padding), or it cannot (max_window= is required). It does not say what happens when both exist — the model determines X and the user also passes max_window=Y.

That third case is where the defect comes back through a declared value. A user passing max_window=5 when the model needs 60 must not get five rows of padding silently — that is the manufactured-edge artifact with the user's own number on it, R236's declared-but-wrong shape (the guard's literal clock, declared, unverified against its fixture).

DECISION 1:
  both the model and the user supply a window
      -> the effective requirement is the LARGER, and the disagreement is REPORTED
         ("model requires 60, you declared 5; using 60"). Never the smaller, never
         silent.
      -> if the design prefers refusing the conflict outright, that is also honest;
         pick one and say which. What is not allowed is trusting the declared
         value because it was declared.
  only the model supplies it
      -> the tool's number, reported as computed.
  only the user supplies it (model cannot determine)
      -> the declared number, reported as declared and unverifiable — so a reader
         knows the padding rests on the user's word, not the model's.

2. THE POSITIVE'S "WITHOUT PADDING" HALF IS THE PLAIN-FRAME PATH

R255 §4 requires showing the edge leak masked without padding before showing it found with. If the slice feature refuses slices without padding, do not read that as "the masked half cannot be produced."

DECISION 2:
  The "without" half is today's actual user path: the truncated slice audited AS AN
  ORDINARY FRAME — which is exactly what a user does now and exactly the silent
  mislead D closes. The slice feature refusing is the fix; the plain-frame path
  masking is the defect. The pair is:
    plain-frame audit of the truncated slice   -> leak MASKED (the defect, real)
    slice feature with correct padding         -> leak FOUND (the fix, real)
  Both measured, on the same frame, same leak, edge-positioned.

3. CARRIED FROM R255 — unchanged, not re-specified

The §1 establish result (how the model determines lookback — per-model or per-frame, where bar_duration lives) quoted in the report before any refusal · the refusal is a refusal, not a warning · context rows never reported as audited-clean · the refusal at the shared consumption point with the entry points enumerated · the establish-first stop if the requirement is not derivable.

4. HALT LIST — round-specific

Using a user-declared max_window= smaller than the model's determined window without refusing or reporting the disagreement · trusting a declared window because it was declared · reading "the slice feature refuses" as "the masked half cannot be shown" · a citation of mine to a section number without its document — flag it back · insufficient padding warned-and-audited · a known positive with the leak in the interior · a padding refusal at one entry point while another bypasses it · any file created or changed through a shell · quoting any count without its command and resolved version · restating a durable rule in a delta halt list.

5. REPORT FORMAT

Unchanged from R255 §7, plus §1's declared-vs-determined rule shown on the conflict case, and §2's pair measured on one frame. Then "what you must rule on."

2. THE CONFOUND LESSON — into the durable rules, as promised

R256 §2's "on the same frame" exposed that R255's positive pair varied two things — extent and values (position-indexed within each range) — so it could have fired because the data differed, not because padding worked. Fixed to one frame cut two ways. My R255 wording permitted it: it said "construct a frame" and described two audits, and never said what was held constant.

DECISION 2 — add to OPERATING_RULES.md as a sharpening of the discriminating-positive
rule:

  owed and continuation is available, CONTINUE. Do not end the turn on a

1. THE BOTH-SUPPLIED BRANCH MUST BE TOTAL — over-declaring is accepted

REFUSE for declared < model floor stands, and your reasoning was better than my "larger-of": the model's window is a floor from the aggregation bucket, not an estimate, so a smaller declared value is invalid rather than merely smaller.

                              declared and sufficient. A branch that refuses every
                              both-supplied case would falsely reject a user who

R2592026-09-09THREE ERRORS OF MINE, AND THE RULE THEY PRODUCE

Supersedes R116 through R258 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.
