Third wrong section citation in four deltas. The guard in R258 caught it — you halted on the number and reported where the content lives — but the rate is the problem.
  2. I wrote "reported as declared and sufficient". "Sufficient" is a claim about the true maximum lookback, which nothing measured. Your wording — DECLARED AND UNVERIFIABLE, clearing a floor is not corroboration — is right and mine is withdrawn. Same shape as R246: "enforced" and "sufficient" are absence claims.
  3. I wrote "both entry points". R255 §5 had already found the third. A delta dropped something the previous round established — the shape halt_audit found at R221.

Rule for me: I do not have the documents, so I do not cite section numbers. I name the content; you cite the section that carries it, and the citation comes back in the report. Any number I do emit is a pointer to check, never a fact.

1. THE CONTINUATION RULE — add it

R258 §0 said add it to OPERATING_RULES.md. It was not added; you asked for the word. The delta is the word.

DECISION 1:
  a rule on disk reserves OPERATING_RULES.md to the author
      -> quote it and stop; Theo rules.
  no such rule
      -> add it to §7 now, with its R258 provenance. Prior rules landed there the
         same way — R226's count rule went into §2 under a delta, by your hand.

2. D's LAST TWO LINES

The accept half exists and is tested twice; the boundary padding == floor is not. That is the one input where < and <= differ — the R216 stamp-on-the-second case in a new place. One test: equal is accepted. The shipped wording stands (see §0.2).

3. RULING 1 — ATTRIBUTION IS THE COMPARATOR, NOT THE SECOND

moved_in_second was never the rule. It is the registered comparator (a <= d available, ties available) under one condition: every perturbed cell has a(j) = F + 1. Under a label horizon H and delay, a(y_j) = t_j + H + delay, and the same test reads: a moved row i is a finding when d(i) < a(y_j), and not a finding when d(i) >= a(y_j). That is the rule L2a implements, per perturbed cell and moved row. It is not a design choice; it is the registration.

DECISION 3:
  (a) L2a's attribution is the comparator above. Nothing else.
  (b) Batch the perturbation so every perturbed label cell in a batch shares ONE
      a(y). Then no row is ambiguous. If the machinery cannot do that cheaply, a
      row whose decision time falls between the batch's smallest and largest a(y)
      is a THIRD STATE — attribution ambiguous — reported as such, never folded
      into finding or observed_silence. Say which of the two you built.
  (c) L3.1 IS NOT TOUCHED THIS ROUND. Instead, establish before any L2a code:
      does every cell L3.1 perturbs have a(j) = F + 1 exactly?
        yes  -> moved_in_second IS the comparator on L3.1's domain. Record the
                identity in L2a's file header: two probes, one rule, one written
                as its special case. Continue to §10 step 3.
        no   -> name the cells and inputs where it is not. That is a Phase 1
                instrument disclosure: record it, repair nothing, stop after §10
                step 3, and report. The probe waits for a ruling.
  (d) Every finding carries its row — L3.1 or L2a — in the output, as findings
      already carry their detector. Confirm L2a's do. That makes §6.2's
      "runtime findings" ambiguity inert in the tool's own output; the registration
      finding stays recorded.

4. RULING 2 — THE STRIDE IS DERIVED

The stride is a consequence of a declared value, not a value about the world. It is D's padding floor again: derive it from the declared availability (horizon + delay + bucket), print it in ABOUT THIS RUN, and refuse only when the data cannot hold it — could_not_run(reason) with the numbers named (needed vs available). L3.1's one-second stride is the special case, and it is not touched.

5. RULING 3 — A NEW RAW-SIDE KEY, SCHEMA v4

Not an extension of label_column. Two reasons: one key with two jobs is the P0 shape (set it for one job, it silently governs the other), and label_column is the built output's and not registered vocabulary — extending it hands a registered job to an unregistered key. New key, named so the side is in the name; the schema text says which side each of the two label keys refers to. label_availability and the locator arrive together at schema version 4, one bump. leakaudit schema describes them only once they are consumed (R216 §5).

6. RULING 4 — REFUSAL SHAPE: THREE CASES, NOT TWO

The registration says absent inputs return unsupported, naming the missing element. Every shipped refusal raises. Both are right, for different cases:

DECISION 6:
  nothing L2a-specific declared
      -> the audit runs; L2a reports EvidenceOutcome `none` with the §8.2 state
         `unsupported(missing: <element>)` in the NOT PROBED block. Never a pass.
  any L2a key present, the set incomplete
      -> REFUSE (raise), naming the missing element. A partial declaration is
         evidence of intent; running past it makes the rest of the output look
         like the audit the user asked for.
  a value malformed
      -> REFUSE, as every shipped refusal does.

  The frozen EvidenceOutcome enum is not touched: `unsupported` is the §8.2 state
  attached to a `none`, the way NOT PROBED already does it. L2a's own result type
  carries it. If the state has to land at a point L3.1 shares, the whole-frame
  guard runs.
  If the registration's "absent" sentence reads as covering the partial case too,
  quote it: it becomes a §8.2 term question for NEXT_REGISTRATION_REQUIREMENTS,
  and the raise stands as a tool-level tightening (R203 permits those).

The refusal is at the shared consumption point for the library export and the CLI availability path. The third entry point is §9.

7. RULING 5 — NON-TEMPORAL MODE: REFUSE NOW, DO NOT BUILD

The unit is feature × affected output cohort; the non-temporal mode has no cohorts; building it means inventing a cohort identity the registration does not supply. R258 already ruled that: a gap the registration leaves is a registration finding, not a judgment call. The mode refuses with that reason, the schema and help surface say so, and the finding goes in the register. The mode selector has one live branch.

8. RULING 6 — THE DISCRIMINATING CONSTRUCTION, ASSERTED

The first construction ships: labels frame declared, so L3.1 runs over the leak and returns observed_silence, not none. Pin L3.1's verdict — if it ever starts catching this, the test says so, and that is information.

The correlation leg is asserted, not printed: with the seed fixed the fixture is deterministic, so assert the check returns no finding and print both statistics beside the threshold so the margin is visible. A printed number is not a pin.

Run it red first: horizon 60 s must produce the finding before horizon 0 s's clean result is believed. Held constant as you listed it; one declared scalar varies.

9. THE THIRD ENTRY POINT, AND THE FIVE FINDINGS

leakaudit check consumes a label and reaches no probe. The two L2a keys reaching it are classified in the complement guard as consumed-by-the-audit-path-only, with that reason; check neither refuses nor acts on them. An L2a key at any of the three entry points without a classification fails the guard.

The five registration findings go into NEXT_REGISTRATION_REQUIREMENTS.md itself, one line each with a pointer to L2A_ESTABLISH.md for the argument. If they are already there, say so. A finding that lives only in a round report is knowledge written where it governs nothing (R216 §6), and that is how a project loses what it already wrote down.

10. BUILD ORDER AND ROUND BOUNDARY

  1. §1, §2, §9 — cheap, one commit.
  2. §3(c) — L3.1's identity, before any L2a code. Its answer decides the round.
  3. §5, §6, §7 — keys, schema v4, refusals at the shared point, third-entry classification, non-temporal refusal. Each refusal shown to fire (R246: a refusal is an absence claim until a positive reddens it).
  4. Only if step 2 returned identity: the probe — §3(a)(b)(d), §4. Then §8's pair, red before green, L3.1 pinned, correlation asserted.
  5. Whole-frame guard if availability.py or any guarded module changed: 8-of-8 SAME or stop.
  6. Closing sequence, own invocations, push under the standing delegation.

If step 2 returned divergence, the round ends after step 3 with the disclosure.

11. HALT LIST — round-specific

Building L2a on moved_in_second · a mixed-band row folded into finding or silence · touching L3.1's attribution or cell selection · a stride not derived from the declared availability · label_column given a second job · an L2a key without a classification at any of the three entry points · the EvidenceOutcome enum touched · non-temporal mode built · the positive's L3.1 leg returning none · the correlation leg printed and not asserted · any L2a result quoted as a §6.2 result or placed beside Phase 1 figures without a line · a section number of mine acted on without resolving it on disk · a registration finding left only in the round report · a refusal shipped without its positive shown red.

12. REPORT FORMAT

§3(c)'s identity result first, one line, with its population (which cells, which inputs). Then step 1's three items. Then the keys and refusals, each positive shown red. Then the probe and the pair if built — both legs, L3.1's pin, the correlation margin. Then the close table. Then "what you must rule on."

DECISION 3:
  (a) L2a's attribution is the comparator above. Nothing else.
  (b) Batch the perturbation so every perturbed label cell in a batch shares ONE
      a(y). Then no row is ambiguous. If the machinery cannot do that cheaply, a
      row whose decision time falls between the batch's smallest and largest a(y)
      is a THIRD STATE — attribution ambiguous — reported as such, never folded
      into finding or observed_silence. Say which of the two you built.
  (c) L3.1 IS NOT TOUCHED THIS ROUND. Instead, establish before any L2a code:
      does every cell L3.1 perturbs have a(j) = F + 1 exactly?
        yes  -> moved_in_second IS the comparator on L3.1's domain. Record the
                identity in L2a's file header: two probes, one rule, one written
                as its special case. Continue to §10 step 3.
        no   -> name the cells and inputs where it is not. That is a Phase 1
                instrument disclosure: record it, repair nothing, stop after §10
                step 3, and report. The probe waits for a ruling.
  (d) Every finding carries its row — L3.1 or L2a — in the output, as findings
      already carry their detector. Confirm L2a's do. That makes §6.2's
      "runtime findings" ambiguity inert in the tool's own output; the registration
      finding stays recorded.

4. RULING 2 — THE STRIDE IS DERIVED

The stride is a consequence of a declared value, not a value about the world. It is D's padding floor again: derive it from the declared availability (horizon + delay + bucket), print it in ABOUT THIS RUN, and refuse only when the data cannot hold it — could_not_run(reason) with the numbers named (needed vs available). L3.1's one-second stride is the special case, and it is not touched.

5. RULING 3 — A NEW RAW-SIDE KEY, SCHEMA v4

Not an extension of label_column. Two reasons: one key with two jobs is the P0 shape (set it for one job, it silently governs the other), and label_column is the built output's and not registered vocabulary — extending it hands a registered job to an unregistered key. New key, named so the side is in the name; the schema text says which side each of the two label keys refers to. label_availability and the locator arrive together at schema version 4, one bump. leakaudit schema describes them only once they are consumed (R216 §5).

6. RULING 4 — REFUSAL SHAPE: THREE CASES, NOT TWO

The registration says absent inputs return unsupported, naming the missing element. Every shipped refusal raises. Both are right, for different cases:

DECISION 6:
  nothing L2a-specific declared
      -> the audit runs; L2a reports EvidenceOutcome `none` with the §8.2 state
         `unsupported(missing: <element>)` in the NOT PROBED block. Never a pass.
  any L2a key present, the set incomplete
      -> REFUSE (raise), naming the missing element. A partial declaration is
         evidence of intent; running past it makes the rest of the output look
         like the audit the user asked for.
  a value malformed
      -> REFUSE, as every shipped refusal does.

  The frozen EvidenceOutcome enum is not touched: `unsupported` is the §8.2 state
  attached to a `none`, the way NOT PROBED already does it. L2a's own result type
  carries it. If the state has to land at a point L3.1 shares, the whole-frame
  guard runs.
  If the registration's "absent" sentence reads as covering the partial case too,
  quote it: it becomes a §8.2 term question for NEXT_REGISTRATION_REQUIREMENTS,
  and the raise stands as a tool-level tightening (R203 permits those).

The refusal is at the shared consumption point for the library export and the CLI availability path. The third entry point is §9.

7. RULING 5 — NON-TEMPORAL MODE: REFUSE NOW, DO NOT BUILD

The unit is feature × affected output cohort; the non-temporal mode has no cohorts; building it means inventing a cohort identity the registration does not supply. R258 already ruled that: a gap the registration leaves is a registration finding, not a judgment call. The mode refuses with that reason, the schema and help surface say so, and the finding goes in the register. The mode selector has one live branch.

8. RULING 6 — THE DISCRIMINATING CONSTRUCTION, ASSERTED

The first construction ships: labels frame declared, so L3.1 runs over the leak and returns observed_silence, not none. Pin L3.1's verdict — if it ever starts catching this, the test says so, and that is information.

The correlation leg is asserted, not printed: with the seed fixed the fixture is deterministic, so assert the check returns no finding and print both statistics beside the threshold so the margin is visible. A printed number is not a pin.

Run it red first: horizon 60 s must produce the finding before horizon 0 s's clean result is believed. Held constant as you listed it; one declared scalar varies.

9. THE THIRD ENTRY POINT, AND THE FIVE FINDINGS

leakaudit check consumes a label and reaches no probe. The two L2a keys reaching it are classified in the complement guard as consumed-by-the-audit-path-only, with that reason; check neither refuses nor acts on them. An L2a key at any of the three entry points without a classification fails the guard.

The five registration findings go into NEXT_REGISTRATION_REQUIREMENTS.md itself, one line each with a pointer to L2A_ESTABLISH.md for the argument. If they are already there, say so. A finding that lives only in a round report is knowledge written where it governs nothing (R216 §6), and that is how a project loses what it already wrote down.

10. BUILD ORDER AND ROUND BOUNDARY

  1. §1(a)/(b), §1(c), §2, §9 — cheap, one commit.
  2. §3(c) — L3.1's identity, before any L2a code. Its answer decides the round.
  3. §5, §6, §7 — keys, schema v4, refusals at the shared point, third-entry classification, non-temporal refusal. Each refusal shown to fire (R246: a refusal is an absence claim until a positive reddens it).
  4. Only if step 2 returned identity: the probe — §3(a)(b)(d), §4. Then §8's pair, red before green, L3.1 pinned, correlation asserted.
  5. Whole-frame guard if availability.py or any guarded module changed: 8-of-8 SAME or stop.
  6. Closing sequence, own invocations, push under the standing delegation.

If step 2 returned divergence, the round ends after step 3 with the disclosure.

11. HALT LIST — round-specific

Building L2a on moved_in_second · a mixed-band row folded into finding or silence · touching L3.1's attribution or cell selection · a stride not derived from the declared availability · label_column given a second job · an L2a key without a classification at any of the three entry points · the EvidenceOutcome enum touched · non-temporal mode built · the positive's L3.1 leg returning none · the correlation leg printed and not asserted · any L2a result quoted as a §6.2 result or placed beside Phase 1 figures without a line · a section number of mine acted on without resolving it on disk · a registration finding left only in the round report · a refusal shipped without its positive shown red.

12. REPORT FORMAT

§3(c)'s identity result first, one line, with its population (which cells, which inputs). Then step 1's items, §1(c)'s one-line answer among them. Then the keys and refusals, each positive shown red. Then the probe and the pair if built — both legs, L3.1's pin, the correlation margin. Then the close table. Then "what you must rule on."

R2612026-09-09WHAT THE ROUND ESTABLISHED, AND WHAT IT LIFTS

Supersedes R116 through R260 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

The identity does not hold, and that decides the next two rounds. L3.1's "which second did it move in" rule equals the registered comparator only on the whole-frame path with a one-second window. Under a declared column_modes block, or any other window, it can lose findings — a real leak reported as observed_silence, the tool's own claim to have looked. Both inputs are accepted by the shipped loader today. The repair is ruled below; then L2a is built on the repaired rule.

0. WHAT THE ROUND ESTABLISHED, AND WHAT IT LIFTS

Measured, one-way, disclosed at D-V30A-98, nothing repaired: that is exactly the sequence the rules ask for. Two things follow.

  • R260's halt line "touching L3.1's attribution" was round-scoped — its job was to get the identity measured before anything moved. Measured. It is withdrawn by this ruling. The durable rule applies instead: a registered instrument is repaired once ruled, disclosed, tested against a known positive, and under the whole-frame guard.
  • Stopping after the disclosure rather than after step 3 was right, and step 3's position was my error. A declaration layer with no consumer is either a schema that lies or dead code. Keys ship with the probe that reads them (§4).

1. RULING — THE COMPARATOR REPLACES THE BUCKETS, ON BOTH ROWS

One rule, two probes. Exemption test: would this change be made if L2a did not exist? Yes — an attribution rule that is not the registered comparator on inputs the loader accepts is a defect on its own. Defect repair, ruled here.

DECISION 1 — the repair:
  (a) For a perturbed batch B (cells j, instants a(j)) and a moved output row i:
        d(i) <  min_B a(j)  -> FINDING   (unavailable for every perturbed cell)
        d(i) >= max_B a(j)  -> LIVENESS  (available for every perturbed cell —
                                          today's "next-second movement")
        otherwise           -> BAND      (a third state, named, never folded
                                          into either)
      Ties available, as registered. On the whole-frame path min = max, so the
      band is empty and the three classes are today's two.
  (b) The stride between probed cohorts derives from the batch's max a(j) − F,
      not from a fixed second; printed in ABOUT THIS RUN with the batch's
      [min, max] instants and the three counts. If cohorts are probed one at a
      time and the stride is only a sampling choice, say so — then (b) is a
      no-op and the print still lands.
  (c) The known positive is the one that failed: same frames, same cohort, the
      declared column mode. It reports observed_silence today and must report the
      finding after. Run it red first.
  (d) The positive DISCRIMINATES against the plausible wrong repair, which is one
      that over-reports the band. One fixture with two mid-second keys in a batch
      (say .3 and .7, instants F+1.3 and F+1.7): a row with d in [F+1, F+1.3) is a
      finding; a row in [F+1.3, F+1.7) is BAND; a row at or after F+1.7 is
      liveness. Three assertions, one fixture.
  (e) The whole-frame guard runs. 8-of-8 SAME on the Phase 1 pair, or stop: the
      whole-frame path with a one-second window must be bit-identical, because
      that is where the identity holds and where every published figure lives.
  (f) One-way is preserved and asserted: on the whole-frame path the repair adds
      no finding and removes none — that is (e). On the per-column path it adds
      findings only on rows in [F + 1, a(j)); a test names that population.

2. THE STOPGAP, ONLY IF THE REPAIR DOES NOT LAND

If (e) is not SAME, or anything in §1 halts, the tree does not stay as it is: the shipped loader accepts two inputs under which the probe's silence is wrong.

DECISION 2:
  repair landed                  -> nothing here.
  repair did not land this round -> the probe path REFUSES a declared
      column_modes block and any window_seconds other than 1.0, naming
      D-V30A-98 and what would lift the refusal. Refuse-don't-default; it is
      the same P0 shape. Shown to fire, then the round ends with that.

3. TWO THINGS THE DISCLOSURE STILL NEEDS

The absence claim is half-populated. "No Phase 1 figure moves" was shown for column_modes (zero files under evidence/phase1/). The second input is window_seconds. Same check: every Phase 1 run's window, from the run record, not from memory.

DECISION 3.1:
  every Phase 1 run is at window 1.0 (or the record shows the whole-frame path
  with a one-second window)
      -> the claim stands with its population complete; one line in D-V30A-98.
  any run is not
      -> that run's attribution is under the divergence. D-V30A-98 gains the
         run's name and the direction (one-way: findings possibly lost, none
         invented). Nothing re-run this round.

R206's reading is suspended. R206 §1 read "whole-frame 25 of 25, per-column 0 of 25" as the coarse path reported leakage that was not there. The geometry can produce a per-column zero while the comparator disagrees, so that reading is no longer supported by its own measurement. Until re-measured under the repaired rule, it is not quoted. Where it was recorded, add one line pointing at D-V30A-98. Re-measure it after the repair, same inputs, both paths — that result is what replaces the reading, whichever way it goes.

4. L2a — AFTER THE REPAIR, ON THE SAME RULE

R260's six rulings stand unchanged: attribution is the comparator (now §1's shared rule); stride derived; a new raw-side key, schema v4, keys shipped WITH the probe; refusal in three cases (nothing declared → unsupported on a none; partial → refuse; malformed → refuse); non-temporal mode refuses with its reason; the discriminating construction ships, L3.1 pinned observed_silence, correlation asserted with its margin printed; the third entry point classified in the complement guard; every finding carries its row.

L2a is built only after §1 closes green. Same round if it does; next round if not.

5. THE BASELINE WRITER IS A DEFECT

A baseline keyed to a work root that is replaced wholesale when the root changes loses the record of what was read under the old one. "Nothing checkable was lost" is true today and will not be true the day the old root is mounted again.

DECISION 5 — bounded:
  (a) Entries carry their root; accepting an increment under root B never touches
      root A's entries. Merge, never replace.
  (b) The baseline file is tracked
        -> restore the 738 from the last commit where the file held them, as
           root-A entries beside the six.
      it is not tracked
        -> record the loss, with the count, where the baseline is documented.
  (c) Nothing else in that instrument changes this round.

6. THE MANIFEST LINE — leave it out, record the tension

Do not touch the ../ set; it is the ceremony's, and the frozen checker's counts sit on it. The tension is real — the file admitted for coverage alone binds nothing, and the file that binds the work is outside — and it is a finding about the registration set, not about this tree. One line in NEXT_REGISTRATION_REQUIREMENTS.md. Git history is the rules file's attestation until then.

The repair landing without §1(c) shown red first · a band row folded into finding or liveness · a stride still fixed at one second after the repair · the guard not 8-of-8 SAME and the repair kept · the tree left accepting column_modes or a non-unit window with the buckets still in force · R206's reading quoted before the re-measurement · the window check answered from memory · the baseline replaced again · a seventh ../ entry · L2a code before §1 closes green · any L2a result quoted as a §6.2 result or beside Phase 1 figures without a line · a section number of mine acted on without resolving it on disk.

R2622026-09-09THE PUSH BACKLOG — a standing rule that was not running

Supersedes R116 through R261 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

0. THE PUSH BACKLOG — a standing rule that was not running

The push range said it: a93b82d..49dda6b, thirty-one commits. The remote sat at R236's commit while twenty-nine rounds of work stayed on one disk. The standing delegation says push at the end of any round where commits landed; through R259 the remote stayed where it was and no report said "not pushed". That is the discipline failure, named as the rule requires.

Two causes, one each side. Mine: the continuation rule I wrote at R258 lists the closing sequence as "suite, certification, commit, report" — no push. A rule that omits a step licenses omitting it. Yours: the range git printed was reported without asking what its left-hand side meant, and you said so.

Awareness is not the fix; a mechanism is. §1 carries it.

1. THREE RULES INTO OPERATING_RULES.md — add them, this delta is the word

DECISION 1:
  (a) The closing sequence is: suite, certification, commit, push, REMOTE AT
      HEAD, report. "Remote at head" is its own step — `git rev-parse origin/main`
      equals HEAD, read as a fact, not inferred from the push's exit. The close
      table carries it as a row. A round that ends with the remote behind says
      so in the report's first line.
  (b) Correct the continuation rule's text to that sequence. Same commit.
  (c) The complexity rule, as you stated it: a correctness suite on toy data
      cannot see a complexity regression; the instruments that run at fixture
      scale are the only complexity instruments here, and they report by not
      returning. Mechanism, not vigilance: every instrument that runs at scale
      prints its wall time in its own output (frame with the figure, R228), and
      a run exceeding the last recorded time by an order of magnitude is stopped
      and looked at, not waited out. Eighteen hours was the cost of the absence.

2. D-V30A-100 — REPAIR THE VERDICT. It is the vocabulary Phase 2 rests on.

observed_silence was returned where nothing relevant was probed. none is not observed_silence; that sentence is the definition of done. Phase 1 already had the licence: the corrected side's silence was believed because 250 liveness movements proved the perturbation reached the pipeline.

DECISION 2:
  (a) The verdict emits observed_silence only when liveness > 0 (or band > 0).
      Findings 0, liveness 0, band 0 -> `none`, with the reason: no perturbed
      cell reached the pipeline. The reason names the population — cells
      perturbed, and where their instants sat relative to the probed range.
  (b) Known positive: R205's per-column case. Today observed_silence; after,
      `none` with that reason. Red first.
  (c) Discriminates: the Phase 1 corrected side stays observed_silence (250
      liveness). A repair that turned every zero-finding run into `none` moves
      it; this one must not.
  (d) Guard: 8-of-8 SAME, or stop. It touches a probe-path file and that is the
      price; the twelve-row suite cannot license this change and the guard can.

3. L2a's SILENCE — what licenses it for a stranger?

The pair licenses L2a's silence in the test: the clean half re-runs the leaking half and confirms the label cells are read. A stranger's pipeline has no leaking half. So: when L2a reports observed_silence on a pipeline it has never seen, what proves the perturbation reached anything? If the answer is nothing, that is D-V30A-100's shape inside the new probe, one round old.

DECISION 3 — establish, then act in the same round:
  (a) State what L2a's verdict is gated on today. Cells actually perturbed per
      cohort? The locator resolving to a real column? Anything?
  (b) Gate it, at least, on perturbed-cells > 0 for the cohort, with the count
      printed per cohort. Zero perturbed -> `none`, reason named — same rule as
      §2, one probe over. (A clean pipeline need not read labels as features at
      all, so a moved-row liveness class is not available to L2a the way it is
      to L3.1; say that in the output, so the reader knows which licence the
      silence carries.)
  (c) Known positive: a locator pointing at a column whose instants sit outside
      the probed range — the R205 geometry, on the label side. Today's verdict,
      then `none`.
  (d) Nine finding cohorts of ten at sixty seconds: name the silent one and why.
      A stated reason beats a silent narrowing.

label_probe.py was placed outside the set by reading imports. The set was built by a trace. Re-run the trace; membership is what it returns. The shared classifier is on-path (the guard already fired on it); label_probe.py is wherever the trace puts it. Record the result in PROBE_PATH_SET.json's provenance. No by-hand placement, in either direction.

5. ITEM 7(vi) — already ruled

R260 §6 pre-ruled it: quote the sentence, record the §8.2 term gap, the refusal stands as a tool-level tightening. You did exactly that. Nothing further.

6. BANKED, IN ONE PLACE

The repair (D-V30A-98 → shared classifier, guard SAME twice, one-way asserted with its population); the window claim completed by parsing, not grepping (D-V30A-99, which also records that run records do not carry the window — that is a frame gap, and every run record gains the window and the path from here); the baseline writer merging per root with its limit stated where it is paid; R205's zero reclassified as a probe that did not happen (D-V30A-100); L2a shipped with three instruments catching it and each given a classification (D-V30A-101). The closing sequence without the remote-at-head row · the verdict repair landing without §2(b) red first · a zero-finding, zero-liveness run reported as observed_silence anywhere, either probe · L2a's silence unlicensed and unlabelled in the output · a probe-path membership decided by hand · a wall time missing from any at-scale instrument's output · C code before its establish is ruled · any Phase 2 result quoted as a §6.2 result or beside Phase 1 figures without a line · a section number of mine acted on without resolving it on disk.

2. THE SHARED RESIDUAL — measure the reach instead of declaring it away

Two features now carry the same sentence: clearing the floor is not sufficiency, because the builder's lookback is not in the model. D's padding and the stride floor both stop where the declaration stops. But this tool's whole claim is that runtime perturbation measures what declarations cannot. The builder's reach is exactly such a quantity.

DECISION 2 — establish, then build if (a) holds:
  (a) Reach: perturb one probed second F in a clean build, rebuild once, and take
      the largest d(i) − F over every row that moved. That is how far forward a
      corruption of F propagates through THIS builder — the lookback, measured
      from behaviour. State whether the existing machinery can do it in one
      rebuild per sampled second.
  (b) What it bounds. The stride must exceed the measured reach; the padding
      must exceed it too. Both residuals become one measured number with one
      stated limit: k sampled seconds give a lower bound on reach, and a lookback
      that showed in none of k samples is the residual that remains. Say k, and
      why that k.
  (c) Cost: k rebuilds at 34.6 s each on the fixture. If k = 3 that is under two
      minutes, once per audit.
  (d) If (a) holds: build it as a control that runs before the probes, prints
      the measured reach and k in ABOUT THIS RUN, and refuses a declared stride
      or padding at or below it — naming the measurement, so the refusal says
      "your stride is 97 and this builder reaches 120" rather than quoting a
      formula. The residual sentence stays in both places, shortened to what k
      samples leave open.
  If (a) does not hold cheaply, report why and both sentences stand as they are.

3. C — RULED. Quick is a budget on the row that costs, not a mode.

L3.1's cohorts cost ~0.02 s; L2a's cost a build each. So:

DECISION 3:
  (a) L3.1 always runs every eligible cohort. There is nothing to save.
  (b) "Quick" is an L2a COHORT BUDGET: a count the user declares, with a default
      that is a cost choice — printed as "default N", exactly as stride 97 is —
      chosen so the default run on the fixture stays under about ten minutes,
      with the arithmetic in the record (build time + N × per-cohort). The
      cohorts are chosen by a derived stride over the eligible set, so the run
      is deterministic and reproducible; never random without a printed seed.
      The stride floor applies to it like any stride.
  (c) Coverage is REPORTED, never thresholded. DESIGN's two-number table exists
      after this round: cohorts probed of eligible, and output rows in probed
      cohorts of all rows. Those two numbers are the population of every
      silence the run reports. No level is required — a level is a threshold,
      and thresholds get adjusted toward.
  (d) Exit codes: silent over a subsample is its own class. Complete and silent,
      finding, refused, and INCOMPLETE-AND-SILENT are four distinct exits.
      Incomplete never exits as complete. A CI user who accepts partial coverage
      declares it — one flag, named for what it accepts — and only then does the
      incomplete class map to the clean exit, with the acceptance printed. A
      declared acceptance, not a default.
  (e) DESIGN's assert_audit_complete(): build its equivalent in the library, the
      same rule as (d) at the second entry point — raises on incomplete unless
      acceptance is passed. Name it from DESIGN if the name still fits.

      read it. DESIGN's sentence gets a note saying the registration overrides
      it on that point; DESIGN is revisable, the registration is not.
  Known positives: a run at budget 5 of 72 exits incomplete; with acceptance
  declared it exits clean and prints the acceptance; at budget >= 72 it exits
  complete. A positive pair around the boundary, cohorts held constant.

R2682026-09-12TWO RULES BROKEN IN ONE COMMAND — the mechanism

Supersedes R116 through R267 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

The reach control worked on its first run, and the first thing it caught was this project: the slice pair's thirty findings were thirty overlapping claims from a builder that reaches sixty seconds, probed two seconds apart. R264 called that pair "confirmed" and I accepted it. Three rulings follow from the round: a mechanism for the two rules broken in one command, the coverage accounting — where I disagree with the change you made — and what the guard carries now.

0. BANKED, AND THREE ERRORS OF MINE

Banked: suite-tree certification with its positive fired for real; reach measured (59.5 s recovered against a known 60 s; 14 s on the acceptance fixture, k=3, none censored; censoring only under-reports, so the max is a sound lower bound); the guard SAME with reach on the path by trace; TB-25's duplicate resolved forward to TB-28 with nothing renumbered; the tie row in its cohort, zero +1 ns siblings; the suite-tree off-by-one caught by its own output and pinned. D-V30A-108.

Mine, three:

  1. R267 §3(a): "L3.1 always runs every eligible cohort — there is nothing to save." Wrong. L3.1 is cheap per cohort because it batches, and batching needs the stride above the reach. One pass at stride 97 covers one second in ninety-seven. Cheap per cohort is not the same as able to probe every cohort.
  2. R267 §2(c): 34.6 s per reach rebuild. That was the clean build. A reach rebuild is 83.9 s. Off by 2.4×, from reusing a figure for a different thing.
  3. R264 §2(b), accepted at R265: "one finding per probed cohort at both strides is what a real leak in every second looks like." It is also exactly what interference looks like when the lookback spans every cohort. The discriminating measurement was the reach, and neither layer had it. The disclosure carries that retraction in those words.

1. TWO RULES BROKEN IN ONE COMMAND — the mechanism

-m instead of -F from a file, and backticks in a shell argument, in the round whose subject is mechanisms over discipline. The message landed intact by luck. The commit stays as it is — an amended commit would erase the record, as at 03b0c6f.

DECISION 1:
  (a) A commit-msg hook, in a TRACKED hooks directory, with core.hooksPath set to
      it. The hook refuses any message that lacks the trailer safe_edit's commit
      path writes. A message that came through the tool came from a file; a
      message that did not is refused before it lands. That closes -m, and it
      closes backticks in commit messages with it, since a file never passes
      through the shell.
  (b) certify_preconditions gains the step: core.hooksPath resolves to the
      tracked directory and the hook is executable. A clone without it cannot
      certify. That is what makes a per-clone setting stick.
  (c) Known positive: git commit -m "x" -> refused, shown.
  (d) Backticks in other shell arguments stay a rule; no hook sees a shell. Say
      so in the rule's own text rather than letting the hook imply more than it
      covers.

2. THE SLICE PAIR, AFTER THE REACH

"Fixed to the registered default, one cohort per side" is a change, not a result. Report the pair's verdicts now: the padded side and the cut side, one cohort each, with the reach printed. A real sixty-second lookback cut by an unpadded slice should still show in one cohort; if it does not, say what the one cohort sees and why. The record for D keeps 30/30 and 15/15 as dated figures, superseded, with the sentence: both were produced at a stride thirty times under the builder's measured reach, and each finding overlapped the next.

3. COVERAGE — the denominator, and where I disagree

You found that counting stride-excluded seconds made every run incomplete, and changed the denominator because "a class that fires always distinguishes nothing." I rule the other way. A default run at stride 97 probes one second in ninety-seven. Its silence is incomplete, and the class that says so is distinguishing the default run from a complete one — which is the distinction the whole feature exists to make. A note beside a clean exit is one shade from a pass (R220 §4); an exit code is not.

DECISION 3:
  (a) The denominator is every cohort the declared model makes probe-able,
      independent of stride and budget. Stride-excluded seconds are UNPROBED and
      counted. State the definition on disk as it now stands, then apply this.
  (b) The table has THREE states, for cohorts and for rows: probed /
      eligible-but-unprobed / ineligible under the declared model. The demo's
      "2 of 1200 rows" needs the third column: a run that is complete over 13
      cohorts must not read as covering 1,200 rows.
  (c) Incomplete-and-silent fires on every default run. That is correct. The two
      honest routes to the clean exit are the declared acceptance (built) and a
      COMPLETE run — which does not exist yet, and is (d).
  (d) Complete, for L3.1: PASSES at offsets. The reach control gives the minimum
      safe stride — measured reach plus the resolution the selection floors
      away. A complete run is that many passes, each probing every stride-th
      second at a different offset, each its own rebuild. On the fixture: 14 s
      reach -> stride 15 -> 15 passes at about three minutes each. Establish
      the cost, then build `--complete` (or the name DESIGN uses) for L3.1;
      for L2a complete is already every eligible cohort at a build each. The
      budget for L3.1 is passes; for L2a, cohorts; both printed.
  (e) The budget default: confirm 16 is what the tree holds, with the arithmetic
      beside it, and 25 gone.

4. THE GUARD CARRIES REACH — keep it on, do not compare it

969 s per probe-path change is the price of the guard running what a user runs. Keep reach on in the guard; do not disable it there. 2. THE REACH WAS FOR THIS — the plain-frame slice that masks a leak

The cut side of D's pair is none because the builder emits NaN over a window shorter than its lookback. That is the polite failure. The dangerous one is a builder that emits values from a partial window (min_periods=1, or any fill): features exist, in-frame cells move rows — liveness — and the leaked cells sit before the frame's first row, never perturbed. Verdict: observed_silence over a real leak. The liveness gate does not catch it, and the slice refusal was stated at R255 to cover declared slices only, because a plain frame carries no declaration of what it was cut from.

It carries a measurement now. Reach is the lookback: a row at d reads back to d − reach. Rows in the first reach seconds of any frame read cells before the frame exists.

DECISION 2:

      declared padding against the MEASURED reach, not only the model's floor —

      ineligible — "lookback exceeds the frame's head; cells before the frame
      cannot be probed" — never as observed_silence. They count in the table's
      ineligible column with that reason, distinct from model-ineligible.
  (c) Known positive, discriminating: a partial-window builder on a cut frame
      whose only leaked cells lie before the frame. Today: observed_silence with
      liveness. After: the head rows `none` with the reason, and the verdict
      over the remaining rows whatever it is. The pair holds the builder and
      frame constant and varies only the cut. That is the headline masking
      case, caught by measurement instead of by a declaration nobody made.
  (d) Reach is a lower bound from k samples; say so in the reason, and the
      residual sentence that remains is "a lookback that showed in none of k

This touches probe-path files. It is this round's one batch, with §1.

3. E's TENSION — ruled now, so the next establish needs no ask

Domain profiles are defaults, and this tool refuses defaults for anything about the world. Resolution: a profile is a named declaration, not a default. The user names it — --profile <name> — and every value it supplies is printed in ABOUT THIS RUN as "from profile <name>", per key. Nothing fills silently; the user's act is naming the profile, and the print makes each filled value theirs to see. A profile never supplies a decision column or a decision frame — those stay required. That is the rule E is built under, next round, establish first.

1. THE CORRECTED SIDE'S FINDING — isolate it, do not re-run it blind

Two readings, as you stated them: leaks in cohorts the 1-in-997 sample never touched, or interference at a stride one second above a reach that is only a lower bound from three samples. A batched finding and an interference finding differ in exactly one way: the real one survives being probed alone.

DECISION 1:
  (a) The instrument: ISOLATION RE-PROBE. Take one finding cohort, rebuild with
      that cohort's cells perturbed and nothing else, classify with the shared
      rule. No other cohort in the batch, so no interference is possible by
      construction. One rebuild per cohort.
  (b) Known positive first, on the contaminated side: pick five finding cohorts
      from the guard's 5,220 records, deterministically, and re-probe each
      alone. Real leaks must persist. If any vanishes, the instrument is wrong
      and the round stops there.

      cohorts choose up to twenty, deterministically (stated how), and re-probe

        all persist       -> reading one. The corrected builder leaks in cohorts

                             not correction.
        all vanish        -> reading two. Interference at stride 16. Measure the
                             reach at those cohorts (k more samples, there) and

                             optional.
        mixed             -> both, and the split is the result. Report the two
                             populations separately with their locations.
  (d) Where the findings sit is recorded whichever way: cohort, feature, count,
      and whether they cluster in time. That is the population the reading
      rests on, and last time it was not kept.

2. COMPLETE MODE'S SAFETY, AND THE FEATURE THIS BECOMES

Stride = reach + 1 s is the minimum, and the reach is a lower bound. A complete run protects an hour of machine time with a fourteen-minute measurement's worth of samples; that ratio is wrong.

DECISION 2:

The rule I owed is §2 below, and it is a measurement rather than a margin, because a margin is a number nobody measured.

1. TWO CHEAP CHECKS BEFORE ANYTHING IS BUILT

DECISION 1:
  (a) The ten-minute check: at the five cohorts, corrupt the earlier neighbour
      ALONE (not F). Row F moves -> the neighbour's reach is 16 s boundary-
      inclusive and the 0.3 ms clearance was the cause. Row F does not move ->
      accumulation: two corruptions inside one window move a row neither
      moves alone. Report which. §2 is built either way; (a) decides what the
      disclosure says the mechanism was.

2. BLOCK REACH — the window, measured, and it governs every stride

The reach control corrupts one second and asks how far the output moves. A feature that sums, thresholds, bins or decays answers "as far as one second's worth of corruption can push it," which is less than its window. A batched pass puts several corruptions inside the window, and the window is what interferes.

DECISION 2 — establish on the corrected fixture, then build:
  (a) BLOCK REACH: corrupt every modelled cell at or before F — the probe's own
      column set, its own corruption — rebuild once, take the largest d(i) − F
      over moved rows. That is the longest lookback any feature has into the
      past, from behaviour. One rebuild. If a whole-history block breaks the
      build (shape guard, types), fall back to a long block — say 3,600 s —
      and state the bound that gives instead.
  (b) On the corrected fixture the expectation is ~60 s. Report the number
      beside the single-second reach (15.9997 s) and beside §1(b)'s source
      read. Three numbers, one row.
  (c) The stride floor becomes max(model floor, block reach + 1 s), for EVERY
      run — default runs included, because a stranger's five-minute feature at
      stride 97 is the same defect. Cost: one rebuild per audit, printed. The
      default 97 stays the sampling default when it clears the floor; below
      it, the floor is used and printed, as the rule already says.
  (d) --complete uses passes at that stride. On the corrected fixture that is
      ~61 passes, ~3.5 h; time one pass, print the prediction, and put the
      figure in the record. If the block reach is longer than the frame can
      hold passes for — an EWM feature can reach for hours — --complete
      REFUSES with the number and says what unbatched would cost. Honest is
      better than a mode that lies at exit 1.
  (e) The residual sentence shrinks to what the block cannot see: a feature
      whose response to a whole-history corruption is below resolution, and a
      lookback that showed in none of k sampled block positions. Say k.
  (f) Known positive: the corrected fixture at the new stride, one pass, must
      be silent; at stride 16 it produced 163,143 findings. That pair is the
      instrument's positive and it goes in the suite at fixture scale, marked
      by cost, run once here and recorded.

Until (c) lands, --complete REFUSES, naming D-V30A-114 and what lifts it. Your recommendation, adopted: a mode that turns a clean builder into exit 1 does not ship with a warning.

3. --confirm — the split, the classes, the cap

Isolation removes a real lookahead leak as surely as it removes interference: a row at F reading a later cohort's unavailable cells moves in the batch and not alone. The earlier/later split is what told the two apart, so it is the instrument.

DECISION 3:
  (a) A batched-only finding is re-probed twice more: with the batch's LATER
      cohorts only, and with its EARLIER cohorts only.
        later reproduces   -> CONFIRMED (lookahead): a real leak; name the
                              later second, unavailable to the row.
        earlier reproduces -> INTERFERENCE: available cells, not a leak.
        neither            -> BATCHED ONLY, as now.
  (b) An interference class in a run is a fact about the run's stride, not
      about one finding: the run's silences are unlicensed. They are reported
      as `none` with the reason "interference detected at stride N; block
      reach M", and the run's exit is the refused class, with confirmed
      findings still listed — they are real regardless.
  (c) The cap derives from the same 600 s cost choice as C's default: cap =
      what fits, at the measured per-confirm cost (108 s here → 5), printed
      as "default cap 5 (600 s target)". Chosen by rank across the findings
      as now. A user raises it; the prediction prints before the re-probes
      run.

0. BANKED, AND MY ERROR

Mine: R271 §2 explained interference as several corruptions summing inside a window and built a theory of thresholds and decays on it. The number it explained was wrong, not subtle. I did not ask whether the instrument had perturbed the frame the feature reads. That question is now a rule, below.

1. EVERY PERTURBING INSTRUMENT PRINTS WHAT IT PERTURBED — one entry point

L2a got this at R262: perturbed-cells > 0 per cohort, printed, or none. Reach did not have it and reported 14 s over zero trades cells.

DECISION 1:
  (a) ONE corruption entry point. Every instrument that perturbs cells — probe
      A, L2a, single-second reach, block reach, isolation, the later/earlier
      split — selects and corrupts through it. It counts cells corrupted per
      declared frame and returns the counts with the corrupted frames.
  (b) The entry point selects by time through the shared decision-clock
      alignment only, and REFUSES a comparison between aware and naive stamps
      — raises, never all-False. That is the defect, closed at the one place
      it can recur.
  (c) A sampled position at which a declared frame contributes zero corrupted
      cells is reported as such; a declared frame that contributes zero at
      EVERY sampled position makes the measurement `none` for that frame,
      never a number. Printed per frame in every run.
  (d) Totality: a test enumerates every site that selects cells by time and
      every site that corrupts, and fails if any does not go through (a) —
      the decision-clock-consumer pattern, floor over tracked plus untracked.
  (e) Known positive: the R270 reach configuration re-run through (a) reports
      "trades: 0 cells at 10 of 10 positions" and refuses to print a reach for
      trades. Red first on the old code path if it still exists; otherwise the
      unit test constructs the aware/naive pair and asserts the raise.

2. THE SEVEN QUESTIONS, RULED

DECISION 2:
  (a) "The demo" was the two-CSV stranger pipeline of the CLI measurement at
      R261/R268 — my label, not a name on disk. If it survives as a fixture,
      report its floor; if it was ad hoc, no figure, and say so.
  (b) Head of frame uses the BLOCK reach. A robust statistic can ignore one
      corrupted second and still read sixty; the head cutoff must not.
  (c) Reach is reported in ROWS and in seconds. State on disk which unit the
      pass stride uses; the floor compares like with like — a rows reach
      against a positions stride, the model's seconds floor converted at the
      frame's smallest row spacing. One test with an overnight gap: a 60-row
      window across the gap, a stride in seconds would interfere, a stride in
      rows must not.
  (d) --confirm is two stages, each predicted before it runs. Stage one:
      isolation, capped by the 600 s target as now. Stage two: the split, on
      every finding that vanished in stage one, up to the same cap, its own
      prediction printed ("N vanished; split ~M min"). A vanished finding left
      unsplit is the worst outcome, so stage two is never silently skipped;
      above the cap it is NOT RE-PROBED with the count.
  (e) Interference gets its OWN exit code — it is not a usage error, it is the
      run discovering its stride was wrong. Precedence, stated in the CLI's
      help: refused > interference > finding > incomplete > clean. Confirmed
      findings are still listed under an interference exit; the run is still
      to be re-done at the stride the message names.
  (f) The R268–R270 cost figures (54.7 min, 61.2 min, 16 passes, and the 15/16-
      second reaches) are marked superseded, dated, beside the new ones, with
      the sentence: produced by a reach that corrupted one frame of two.
  (g) A mechanism for D-V30A-117, yes — and symmetric:
        - the suite run records a fingerprint of the WORKING tree it ran on
          (HEAD plus the content hashes of every modified and untracked
          non-ignored file), not HEAD alone;
        - safe_edit.commit computes the same fingerprint and REFUSES when no
          suite record matches it. Fifty-two seconds per commit is the price
          and it is the right one;
        - a commit touching a path-set file also needs a guard record with a
          matching fingerprint, or it is refused. The guard's times file
          gains the fingerprint.
      Known positives: commit without a matching suite run -> refused;
      probe-path commit without a matching guard run -> refused. Records-only
      commits get the suite too; the suite reads the records.

The suite in the closing sequence runs unpiped, and the runner records its own wall time; 600 s against 52 s was the pipe, and the 10× rule caught it.

Supersedes R116 through R272 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

The commit gate refused twice on the real repository before accepting, one corruption entry point now counts every cell every instrument perturbs, and the gap test showed why reach has to be in rows. Nine questions came back; they are ruled below, one of them against the change as made. Then E's establish, which has waited four rounds and gets the rest of this one.

0. BANKED

The two gate refusals shown live and pinned in a throwaway repo; the totality population named (five call shapes, two selecting-and-corrupting sites, two allowed with reasons, seven routed); the aware/naive raise both ways; the fixture positive reading trades at 5 of 10 where the old copy read 0, reach 60 s and 60 rows; head on the block reach; the gap test — 60 rows across nine hours, five rows apart interfering, 61 positions silent, 40 refused; two-stage confirm with both predictions; interference at exit 5 with the precedence printed; the guard SAME with the path-set fingerprint matching HEAD; "the demo" resolved to scratch and no figure claimed; the superseded figures carrying their sentence.

1. THE NINE, RULED

DECISION 1:
  (a) Mixed-timezone keys: CONVERT UNDER A DECLARATION, otherwise REFUSE. An
      aware key aligned to a naive decision clock assumes the naive clock's
      zone, and a zone is a fact about the world. Where the model declares the
      decision clock's zone, the alignment is exact and converts; where it does
      not, the shared alignment refuses naming the key that would settle it. A
      timezone mismatch is itself a classic leak, and this tool does not guess
      it. The fixture's declaration gains the key as an as-built fact; the
      schema bumps; the complement guard classifies it. That is how D-V30A-42
      settles — not in the probe's favour unconditionally, in the
      declaration's.
  (b) corruption.corrupt (the column probe): IN for the counting half. It
      perturbs cells, so it reports cells corrupted per frame and returns
      `none` on zero. Its selection is by column, not time, so the alignment
      half does not apply; the allow-list says so as its reason.
  (c) The model floor's exact time-gap check: accepted, with the absence claim
      shown — one line from the code or the gap fixture that there is no input
      the exact check accepts and the converted one would refuse.
  (d) The split's NOT RE-PROBED branch is dead by construction (vanished <=
      isolated <= cap). Remove it; assert the invariant in a test; no second
      cap. A vanished finding is never left unsplit, as ruled.
  (e) Exit precedence as you placed it: 2 > 5 > 1 > 3 > 4 > 0. Nothing probed
      outranks incomplete. Confirmed.
  (f) ReachResult.note()'s "censored" wording: next batch, one line in the
      backlog now.
  (g) §1(e)'s positive: the unit test, the synthetic frame, and the fixture's
      5-of-10 together are sufficient. Confirmed.
  (h) Export shadowing (G): the function loses the name. `from leakaudit import
      availability` returns the module, as Python's own import would. The
      function is renamed to something that says what it does; no alias, since
      an alias named `availability` shadows the module again. Pre-1.0 and the
      CLI is the stranger's surface; the rename goes in INSTALL's changes
      section. Theo may veto this in chat; absent that, it ships.
  (i) E's establish is §2.

2. E — DOMAIN PROFILES: establish, no code

Under R269 §3's rule: a profile is a named declaration the user invokes, every value it supplies is printed per key as "from profile <name>", and it never supplies the decision column or the decision frame.

DECISION 2 — report and stop:
  (a) What DESIGN says a profile is, cited from disk, and every key the
      registration's declared model has that a profile could fill. Two lists.
  (b) Which of those keys are ABOUT THE WORLD (availability, zones, delays,
      horizons) and which are STRUCTURAL. A profile may fill either, but the
      world-facing ones are the reason the print exists.
  (c) The two profiles the fixture itself implies — the contaminated and the
      corrected declarations — written as profiles, and whether a stranger
      with CME data would want either. If the answer is that no profile is
      general enough to ship, that is a finding, not a failure.
  (d) Refusals: a profile naming a key the schema does not have; a profile
      value overridden by an explicit declaration (explicit wins, and the
      print says so); a profile supplying decision_column or the frame.
  (e) The complement guard's view: profile keys are consumed by the loader
      and classified like any key.

3. BUILD ORDER AND ROUND BOUNDARY

  1. §1(a)(b)(d)(f-record)(h) — one batch of probe-path edits. §1(c)'s line.
  2. One guard run. SAME or nothing is committed.
  3. §2 — the establish, a read.
  4. Closing sequence, remote at head.

4. HALT LIST — round-specific

An aware key aligned without a declared clock zone · the column probe left outside the counting half · the split's dead branch left in without its invariant asserted · an alias named availability · E code before its establish is ruled · a second guard run inside the round · any Phase 2 result quoted as a §6.2 result or beside Phase 1 figures without a line · a section number of mine acted on without resolving it on disk.

5. REPORT FORMAT

First line: remote at head, yes or no, with the hash. Then §1(a): the refusal shown without the declaration, the conversion shown with it, the fixture's key. Then (b)(c)(d)(h) as landed. Then the guard's eight terms, reach in both units on both sides, wall time. Then §2's five parts. Then the close table. Then "what you must rule on."

2. E — BUILD IT AS A MECHANISM FOR THE USER'S OWN PROFILES

      carrying ONLY world-facing keys that have a consumer today:

      exists — the complement guard would rightly call them read-and-ignored.

      every key the profile supplied prints in ABOUT THIS RUN as

      (<its value>)". Nothing fills silently.

      carrying decision_column, any frame, raw_label, label_column, split or
      label_availability — its own message, not the generic one; a profile
      path that does not resolve; a profile at the wrong schema version.
  (d) The complement guard: --profile and each profile key are their own
      population, each in one of the three states. A totality test: the set of
      keys a profile filled equals the set printed "from profile".
  (e) One TEMPLATE ships — a documented example of the four keys — named as a
      template, not as a domain. It is the only profile in the repository.
  (f) Known positives beyond (c): a run with a profile and no overrides prints
      four "from profile" lines; the same run with one explicit key prints
      three and one "overriding"; a run without --profile prints none.

1. THE SANCTIONED PATH FOR CAPTURING A RUN

Every slip against the shell rule this project has recorded had a real need behind it, and this one was "capture both streams and the exit of a run." No tool offered that, so the shell did.

DECISION 1:
  tools/capture_run.py: runs a command via subprocess with no shell, writes
  stdout, stderr and the exit code to three named files through Python, prints
  the byte counts. It is the way to capture a run, and OPERATING_RULES' shell
  rule gains one sentence pointing at it. Known positive: a command that
  writes to both streams and exits 3 produces three files with those contents.

2. CRITERION 5 ON A MACHINE NOBODY HERE CONFIGURED

"Installable by a stranger" has been measured from a wheel in a fresh venv — on vengeance, by the agent that built it. The registration's deadline is 15 October. A machine that has never seen this repository is one workflow away.

DECISION 2:
  (a) A GitHub Actions workflow, tracked: on push to main, build the wheel with
      tools/build_wheel.py, install it into a fresh venv, run README's five
      lines against the walk's small CSV pair, and ASSERT the exit contract —
      the leaky demo exits 1, the clean demo exits 4, the clean demo with
      --accept-partial-coverage exits 0, a misspelt key exits 2. A green run is
      the contract holding on a clean machine; a red run names which exit

Structurally impossible — a dependence across a time boundary is a dependence on a later cell, which is what L3.1 detects. The R215 rule is that a known positive must discriminate; the discriminating case here is not "L3.1 silent" but "L3.1's SAMPLE silent", and §2 builds it.

2. THE PROBE'S VALUE, STATED EXACTLY, WITH THE PAIR THAT SHOWS IT

Your sentence is the true one: the probe does not depend on where a sampled stride lands — one rebuild, exactly the test side, exactly the training rows. A global scaler moves every row at every sampled second, so L3.1 at any stride finds it too. A NARROW dependence does not.

  (a) The discriminating pair: a training output that depends on ONE test-side
      cell — a feature anchored to the test period's first value, say — placed
      in a second the default stride never samples. Three verdicts, pinned:

      against the test side, in one rebuild instead of stride passes.

      boundary every finding here is also an availability violation; this
      probe reaches it in one rebuild regardless of stride." No claim that it
      detects what L3.1 cannot; a claim about cost and sampling.

Selection floors to seconds, so a test_from inside a second names a mixed second. after = test_from − 1 s perturbs a training second, and a training row that reads the previous second is legitimate — that is a false finding waiting.

DECISION 3:
  A test_from inside a second EXCLUDES that second from both sides: its cells
  are not perturbed and its rows are not compared. The output prints the
  exclusion with counts ("boundary second 09:03:20 excluded: N cells, M rows").
  A test_from exactly on a second boundary excludes nothing. If the exclusion
  empties a side, could_not_run(alignment) as now. Known positive: a
  mid-second boundary with a legitimate previous-second read on the training
  side reports observed_silence, not a finding.

README's first screen shows the command. What it does not show is what the tool checks and what it does not, and every stranger asks that before typing.

  (a) A section "What it checks, and what it does not", one entry per probe
      from verdicts.PROBES: what the probe perturbs, what a finding means in
      one sentence, what its silence covers, and its residual sentence (the
      reach's k, the stride, the boundary second, the site it cannot name).
      Then the §8.2 states in one line each: none, unsupported,
      could_not_run, and that none of them ever displays as a pass.
  (b) It is kept true by the tree, not by memory: a test asserts every probe
      in verdicts.PROBES has an entry, every entry names a probe that
      exists, and every residual sentence in the section is byte-identical
      to the one the probe prints — the count-in-prose lesson applied to
      prose about probes.
  (c) A last paragraph, plain: the registered claim is the availability
      probe; everything else is Phase 2, never quoted as a §6.2 result. That
      sentence has stood on every halt list since R201 and belongs where a
      reader meets the tool.

4. BUILD ORDER AND ROUND BOUNDARY

  1. §1(a)(e), §2 — small; guard once if a path-set file changed.
  2. §3 — the section and its test.
  3. §0 when the scope exists: push, read, record.
  4. Closing sequence.

5. HALT LIST — round-specific

An exit-class test that allows rather than asserts · a verdict word outside the headline without its probe · a README entry whose residual sentence differs from the probe's own · the suite record committed · CI claimed before the run is read · a second guard run inside the round · any Phase 2 result quoted as a §6.2 or L1.2 result · a section number of mine acted on without resolving it on disk.

6. REPORT FORMAT

First line: remote at head, yes or no, with both hashes. Then §1(a)'s assertion and population, §1(e) as landed. Then §2's red and green. Then §3's section, quoted, and its test's population. Then the guard if run. Then the close table. Then "what you must rule on."

Seven commits wait on one command. The five items are ruled below. Then the round this project has been building toward since Phase 2 opened: the tool audits its author's own pipeline through the front door, as a stranger would, and the front door's verdicts are compared with the harness's.

0. THEO'S ACT — seven commits, six rounds

Theo, once, on vengeance:   gh auth refresh -h github.com -s workflow

Nothing else can move those commits: the rejection is about the commits, not the branch, and history is not rewritten here.

1. THE FIVE, RULED

DECISION 1:
  (a) [run]: ratified. The lines that are legitimately over all probes — exit
      class, coverage header, COMPLETE, INCOMPLETE AND SILENT, ACCEPTED,
      INTERFERED, the PROBES block — carry a visible tag and are enumerated in
      RUN_VOICED, so a tenth is a decision, not a drift. Better than pushing
      them onto a probe they are not about.
  (b) [checks]: ratified, same reason; the four no-model checks are a voice of
      their own.
  (c) The word list: add "silent" (whole word). It costs nothing where the
      line is tagged and catches an untagged one. The three states stay out
      for the reason you gave — their place is beneath the headline.
  (d) The reach residual over the stride residual, at the price of a guard
      run: right. The sentence lives with the thing it describes; that is
      what the guard is for.
  (e) Two commits, one disclosure: right — chain mechanics, not a deviation.
      The order that avoids it — every working file the round needs written
      before the baseline step — goes into the step set's text, not into
      memory.

2. THE AUTHOR'S PIPELINE, THROUGH THE FRONT DOOR

Every probe has been run on the Phase 1 fixture through the harness. None has been run on it the way a user runs the tool: from a wheel, leakaudit run, a model file, the report on stdout, the exit code read. The fixture is the author's CME pipeline — the contaminated build and the corrected one. This is the run the tool exists for, and it is also a consistency check the project has never made: do the front door and the harness agree?

DECISION 2:
  (a) The model file. Start from the guard's fixture model (it declares UTC and
      the frames). Add what the front door can now take and the harness never
      declared:
        - raw_label + label_availability: the paper's label is a forward
          return with a stated horizon; read the horizon and the label's
          source column from the declaration or the harness, cited. If it is
          nowhere on disk, that is the one line Theo supplies, and the round
          stops at (b) until it arrives.
        - input_split.test_from: the paper's train/test boundary, from the
          declaration or the harness, cited; same rule if absent.
        - key_timezones if any frame's key is naive; the alignment table
          says which.
      Nothing inferred. Every value cites where it came from.
  (b) The runs, from a wheel built by the tool, captured with capture_run:
        contaminated: `leakaudit run` at the shipped default; then --confirm.
        corrected:    the same two.
      Each report quoted in full in the round's record; exit codes read.
  (c) THE CONSISTENCY CHECK. For L3.1, the front door's verdict, eligible
      count, record count and feature count on each side against the guard's
      eight terms — same stride (997, declared), same model. They must agree
      or the disagreement is the round's finding, reported with no fix.
      For L2a and the split probe there is no harness figure; their verdicts
      are new results, recorded as Phase 2, each with its probe's residual
      sentence beside it.
  (d) What the corrected side says is the interesting number. Its L3.1
      silence is expected (the guard has it). L2a and split-dependence on the
      corrected build have never been run: a finding there is a real finding
      about the author's own corrected pipeline, and it is reported exactly
      as it comes — the tool does not know whose pipeline it is. A silence
      there carries its coverage numbers and nothing more.
  (e) --confirm's classes on the contaminated side: how many of its findings
      survive isolation, at the default cap, with the cap's cost printed.
  (f) The record: one file under evidence/ for the run, with the model file,
      the four reports, the exit codes, the consistency table, and the
      sentence that all of it is Phase 2 and none of it touches a §6.2 figure.

Halt: if (a) needs a value that is on disk nowhere, report which and stop; a guessed horizon or boundary is exactly what this tool refuses.

3. BUILD ORDER AND ROUND BOUNDARY

  1. §1(c)(e) — small; guard once if a path-set file changed (unlikely).
  2. §2(a) — the model file, every value cited, or the stop.
  3. §2(b)-(f).
  4. §0 when the scope exists: push, read, record.
  5. Closing sequence.

4. HALT LIST — round-specific

A model-file value without its citation · a horizon or boundary guessed · a front-door/harness disagreement fixed rather than reported · a corrected-side finding softened, explained away, or held back · any of §2's results quoted as a §6.2 or L1.2 result · CI claimed before the run is read · a second guard run inside the round · a section number of mine acted on without resolving it on disk.

5. REPORT FORMAT

First line: remote at head, yes or no, with both hashes. Then §2(a)'s model file with citations, or the stop. Then the four reports, quoted. Then §2(c)'s consistency table. Then §2(d)'s corrected-side verdicts with their residuals. Then §2(e). Then the close table. Then "what you must rule on."

R2842026-09-21THE AUDIT, COMPLETED — two new runs, reported as new results

Supersedes R116 through R283 in their entirety. Work from this document only. OPERATING_RULES.md carries the durable set and is in force in full.

The front door and the harness agree term for term — 5,220 records over 29 features on the contaminated build, zero on the corrected, the feature names identical — and that was never checked before. The run also found what dogfooding finds: the label probe cannot take the project's own label, because the declaration's horizon is positional and the schema only holds seconds. That is a real gap and it is built this round. Then the two runs that make the audit of the author's pipeline complete rather than comparable.

0. THEO'S ACT — eight commits

Theo, once, on vengeance:   gh auth refresh -h github.com -s workflow

1. BANKED, AND THE FIVE RULINGS

Banked: every model-file value cited to a line; stride, cap and seed declared so the comparison is between the same runs; the consistency table SAME on all nine terms with the record count reached two ways; the corrected side's silence carrying 0.1% coverage and exit 4; --confirm at the cap, five of five confirmed with the cost printed first; the label gap refused rather than approximated — entering 5.0 s would have been the substitution the declaration itself names. D-V30A-131.

DECISION 1:
  (a) The label gap: BUILD the positional unit. label_availability gains
      horizon_rows, exclusive with horizon_seconds: a(y) for the label at row
      t is the stamp of the row h positions later on the label frame, plus
      the delay — the declaration's own definition, AVAILABILITY_DECLARATION
      478-489, cited in the code. The reach-in-rows work already models
      positions against gaps; this is the same unit on the label side. Known
      positive: the fixture's label, h=5, at a session boundary where the
      duration reading would be wrong by days — the row-based a(y) is right
      and a seconds-based one is shown wrong, as the declaration says. Then
      L2a runs on the fixture: §2(a).
  (b) could_not_run(alignment) for three causes: one state, three REASONS,
      each its own text and each shown to fire. The state is right; the
      reason is what a reader needs, and this run's reason was "one side is
      empty", which it printed.
  (c) LEAKAUDIT_F2_DIR read at import time: FIX. "A repair resolving the work
      root at import time" has been on this project's halt list since R216;
      this is the same defect one module over. Read at call time; test: set
      after import, honoured. The four dead runs are the population.
  (d) Captures into evidence: yes, a sanctioned path — capture_run gains
      --keep <evidence path> (or a sibling tool), copying the three files in,
      verifying the sha256 the record carries, and adding the manifest lines.
      The 1.3 MB of this round's captures go in through it, so the record's
      hashes point at files that exist.
  (e) snap unprobed: right for the consistency run — declaring it would have
      changed what was compared. For the AUDIT it is the gap that matters:
      the label's base column sits in a frame the probe never touched. §2(b).

2. THE AUDIT, COMPLETED — two new runs, reported as new results

The consistency run held the model fixed to the harness's. These two do not, and they are never compared to the harness; they are the tool's own results on the author's pipeline, Phase 2, with their residuals.

DECISION 2:
  (a) With the label declared (horizon_rows from §1(a), base mid(t) from
      snap.mid_price, delay 0 as the declaration states): both sides, default
      stride, --confirm. L2a's verdict on the contaminated build and on the
      corrected build, each with its cells-per-cohort counts and, for any
      finding, the cell-and-row record. The corrected side's L2a verdict is
      new information about the author's corrected pipeline; report it as it
      comes.
  (b) With snap declared as an aggregate frame (its mode from the alignment
      table and the declaration, cited): both sides, default stride. L3.1's
      verdict over snap's 24 columns is new — the harness never probed them.
      Any finding on the corrected side is a finding; a silence carries its
      coverage.
  (c) The split probe stays could_not_run on this fixture and the record says
      why: the fixture is one month and the declared boundary is in August.
      Running it needs a fixture spanning the boundary — recorded as what it
      would take, not done this round.
  (d) The corrected side, --complete, overnight: 61 passes, ~3.3 h, its own
      step after the commit, records kept, prediction printed first. Zero
      findings over every eligible cohort is the strongest sentence this
      tool can say about that pipeline, and it has never been said; a
      finding is confirmed in isolation and reported as it comes.
  (e) One record file, beside R283's: the models with citations, every
      report quoted, exit codes, the residual sentences, and the line that
      none of it is a §6.2 figure.

3. BUILD ORDER AND ROUND BOUNDARY

  1. §1(a)(b)(c)(d) — one batch; guard once if a path-set file changed (label and split probes are off-path by trace; the F2_DIR read may not be).
  2. §2(a)(b) — the four runs, captured and kept.
  3. §2(c)(e) records.
  4. §2(d) — after the commit, its own step; its figure into the record when it lands, even if that is next round.
  5. §0 when the scope exists: push, read, record.
  6. Closing sequence.

4. HALT LIST — round-specific

A seconds horizon entered where the declaration says rows · a corrected-side finding softened or held back · §2's runs compared to the harness · the complete run started without its prediction printed · a capture recorded by hash without the file kept · CI claimed before the run is read · a second guard run inside the round · any of §2's results quoted as a §6.2 or L1.2 result · a section number of mine acted on without resolving it on disk.

5. REPORT FORMAT

First line: remote at head, yes or no, with both hashes. Then §1(a)'s positive — the boundary case where seconds are wrong by days and rows are right. Then §2(a)'s four L2a verdicts and §2(b)'s two L3.1-over-snap verdicts, each quoted with its residual. Then §1(c)'s test, §1(d)'s kept files. Then the guard if run. Then §2(d)'s status. Then the close table. Then "what you must rule on."
